context.description: SGLang is a high-performance serving framework for large language models and multimodal models.

latestRelease.title: v0.5.17
latestRelease.notes:
# Highlights

*582 PRs from 194 contributors.*

**Kimi K3 day-0 support**: A 2.8T-parameter multimodal LatentMoE (896 experts, top-16, routed in a 3584-dim latent space) with a 1M-token context, 69 KDA linear-attention layers interleaved with 24 MLA layers, and a MoonViT3d vision tower, shipping as a native MXFP4 checkpoint. SGLang serves it from day 0 with DCP, DSpark speculative decoding, chunked-prefill PP with TP decode, KDA-aware prefix caching, HiCache L2 over DCP, LoRA on the quantized weights, and reasoning, tool-call and OpenAI-compatible serving, verified on NVIDIA GB300 and AMD MI35x ([#32541](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/32541), [#32828](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/32828), [#32890](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/32890), [#33025](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/33025), [#33112](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/33112), [blog](https://www.lmsys.org/blog/2026-07-27-kimi-k3-day0-support), [cookbook](https://docs.sglang.io/cookbook/autoregressive/Moonshotai/Kimi-K3), [roadmap](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/32607)).

**MiniMax-H3 day-0 support**: MiniMax's video generation model that produces a video and a synchronized stereo audio track in one request, served natively on SGLang-Diffusion across all three public task profiles: text-to-video-and-audio (`t2va`), first/last-frame conditioning (`fl2va`), and image/video/audio reference conditioning (`ref2va`, which also covers video-to-video). Verified on B200 (TP2 + Ulysses4), H100 (TP2 + Ulysses2), AMD MI300X and MI355X (Ulysses1/2/4/8), and 2x RTX 5090 with layerwise offload ([#33275](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/33275), [cookbook](https://docs.sglang.io/cookbook/diffusion/MiniMax/MiniMax-H3)).

**Other new models added**: [EmbeddingGemma](https://docs.sglang.io/cookbook/autoregressive/Google/EmbeddingGemma) and [LFM2.5](https://docs.sglang.io/cookbook/autoregressive/LiquidAI/LFM2.5) embedding models, nvidia/MiniMax-M3-NVFP4, plus cookbook recipes for Poolside's [Laguna-S-2.1](https://docs.sglang.io/cookbook/autoregressive/Poolside/Laguna-S-2.1) family and [Inkling-Small](https://docs.sglang.io/cookbook/autoregressive/ThinkingMachines/Inkling-Small).

**Initial support for the Rust frontend**: Migrates the front half of the server, everything from network ingress up to the point a tokenized request is handed to the GPU scheduler, from Python to a multi-threaded Rust implementation ([#29799](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/29799)).

**DCP communication backends and q-replicate (Helix)**: The DeepSeek-MLA decode context-parallel path gains pluggable comm backends. `a2a` exchanges packed attention output plus fp32 LSE in a single NCCL collective per layer, with fp8 KV carried as uint8 byte transport; `fi_a2a` delegates the cross-rank exchange to the FlashInfer MNNVL kernel on GB200. `--dcp-replicate-q-proj` projects full-head Q locally and skips the per-layer Q head-dim all-gather. Select with `--dcp-comm-backend {ag_rs, a2a, fi_a2a}` ([#21637](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/21637)).

**DWDP for MoE prefill**: A new prefill parallelism strategy that prefetches peer expert weights over NVLink P2P and computes all experts locally, removing EP all-to-all token dispatch. On 4x B200 with gpt-oss-120b, prefill-only, DWDP4 reaches **1.92x over DEP4** at MNT 32K / ISL 32K, and **506K vs 329K tok/s (1.54x)** at saturation (CONC=128, ISL=8K). Enable with `--dwdp-size`; the authors mark it early-development ([#29778](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/29778)).

**Session-reference-aware Unified Radix Cache**: For agentic and RL-rollout workloads, requests can carry a stable `session_id` so eviction knows which prefixes an active session still references, instead of evicting purely by cache policy. Release the references with `/close_session`. Opt in with `--enable-session-radix-cache` ([#29173](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/29173)).

**SM90 FP8 MegaMoE for DeepSeek-V4**: Adds the DeepGEMM MegaMoE A2A path on SM90 for DeepSeek-V4-Flash/Pro FP8, including the pre-dispatch JIT kernel and FP8 expert weight preparation. Guarded behind `SGLANG_OPT_USE_DEEPGEMM_MEGA_MOE=1` ([#29016](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/29016)).

**Faster large-MoE model loading**: Oversized or non-contiguous CPU weight views were driving pathological H2D transfers, with DeepSeek-V4-Pro TP8 spending 27 to 32 minutes in H2D on some ranks. Copying those views into contiguous storage before H2D cuts full model loading from about **35 minutes to 6m20s (5.6x)**, and GPT-OSS-20B BF16 from **545s to 70s (7.8x)**, with Qwen3.5-397B measured at 1.93x to 2.3x. Opt in with `SGLANG_MOE_COPY_WEIGHT_VIEWS_BEFORE_H2D`, off by default ([#32315](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/32315)).

**Lower DeepSeek-V4 memory on AMD**: Removing unnecessary expert padding drops MI355X FP4 MoE model weights from **159.07 GB to 112.36 GB**, and bringing the HIP compress-state pool into the memory_saver KV_CACHE region lets colocated RL reclaim it, cutting the measured training-phase footprint from about **143 GiB to 87 GiB per GPU** ([#31450](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/31450), [#31747](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/31747)).

**Faster engine recovery**: Large-model restarts cost 3 to 6+ minutes today, about 6.5 minutes for Qwen3-235B FP8 on 4 GPUs, because weights reload from storage and CUDA graphs recapture. A weight-cache daemon holds weights per GPU so a restarting engine can recover from cache instead ([#27139](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/27139)).

**Lower host overhead in hybrid-linear MTP decode**: Under spec-v2 overlap scheduling each decode step runs draft, verify and extend CUDA graphs, and the eager seams between them become GPU idle time at low concurrency. This trims that host work so the host stays off the critical path ([#32219](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/32219)).

**Dependencies**: flashinfer 0.6.15.post1 ([#31927](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/31927)), sgl-deep-gemm 0.1.5.post1 ([#32345](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/32345), [#33143](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/33143)), helion 1.4 ([#32562](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/32562)), mooncake 0.3.12.post1 ([#32302](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/32302)), dynamo-tokenizers 1.7.0 ([#32981](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/32981)). PyTorch stays at 2.11.0 and the CUDA base image at 13.0.1.

*Full release notes by category below; breaking changes and known issues are at the end.*

## Breaking Changes & Upgrade Notes

* **`helion` jumps 0.2.6 to 1.4**, a major-version move for anyone depending on helion-backed kernels: [#32562](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/32562)
* **`sglang.jit_kernel` is retired into `sglang.kernels`**, completing RFC [#29630](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/29630). Imports from the old module path must move: [#32072](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/32072), [#31666](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/31666), [#32015](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/32015), [#32045](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/32045)
* **Breakable prefill CUDA graph is now on by default for DP attention**: [#31682](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/31682)
* **CuteDSL BF16 GEMM on SM100 is on by default** when the heuristic allows it: [#30567](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/30567)
* **sgl-kernel AOT `bmm_fp8` is deleted in favor of `flashinfer.bmm_fp8`; the AOT router GEMM and fused A GEMM are also removed**: [#31202](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/31202), [#30280](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/30280)
* **The FP8 per-tensor GEMM backend on SM120 switches to cuBLAS**: [#31961](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/31961)
* **Unfetchable or unparseable multimodal inputs now return HTTP 400 instead of 500**, and text-only models reject media input outright: [#31417](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/31417), [#32914](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/32914)
* **Diffusion request-level quality is restricted to two validated tiers**, lossless (default) and high: [#33453](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/33453)
* **`ServerArgs` is being made read-only** behind namespace config bags. Code that mutated `ServerArgs` at runtime must route through the new accessors: [#31809](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/31809), [#31811](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/31811), [#33334](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/33334), [#33338](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/33338)

signals.title: [Roadmap] sglang auto tuner
signals.text: Now we have many kernel backends for moe (e.g., triton, cutlass), attention, and allreduce. For each kernel, we can also tune some configs (e.g., the tile sizes in triton fused moe). Tuning these kernels and choosing dispatching heuristics can be non-trivial. We would like to build a simple command that auto-tune all the kernels and dispatch heuristic for a model. ## Todo 1. Implement a script sglang.auto_tune to tune the kernels and hyperparameters for a specific model. It should dump the optimal tile sizes/dispatching heuristics for all kernels used in this model. Example usage: - `python3 -m sglang.auto_tune --model-path Qwen/Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507 --tp 8` - `python3 -m sglang.auto_tune --model-path Qwen/Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507 --tp 4` 2. Start from tuning the triton fused moe https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/tree/main/benchmark/kernels/fused_moe_triton 3. Implement a github action workflow that tunes 20 popular models on 5 common platforms. - The workflow should take in two arguments: a list of model names, and a list of runner names - Our CI has H100, H20, H200, B200, GB200 4. Auto choose allreduce algorithms (custom allreduce, nccl, nccl symmetric memory, torch symmetric memory). 5. Auto choose attention kernel backend and moe runner backend. 6. Auto tune the cutlass gemm kernels (with cutlass profiler) 7. Auto choose speculative decoding parameters for different batch sizes.

signals.title: [Feature] Improve Unit Test Coverage
signals.text: ## Motivation SGLang's test suite has **600+ test files**, but most are E2E tests that launch a full server. While these cover many code paths, core modules like `managers/`, `mem_cache/`, `entrypoints/`, `sampling/`, `parser/`, `function_call/`, and `utils/` still need better unit test coverage (tests that run without launching a server). **Why this matters:** - E2E tests launch a server and load model weights, taking minutes. Unit tests run in seconds with mocked dependencies. - When an E2E test fails, the root cause could be anywhere. Unit tests pinpoint the exact broken function. ## What's Already Done - **Unit test directory** [`test/registered/unit/`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/tree/main/test/registered/unit) with READMEs ([`test/registered/README.md`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/test/registered/README.md), [`test/registered/unit/README.md`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/test/registered/unit/README.md)) documenting conventions - **32 unit tests migrated** across 12 subdirectories - **Coverage tooling** configured ([`.coveragerc`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.coveragerc), `pytest-cov`) - **CI coverage reporting** in [`ci-coverage-overview.yml`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/workflows/ci-coverage-overview.yml) (daily + manual trigger) — [example run](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/24032286387/attempts/1#summary-70083527423) - **Contribution guide** updated with [unit test section](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/docs/developer_guide/contribution_guide.md#run-and-add-unit-tests) ## Directory Structure ``` test/registered/unit/ # mirrors python/sglang/srt/ ├── mem_cache/ (6 files) ├── function_call/ (5 files) ├── utils/ (4 files) ├── parser/ (3 files) ├── managers/ (3 files) ├── entrypoints/ (2 files) ├── layers/ (2 files) ├── observability/ (2 files) ├── model_loader/ (2 files) ├── server_args/ (1 file) ├── model_executor/ (1 file) ├── batch_invariant_ops/ (1 file) └── ... (new subdirs added as tests are written) ``` **Principle:** Source file at `srt/mem_cache/radix_cache.py` → test at `unit/mem_cache/test_radix_cache.py`. ## Open Tasks Below are some suggested starting points. Comment on this issue to claim one. You can check the latest UT coverage report run ([example](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/24032286387/attempts/1#summary-70083527423)) or run coverage locally to find your own opportunities — modules with low coverage under core directories (`managers/`, `sampling/`, `parser/`, etc.) are good candidates: ```bash pytest test/registered/unit/ --cov --cov-config=.coveragerc --cov-report=term-missing -v ``` ### Easy (good first issue) - `srt/parser/` — conversation templates, reasoning parsers, code completion parser - `srt/sampling/` — parameter validation, normalization, logit processor serialization - `srt/entrypoints/openai/` — encoding/decoding, tool call formatting - `srt/function_call/` — extend existing detector tests, add new detector coverage ### Medium - `srt/utils/` — common util helpers - `srt/multimodal/` — media utils, processor base logic - `srt/constrained/` — grammar dispatch logic - `srt/managers/` — template manager, tokenizer utils, batch metadata helpers ## How to Contribute 1. **Pick a task** from above (or find your own via coverage), comment to claim it 2. **Look at existing examples:** - `test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_evict_policy.py` — pure logic, zero deps - `test/registered/unit/managers/test_prefill_adder.py` — mock factories for scheduler tests - `test/registered/unit/parser/test_reasoning_parser.py` — streaming parser tests 3. **Follow the conventions** in [`test/registered/unit/README.md`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/tree/main/test/registered/unit/README.md) and the [contribution guide](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/docs/developer_guide/contribution_guide.md#run-and-add-unit-tests) 4. **Run locally:** ```bash pytest test/registered/unit/ -v pytest test/registered/unit/ --cov --cov-config=.coveragerc -v # with coverage ``` 5. **Submit a PR** titled `[Test] Add unit tests for <module_name>`, referencing this issue ### PR Quality Bar **Note:** AI-assisted code is acceptable, but you are responsible for the quality — **understand every line you submit.** We will reject PRs that look auto-generated without understanding — e.g., tests that only check trivial cases, assert on mock return values, or don't actually exercise the real code logic. Read the source code first, then write tests that would catch real bugs. ### PR Requirements - [ ] Test is in `test/registered/unit/<module>/` (mirroring `srt/`) - [ ] Does NOT launch a server or load real model weights - [ ] Includes edge cases, not just happy paths - [ ] Use `CustomTestCase` instead of `unittest.TestCase`. - [ ] Registered with `register_cpu_ci()` or `register_cuda_ci()` - [ ] **Locally tested and passing.** Paste both the command and its output in your PR description: ```bash # command pytest test/registered/unit/<your_module>/test_xxx.py -v # output (copy-paste the full result) ```

signals.title: [Roadmap] Context Parallelism  (2026 Q3)
signals.text: ## Current Status There has been some prior efforts on context parallelism: - Refactor and unify parallel states for CP #17213 - Prefill CP for DSA models (Dpsk v32/glm 5) #12065 #13959 - Prefill CP for MHA/GQA model (Qwen3-MoE + FA3 attention backend) #18233 However, the current support only covers a small number of models. To generalize the usage of CP, we need to work on following features and tasks ## Prefill CP - [x] Compatibility with allreduce fusion #21249 - [x] Support attention cp size != moe_dp size #22003 - [x] Prefill CP for MLA models (Dpsk v3/Kimi-K2.5) #23292 @kpham-sgl - [ ] Prefill CP for more MHA/GQA attention backends (flashinfer/trtllm-mha) - [x] Prefill CP for models with SWA (GPT-OSS/Mimo V2.5) #29972 - [ ] Optimize all-to-all communication pattern for CP+EP with hybrid EP @Fridge003 - [x] Support batch size > 1 #23269 - [ ] Support sharded kv cache between CP ranks, can be any of the following: @Shunkangz - [x] Sharding KV cache by layers dim (https://z.ai/blog/scaling-pain) #29421 - [ ] Sharding KV cache by sequence dim (probably with Ring Attention) #30501 - [ ] Sharding KV cache by flattened(page_size x num_heads x hidden_state) dim - [x] Support Breakable Cuda Graph for Prefill CP #33136 - [x] Support Prefill CP + Decode TP in collocated serving #27657 - [ ] Refactor Efforts @Fridge003 #27252 ## Decode CP See separate roadmap: #29736 ## Others - [ ] Add a standalone document for context parallelism feature @Fridge003 @Shunkangz @ShangmingCai @ch-wan @kpham-sgl

signals.title: [RFC] Sglang non-GPU process rust migration
signals.text: ### Checklist - [x] If this is not a feature request but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed. - [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed. **PR** - https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/29799 Refer Roadmap https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/22949 Release Roadmap https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/1Y71GY3DOzZwuAp2ytehW0rJ4uzOx276PMtgTORgD49c/edit?slide=id.g3e59bc0132c_0_0#slide=id.g3e59bc0132c_0_0 ### Motivation **Status**: Draft **Author**: @rainj-me **Created**: Apr 20 2026 **Version**: 0.1 # Rust Server Migration Plan **Status:** Draft · **Last updated:** 2026-06-18 · **Owner:** Rain Jiang Migration of the SGLang request front-half (everything from network ingress up to the point a tokenized request is handed to the GPU scheduler) from Python to a multi-threaded Rust implementation. --- ## 1. Goals & scope **Goal.** Replace the Python tokenizer/detokenizer managers and HTTP server with a single-process, thread-per-core Rust implementation that owns the request lifecycle up to scheduler submission. **In scope:** HTTP(S)/gRPC/WS/h2/h3 server, request FSM, tokenizer & detokenizer managers, multimodal encoder dispatch, control API (abort/flush/weight update etc.), large tensor zero-copy handoff to the scheduler, cross-dp-group dispatch. **Out of scope (this plan):** model kernels, attention backends, KV-cache internals, quantization. The Rust server keeps the existing Python scheduler and GPU worker framework; it does not reimplement them. **Non-goals:** behavioral changes to the public API. The Rust server must be a drop-in for the Python one — same endpoints, same request/response schemas, same streaming semantics — so it can ship behind a flag and be A/B'd against Python. --- ## 2. Architecture summary The design this phase implement (decided separately; recorded here for context): - **Two FSMs, one process.** An **ingress FSM** (per request, multi-threaded, thread-per-core) carrying a request from `Received` through validation and optional encode/tokenize to `Queued`; and an **egress FSM** handling streaming (`Streaming` self-loop → `Finalizing` → `Completed`). They are the two halves of one request's lifecycle, owned by the same core and meeting at the ring-buffer / scheduler boundary — no shared locks. - **Six thread groups:** (1) **api-server** on an async runtime — accepts connections, terminates protocols; (2) **tokenizer-manager** running the ingress/egress request FSMs, CPU-core-bound; (3) **encoder** (core-bound); (4) **tokenizer** (core-bound); (5) **detokenizer** (core-bound); and (6) the python **scheduler** group within main thread. Groups talk only via channels — no shared locks across group boundaries. - **Channels:** bounded **MPSC** TokenizerManager→Scheduler (`try_send` = backpressure), per-core **SPSC** returns; userspace rings carry the payload, no ZMQ involved. Crossing the Rust→Python boundary, request objects are serialized with **msgpack** so only immutable bytes transfer — keeping the GIL out of the hot path. Tensor data bypasses msgpack entirely and is shared through **pinned memory**, handed across as a handle rather than copied or serialized. - **Zero-copy:** for encoded multimodal data, Python pre-allocates the pinned buffer pool at startup and Rust writes into slots by index during the encode/tokenize phase. Channels move slot handles (plus small msgpack metadata), never tensor bytes; lifetime is the pool's slot-reuse policy — a slot returns to the free list only after both Python's read and any GPU DMA complete, not Rust's `Drop`. - **Cross-rank:** For DP attention, the first rank of each DP group runs the Rust server *without* the api-server; a single api-server then fans **control** messages to every DP group (duplicated, since control must reach all), while **generation** requests are **round-robined** across DP groups for load balancing. - **Streaming:** a single `Streaming` macro state self-loops per chunk; non-streaming is just a stream whose frames are accumulated and emitted in `Finalizing`. See the request-FSM and topology diagrams in the Appendix for detail. --- ## 3. Phase 1 — Rust server (tok/detok manager + HTTP server) **Target: 2026-07-17** Phase 1 delivers the Rust front-half running in front of the **existing Python scheduler + GPU worker**, inside one process via multi-threaded Rust ⇄ Python. ### 3.1 Work breakdown | | Item | Status | Depends on | Notes | | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | | 1 | Rust frontend \+ scheduler PoC | ✅ Done | — | PR [\#23360](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/23360) \[Closed\] | | 2 | Architecture design | ✅ Done | — | Pending final approval | | 3 | Pickle → msgpack migration | ✅ Done | — | PR [\#28688](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/28688) \[Merged\] Followup issue [\#29465](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/29465) | | 4 | Single-process framework: multi-threaded Rust \+ Python scheduler/GPU worker | ✅ Done | 3 | | | 5 | Tokenizer & detokenizer manager | ✅ Done | 4 | | | 6 | HTTP server: /generate \+ streaming | ✅ Done | 4, 5 | | | 7 | Encoder support | 🟡 WIP | 4, 5 | Work with dynamo team check whether this can export to dynamo crate. | | 8 | PD disaggregation | ✅Done | 4 | Large. Prefill/decode split — see risk note. | | 9 | DP attention \+ cross-node DP controller | ✅ Done | 4 | Large, cross-node. See risk note. | | 10 | Metrics / logging | 🟡 WIP | 4 | Logging Done, Metrics WIP | | 11 | Port existing HTTP APIs other than the listed APIs below | ⏳ Pending | 6 | Full endpoint parity for drop-in replacement. | | 12 | Unified multi-protocol lib (server \+ gateway) | ⏳ Pending | 6 | Shared http(s)/h2/h3/gRPC/WS layer reused by sglang-gateway. | | 13 | Code Refactor | 🟡 WIP | | | | 14 | AuthZ support | | | | | 15 | Parallel Sampling | | | | | 16 | Benchmark\_serving perf optimization | 🟡 WIP | | | | 17 | Embedding request | | | | | 18 | offline Engine API support | | | | | 19 | Other flags in the TokenizedGenerateReqInput | | | | | 20 | cache\_tokens | | | | | 21 | custom\_logit\_processor | | | | | 22 | preferred\_sampling\_params | | | | | 23 | Standalone API-Server for DP Attn | 🟡 WIP | | | | 24 | Anthorpic API support | | | | | 25 | SageMaker API support | | | | | 26 | Vertex AI API support | | | | | 27 | Ollama compatible API support | | | | | 28 | Weight update APIs | | | | | 29 | HiCache APIs | | | | ### 3.2 Sequencing & critical path Items are **not** independent. The dependency spine is: ``` #3 pickle→msgpack ──► #4 single-process framework ──► #5 tok/detok ──► #6 /generate+stream ──► #11 API parity └─► #10 metrics (parallel) └─► #7 encoder (parallel, after #5) ``` **Critical path to a usable July 17 milestone:** 3 → 4 → 5 → 6, with 10 landing in parallel and 11 close behind. That subset is what makes the Rust server a working, A/B-testable drop-in for text LLM traffic. **Recommend deferring out of the July 17 milestone** (track as Phase 1.5 / stretch): items **8 (PD disaggregation)** and **9 (DP attention + cross-node DP controller)**. Both are large, both can land after the core path is proven, and bundling them into the July date puts the whole milestone at risk. Item **12 (unified protocol lib)** is valuable but is a refactor that can follow once #6 stabilizes the protocol surface. > **Date reality check.** July 17 is ~4 weeks out and #4 (the foundation) is still > pending-start. The 3→4→5→6+7 path is achievable in that window if #4 starts > immediately and 8/9/12 are explicitly descoped. Carrying all 12 to July 17 is not > realistic; pick the milestone definition deliberately. ### 3.3 Phase 1 exit criteria - Rust server handles `/generate` (streaming + non-streaming) at parity with Python. - Tok/detok managers run in-process; detok is incremental and order-correct. - Encoder path works for at least one multimodal input type. - Metrics + logs at parity; runs behind a flag, A/B-able against Python. - Endpoint parity sufficient to route production text traffic. --- ## 4. Cross-cutting concerns **Rollout / fallback.** Every phase ships behind a flag with the Python path as the live fallback. Migrate by traffic slice (shadow → small % → ramp), not big-bang. keep the Python path runnable as the live fallback until the Rust path reaches parity. **Testing.** Differential testing against Python (same inputs → same tokens/frames) is the primary correctness gate. Add: FSM property tests (every state has a terminal exit; post-terminal events are no-ops/idempotent); streaming order + UTF-8-boundary tests for detok. **Observability.** Metrics/logging (P1 #10) should land *with* the core path, not after — debugging the channel/FSM/threading layers without it is painful. Per-state request counts, queue depths (ring-buffer occupancy = backpressure signal), per-core load, and control-op latencies. **Kernel / environment.** io_uring features used (`MSG_RING` 5.18+, `SEND_ZC` 6.0+, `DEFER_TASKRUN` 6.1+) set a minimum kernel; some hardened/container environments disable io_uring — keep an epoll+eventfd fallback behind the same loop abstraction. --- ## 5. Top risks | Risk | Impact | Mitigation | | ------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | July 17 scope (all 12 items) | Milestone slips / quality suffers | Descope 8/9/12; define milestone as 3→4→5→6+10. | | #4 framework is the foundation and hasn't started | Blocks 5–7; whole phase waits | Start immediately; treat as the single highest-priority item. | | Rust↔Python boundary in the single-process step | Perf cliffs, GIL contention | Keep the boundary narrow (handles, not data); measure early. | | Detok ordering / UTF-8 under streaming | Corrupt user-visible output | Shard by `hash(req_id)`; stateful decode offsets; boundary tests. | | Slow-client backpressure on egress | GPU stalls / memory growth | Bounded egress buffers; treat persistent slow consumer as disconnect. | --- ## 6. Milestones | Date | Milestone | | ---------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | ~Now | #1 PR #23360, #3 merged (PR #28688); #4 started. | | 2026-07-17 | **Phase 1 core:** Rust server with `/generate` + streaming + encoder + metrics, A/B-able vs Python (items 3–7, 10, 11). | | Phase 1.5 | PD disaggregation (#8), DP attention + cross-node controller (#9), unified protocol lib (#12). | ## 7. Appendix 1. [Initial plan](https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/1Y71GY3DOzZwuAp2ytehW0rJ4uzOx276PMtgTORgD49c/edit?slide=id.g3e59bc0132c_0_0#slide=id.g3e59bc0132c_0_0) 2. signals.title: [Bug] flashinfer_trtllm MoE runner corrupts MiniMax-M2.7-NVFP4 output and asserts on DeepSeek-V4-Flash on B200
signals.text:
### Checklist - [x] I searched related issues but found no solution (see Related issues section below for adjacent reports). - [x] Reproduces on SGLang `v0.5.12` and `v0.5.12.post1` (current stable release at draft time); `dev` / `nightly-dev` not tested. - [x] Environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are included below. - [x] This is a bug report, not a general question. - [x] Posted in English. ### Summary On 8x NVIDIA B200 (SM100), the `flashinfer_trtllm` MoE runner shows two failure modes across the two MoE checkpoints I tested in SGLang `v0.5.12` and `v0.5.12.post1`: 1. **`nvidia/MiniMax-M2.7-NVFP4`**: the server starts successfully and returns HTTP 200, but generation is deterministic replacement-character-heavy corrupted text at `temperature=0`. This reproduces across the localization sweep below: FP4 GEMM backend, prompt shape, max_tokens, SGLang version, and both TP=8 and TP=1. 2. **`deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash`**: the server crashes at first forward pass with an `AssertionError` at `flashinfer_trtllm.py:686`. For comparison, the launch command shown on the NVIDIA model card for `nvidia/MiniMax-M2.7-NVFP4` uses `--moe-runner-backend flashinfer_cutlass`. On the same hardware, image, weights, and probes, that path produces clean expected output for M2.7-NVFP4, including `"What is 2+2?"` → `"4"` and 0% non-ASCII ratio across all four probes. The M2.7 failure narrows to the `flashinfer_trtllm` MoE runner path; I did not capture a server-side trace pinpointing the specific fused function reached on M2.7. The V4-Flash crash reaches the FP8 fused-experts path at `flashinfer_trtllm.py:686` (`fused_experts_none_to_flashinfer_trtllm_fp8`) per the stack trace below. **Maintainer note:** - **Scope:** I filed this as one issue because both failures occur through the `flashinfer_trtllm` MoE runner module. I have not verified that they share a root cause. I can split into separate issues if triage prefers. - **Terminology:** `flashinfer_trtllm` here refers to FlashInfer's TRT-LLM-derived MoE kernel path used through SGLang dispatch, not standalone TensorRT-LLM. ### Environment | Field | Value | | --- | --- | | Hardware | 8x NVIDIA B200 SXM (SM100) | | Driver | 580.126.09 | | CUDA in container | 13.0.1 (NVCC 13.0.88) | | Image | `lmsysorg/sglang:v0.5.12.post1` | | Image digest | `sha256:b9079f568489b6620b580c2658e68e24791f02a212c4de23b8b5d42661de4b11` | | Image label | `ai.sglang.image.tag=lmsysorg/sglang:v0.5.12.post1` | | SGLang commit | `5a15cde858ea09b77116212a39356f2fc51b8584` (per image labels) | | SGLang version (in-container) | `0.5.12.post1` | | FlashInfer | `0.6.11.post1` | | PyTorch | `2.11.0+cu130` (wheel built against CUDA 13.0; runs on container CUDA 13.0.1) | | Triton | `3.6.0` | | ModelOpt | `0.44.0` | | Transformers | `5.6.0` | | Python | `3.12` | | HF revision: `nvidia/MiniMax-M2.7-NVFP4` | `e79701cb1f9dce8fe5395b9ed2b20170beebecde` (uploaded 2026-04-24) | | HF revision: `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash` | `6976c7ff1b30a1b2cb7805021b8ba4684041f136` (uploaded 2026-05-06) | Also confirmed with base `lmsysorg/sglang:v0.5.12` (the original V4 day-0 build before the `.post1` patch). Both versions exhibit the same failure mode (output reproduces under the base tag; see Cross-version evidence table below for the caveat that I captured `pip freeze` only inside the `.post1` container). This is not a `.post1`-only regression. > Note for maintainers: per FlashInfer release notes, DeepSeek-V4 sparse MLA TRTLLM-GEN kernels (PR flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#3269) landed in FlashInfer `v0.6.12rc1` (2026-05-22), which post-dates the FlashInfer `0.6.11.post1` shipped inside `lmsysorg/sglang:v0.5.12.post1`. This may be relevant to Failure Mode 2 (V4-Flash assertion). I have not yet tested with FlashInfer `0.6.12+` and can do so on request.
python3 -m sglang.check_env output (captured inside lmsysorg/sglang:v0.5.12.post1 on the test node) ``` ========== == CUDA == ========== CUDA Version 13.0.1 Python: 3.12.3 (main, Mar 23 2026, 19:04:32) [GCC 13.3.0] CUDA available: True GPU 0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7: NVIDIA B200 GPU 0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7 Compute Capability: 10.0 CUDA_HOME: /usr/local/cuda NVCC: Cuda compilation tools, release 13.0, V13.0.88 CUDA Driver Version: 580.126.09 PyTorch: 2.11.0+cu130 sglang: 0.5.12.post1 sglang-kernel: 0.4.2.post2 flashinfer_python: 0.6.11.post1 flashinfer_cubin: 0.6.11.post1 flashinfer_jit_cache: 0.6.11.post1+cu130 triton: 3.6.0 transformers: 5.6.0 torchao: 0.17.0+cu130 numpy: 2.3.5 aiohttp: 3.13.5 fastapi: 0.136.1 huggingface_hub: 1.16.1 interegular: 0.3.3 modelscope: 1.37.1 orjson: 3.11.9 outlines: 0.1.11 packaging: 26.2 psutil: 7.2.2 pydantic: 2.13.4 python-multipart: 0.0.29 pyzmq: 27.1.0 uvicorn: 0.47.0 uvloop: 0.22.1 vllm: Module Not Found xgrammar: 0.2.0 openai: 2.6.1 tiktoken: 0.13.0 anthropic: 0.104.1 litellm: Module Not Found torchcodec: 0.11.1+cu130 NVIDIA Topology: GPU0 GPU1 GPU2 GPU3 GPU4 GPU5 GPU6 GPU7 CPU Affinity NUMA Affinity GPU NUMA ID GPU0 X NV18 NV18 NV18 NV18 NV18 NV18 NV18 0-79 0 N/A GPU1 NV18 X NV18 NV18 NV18 NV18 NV18 NV18 0-79 0 N/A GPU2 NV18 NV18 X NV18 NV18 NV18 NV18 NV18 0-79 0 N/A GPU3 NV18 NV18 NV18 X NV18 NV18 NV18 NV18 0-79 0 N/A GPU4 NV18 NV18 NV18 NV18 X NV18 NV18 NV18 80-159 1 N/A GPU5 NV18 NV18 NV18 NV18 NV18 X NV18 NV18 80-159 1 N/A GPU6 NV18 NV18 NV18 NV18 NV18 NV18 X NV18 80-159 1 N/A GPU7 NV18 NV18 NV18 NV18 NV18 NV18 NV18 X 80-159 1 N/A Hypervisor vendor:: KVM ulimit soft: 1024 ```
### Failure Mode 1: M2.7-NVFP4 produces deterministic mojibake **Reproduction.** Launch: ```bash docker run --rm --gpus all --ipc=host --network=host --shm-size=32g \ --ulimit nofile=1048576:1048576 --ulimit memlock=-1 --ulimit stack=67108864 \ -v /path/to/m27-nvfp4:/models/m27-nvfp4:ro \ -e HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 \ lmsysorg/sglang:v0.5.12.post1 \ python3 -m sglang.launch_server \ --model /models/m27-nvfp4 \ --served-model-name nvidia/MiniMax-M2.7-NVFP4 \ --tensor-parallel-size 8 \ --quantization modelopt_fp4 \ --trust-remote-code \ --reasoning-parser minimax-append-think \ --tool-call-parser minimax-m2 \ --moe-runner-backend flashinfer_trtllm \ --fp4-gemm-backend cutlass \ --attention-backend flashinfer \ --host 127.0.0.1 --port 30000 ``` Probe (temperature=0): ```bash curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:30000/v1/chat/completions \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"model":"nvidia/MiniMax-M2.7-NVFP4","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"What is 2+2? Reply with the number only."}],"temperature":0,"max_tokens":64}' \ | python3 -c 'import json,sys; print(repr(json.load(sys.stdin)["choices"][0]["message"]["content"]))' ``` **Expected**: clean answer content. With the `flashinfer_cutlass` MoE path, this probe returns `'... 4'`. **Observed** with `flashinfer_trtllm` MoE: `'�s000,�s,�s�l�l�s�l�l�s�l�n�s�l�s�l�s�l�i�s�l�i�s�l�i�s�l�i�s�l�'`. The output is deterministic across repeated `temperature=0` invocations and has a high non-ASCII/replacement-character ratio. **Localization sweep.** Failure reproduces under every combination I tested across these five axes: | Axis | Variants tested | All mojibake? | | --- | --- | --- | | FP4 GEMM backend | `auto`, `cutlass`, `flashinfer_cutedsl` | yes | | Prompt content / shape | 4 probes (2+2 short, 2+2 long max_tokens, reasoning, chat-shape long-context) | yes | | Prompt max_tokens | 64, 256, 512 | yes | | SGLang version | `v0.5.12`, `v0.5.12.post1` (byte-identical outputs) | yes | | Tensor parallelism | TP=8, TP=1 (single B200) | yes (TP=1 produces denser corruption than TP=8; see following table) | Sample per-probe statistics from the `cutlass` FP4 + `flashinfer_trtllm` MoE configuration at TP=8: | Probe | Probe description | max_tokens | Non-ASCII chars (code points) | Total chars (code points) | Non-ASCII ratio | | --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | | p1 | "What is 2+2?" | 64 | 30 | 71 | 42.25% | | p2 | Same prompt | 256 | 121 | 276 | 43.84% | | p3 | Reasoning ("trains meeting") | 256 | 203 | 279 | 72.76% | | p4 | Chat-shape long-context | 512 | 178 | 791 | 22.50% | Same probes at TP=1 (single B200), same model, same backend flags except `--tensor-parallel-size 1`: | Probe | Non-ASCII ratio (TP=1) | Non-ASCII ratio (TP=8) | | --- | ---: | ---: | | p1 | **88.73%** | 42.25% | | p2 | **96.96%** | 43.84% | | p3 | **96.20%** | 72.76% | | p4 | **75.72%** | 22.50% | TP=1 produces replacement-char-heavy output more densely than TP=8 across every probe. The failure reproduces on a single rank, so TP-distributed expert dispatch and all-to-all are not required to trigger it. This narrows the M2.7 repro to the single-rank `flashinfer_trtllm` runner/kernel path. **Cross-version evidence.** Identical config (`cutlass` FP4 + `flashinfer_trtllm` MoE), same hardware, same probes, only the SGLang image differs: | Image | Image digest | p1 first 200 chars | p2-p4 | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `lmsysorg/sglang:v0.5.12.post1` | `sha256:b9079f568489b6620b580c2658e68e24791f02a212c4de23b8b5d42661de4b11` | `�s000,�s,�s�l�l�s�l�l�s�l�n�s�l�s�l�s�l�i�s�l�i...` | replacement-char-heavy | | `lmsysorg/sglang:v0.5.12` | `sha256:79d577610f5022e66b5bb618d434b23ab7121fc9f96d5dba3ee046d5eecfd4df` | byte-identical to row above | byte-identical | `v0.5.12.post1` is the post-release patch of the base `v0.5.12` release that introduced day-0 DeepSeek-V4 support. I observe the same output under the base tag; the in-container `pip freeze` was captured only for `.post1`, so I report this as "same output reproduces on base `v0.5.12`" rather than "byte-identical package set." This is not a `.post1`-only regression. **Reference comparison.** "Reference" throughout this draft means the NVIDIA model-card-recommended launch command (`--moe-runner-backend flashinfer_cutlass`); see . Same hardware, same image, same weights, same probes, only swapping `--moe-runner-backend flashinfer_trtllm` (the bug repro) back to `--moe-runner-backend flashinfer_cutlass`: | Probe | Non-ASCII ratio (`flashinfer_cutlass` MoE) | | --- | ---: | | p1 | 0% (cleanly returns "4") | | p2-p4 | 0% (clean prose) | ### Failure Mode 2: V4-Flash crashes at first forward pass Same image, same hardware, weights at `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash`. Launch command: ```bash docker run --rm --gpus all --ipc=host --network=host --shm-size=32g \ --ulimit nofile=1048576:1048576 --ulimit memlock=-1 --ulimit stack=67108864 \ -v /path/to/v4-flash:/models/v4-flash:ro \ -e HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 \ lmsysorg/sglang:v0.5.12.post1 \ python3 -m sglang.launch_server \ --model /models/v4-flash \ --served-model-name deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash \ --tensor-parallel-size 8 \ --trust-remote-code \ --moe-runner-backend flashinfer_trtllm \ --attention-backend flashinfer \ --host 127.0.0.1 --port 30000 ``` This launch differs from Failure Mode 1 only in: model path and served-model-name swapped to V4-Flash; M2.7-specific `--reasoning-parser minimax-append-think`, `--tool-call-parser minimax-m2`, and `--quantization modelopt_fp4 --fp4-gemm-backend cutlass` flags dropped. V4-Flash carries its quantization in the model config. The server crashes during initial forward pass: ``` File "/sgl-workspace/sglang/python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/fused_moe_triton/layer.py", line 1062, in forward return self.forward_impl(hidden_states, topk_output) File "/sgl-workspace/sglang/python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/fused_moe_triton/layer.py", line 1072, in forward_impl combine_input = self.run_moe_core( File "/sgl-workspace/sglang/python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/fp8.py", line 1874, in apply return self.runner.run(dispatch_output, quant_info) File "/sgl-workspace/sglang/python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/moe_runner/runner.py", line 100, in run return self.fused_func(dispatch_output, quant_info, self.config) File "/sgl-workspace/sglang/python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/moe_runner/flashinfer_trtllm.py", line 1116, in fused_experts_none_to_flashinfer_trtllm return fused_experts_none_to_flashinfer_trtllm_fp8( File "/sgl-workspace/sglang/python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/moe_runner/flashinfer_trtllm.py", line 686, in fused_experts_none_to_flashinfer_trtllm_fp8 assert TopKOutputChecker.format_is_bypassed(topk_output) AssertionError ``` The same `flashinfer_trtllm.py` module that produces corrupted output on M2.7 fails an explicit format check on V4-Flash. The assertion suggests the FP8 fused path is receiving a `topk_output` format that does not satisfy `TopKOutputChecker.format_is_bypassed(topk_output)`. ### Localization summary The tested failures localize to the **`flashinfer_trtllm` MoE runner path**: - V4-Flash reaches the FP8 fused-experts code at `flashinfer_trtllm.py:686`. - M2.7 returns corrupted text through the same runner path, though I did not capture a trace identifying the exact fused function reached. The M2.7 sweep makes these less likely as primary triggers: - FP4 GEMM backend: varied `auto`, `cutlass`, and `flashinfer_cutedsl`; all reproduced. - Prompt content / shape: four probes reproduced. - Tensor parallelism: reproduced at both TP=8 and TP=1 (TP=1 produces denser corruption than TP=8 across all four probes; the bug is not TP-distribution-specific). - SGLang image: reproduced under both `v0.5.12` and `v0.5.12.post1`. - Weight loading / basic scheduler path: the `flashinfer_cutlass` MoE path on the same image, hardware, weights, and probes produced clean output. ### What this issue does NOT validate Untested axes (all orthogonal; I can run any on request): - FlashInfer `0.6.12rc1` or newer (only `0.6.11.post1` tested, as bundled in `lmsysorg/sglang:v0.5.12.post1`). - SGLang `dev` / `nightly-dev` tags. - Different SM (only B200/SM100 tested; H100/H200 not tested). - Different attention backend (only `flashinfer` tested; `fa3`/`fa4`/`trtllm_mha`/`flashmla` not tested). - DeepEP / expert-parallelism enabled. - Speculative decoding enabled. - KV cache dtype other than default. - `--disable-flashinfer-autotune` (per the SGLang cookbook for DeepSeek-V4; not tested here). - Other NVFP4 MoE checkpoints beyond `nvidia/MiniMax-M2.7-NVFP4` and `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash`. - Direct FlashInfer-only repro (I observe the failure through SGLang's dispatch into FlashInfer). ### Repro artifacts Run directories on the test node, by purpose: - M2.7 isolation sweep manifest + per-probe smoke responses (A1 / X1 / TW configs at chat 2K/512 Poisson 4 rps): `track1-prepost-moe-isolation-20260525T180536Z/` - Cross-version probe artifacts (M2.7 on `v0.5.12.post1` + base `v0.5.12`, 4 probes per image, full analysis.txt): `mojibake-probe-20260525T182412Z/` - Localization probe artifacts (V4-Flash full crash log + M2.7 TP=1 single-rank probes): `localization-probes-20260525T184624Z/` - Reference (`flashinfer_cutlass` MoE) baseline + 3-run regimes: `track1-m27-reference-20260525T155755Z/` and `track1-reference-regimes-20260525T044957Z/` - Inside-container `pip freeze` (full 335-line capture from `lmsysorg/sglang:v0.5.12.post1`): `env-capture-20260525T191232Z/env.txt` Available inline on request: full V4-Flash traceback, complete `pip freeze`, per-probe response JSONs, M2.7 server logs around the bad-output requests, raw response bytes (hex) for byte-level inspection. I can post a gist with any subset the maintainer wants to inspect. ### Potential next checks - Test whether FlashInfer `0.6.12rc1` or newer changes either failure mode. I can run this if useful. - Open a parallel issue in `flashinfer-ai/flashinfer` if maintainers believe the root cause is upstream of SGLang dispatch. - Consider replacing the V4-Flash assertion with a clearer error or fallback path if this topk format is currently unsupported by the FP8 `flashinfer_trtllm` path. ### Related issues Adjacent reports surfaced during issue search. I did not find an exact duplicate; these appear adjacent on the axes called out per bullet (let triage decide on duplication). None of them include an applicable fix or workaround for the failure modes reported here. Included for triage context in case they share a root cause or a tracking owner. - #19971 — `MiniMax-M2.5 FP8 produces garbage output on B200 with default trtllm gemm backend`. Same hardware (B200), same model family (M2 series), same "garbage output" symptom, different quantization (FP8 vs NVFP4) and different layer (trtllm GEMM vs trtllm MoE). May indicate a pattern in trtllm-derived kernels on B200 for this family. - #18989 (closed) — `[Bug] deepseek 3.2 nvfp4 moe-runner-backend=flashinfer_trtllm illegal memory access`. Same MoE runner, different NVFP4 MoE checkpoint, different failure mode (illegal memory access vs mojibake/assertion). Same kernel family. - #24502 — `[Bug] flashinfer_trtllm MoE runner has no DeepEP fused func registered — blocks EP+NVFP4 on Blackwell`. Same MoE runner, Blackwell-specific structural gap on a different code path. - #20022 — `[Tracking] Minimax-M2.5 (G)B200 Functional Support and Optimizations`. Cross-linking for the M2-family Blackwell tracking owners. Reporter context: independent benchmarking work on Nebius B200 hardware.

signals.title: [Bug] Intermittent NCCL hang during Spec V2 verify with DSA backend + HiCache (post PR #18958 fix)
signals.text: ## Summary We are experiencing intermittent NCCL collective timeout / hang during EAGLE Spec V2 verify phase. We have two separate crash dumps: - **Crash 1**: Pure NCCL timeout hang (no CUDA assert observed), with TP rank desync during broadcast/allgather collectives. - **Crash 2**: Explicit `IndexKernel.cu:111: index out of bounds` CUDA device-side assertion, which poisoned the CUDA stream and caused subsequent NCCL timeout. The second crash appears **very similar** to #18744, but reproduces on a version that already contains the `record_stream` fix. Both crashes occur during the same code path (`_apply_cuda_graph_metadata` in `dsa_backend.py:1070`). ## Environment ``` Python: 3.12.11 | packaged by Anaconda, Inc. | (main, Jun 5 2025, 13:09:17) [GCC 11.2.0] CUDA available: True GPU 0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7: NVIDIA H20-3e GPU 0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7 Compute Capability: 9.0 CUDA_HOME: /root/miniconda3/envs/ray NVCC: Cuda compilation tools, release 12.9, V12.9.86 CUDA Driver Version: 535.261.03 PyTorch: 2.11.0+cu129 sglang: 0.5.12.post2.dev908+g2c8357f79 sglang-kernel: 0.4.3+cu129 flashinfer_python: 0.6.8.post1 flashinfer_cubin: 0.6.8.post1 flashinfer_jit_cache: 0.6.8.post1+cu129 triton: 3.6.0 transformers: 5.6.0 ``` GPU Topology: 8× H20-3e connected via NV18 (NVLink). ## Launch command ```bash python -m sglang.launch_server \ --model-path GLM-5.1-FP8 \ --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000 \ --enable-metrics --enable-cache-report \ --tp 8 \ --reasoning-parser glm45 --tool-call-parser glm47 \ --watchdog-timeout 900 \ --speculative-algorithm EAGLE \ --speculative-num-steps 3 \ --speculative-eagle-topk 1 \ --speculative-num-draft-tokens 4 \ --mem-fraction-static 0.85 \ --enable-hierarchical-cache \ --hicache-ratio 1.0 \ --hicache-storage-backend mooncake \ --hicache-storage-backend-extra-config '{"protocol":"rdma","device_name":"mlx5_bond_1,mlx5_bond_2,mlx5_bond_3,mlx5_bond_4,mlx5_bond_5,mlx5_bond_6,mlx5_bond_7,mlx5_bond_8","global_segment_size":"512gb","prefetch_threshold":256,"local_hostname":"21.29.161.70","master_server_address":"21.29.161.70:50051","metadata_server":"P2PHANDSHAKE"}' ``` Key features enabled: - **Spec V2** (EAGLE, 3 steps, topk=1, 4 draft tokens) - **DSA attention backend** (prefill=flashmla_sparse, decode=fa3) - **HiCache** (mooncake RDMA storage backend) - **Overlap scheduling** (default, not disabled) ## Crash Details We observed two separate hang incidents on the same machine within ~30 minutes. Both share the same py-spy stuck location but have different NCCL desync patterns. --- ### Crash 1: 2026-06-11 ~11:30 (ran ~5.5 hours before crash) **py-spy dump** — All 8 TP workers stuck: - **TP0**: stuck at `_apply_cuda_graph_metadata (dsa_backend.py:1070)` → `verify (eagle_worker_v2.py:1141)` - **TP1–TP7**: stuck at `resolve_seq_lens_cpu (overlap_utils.py:249)` → `synchronize (torch/cuda/streams.py:108)` **NCCL timeout error:** ``` [rank0] Watchdog caught collective operation timeout: WorkNCCL(SeqNum=240306, OpType=_ALLGATHER_BASE, ...) [rank3] Watchdog caught collective operation timeout: WorkNCCL(SeqNum=240303, OpType=BROADCAST, ...) ``` **NCCL trace PG status (PG 2):** ``` Rank 0: enqueued=240306, started=240305, completed=240305 Rank 1: enqueued=240306, started=240302, completed=240302 Rank 2: enqueued=240306, started=240303, completed=240302 Rank 3: enqueued=240306, started=240303, completed=240302 Rank 4: enqueued=240306, started=240303, completed=240302 Rank 5: enqueued=240306, started=240303, completed=240302 Rank 6: enqueued=240306, started=240303, completed=240302 Rank 7: enqueued=240306, started=240303, completed=240302 ``` **Scheduled (pending) ops at deadlock:** ``` Rank 0: seq=240306 op=nccl:_all_gather_base caller=_all_gather_into_tensor@parallel_state.py:861 Rank 3: seq=240304 op=nccl:broadcast caller=broadcast@parallel_state.py:1077 seq=240305 op=nccl:broadcast caller=broadcast@parallel_state.py:1077 seq=240306 op=nccl:_all_gather_base caller=_all_gather_into_tensor@parallel_state.py:861 ``` Rank 0 completed seq 240305 but other ranks are still stuck at seq 240302/240303 (broadcast ops), indicating Rank 0 advanced 2-3 collectives ahead before hitting the allgather that requires all ranks. --- ### Crash 2: 2026-06-12 ~11:53 (ran ~8 minutes before crash) **py-spy dump** — All 8 TP workers (only 6 captured by py-spy before TP6/TP7 crashed): - **TP0–TP5**: all stuck at `_apply_cuda_graph_metadata (dsa_backend.py:1070)` → `verify (eagle_worker_v2.py:1141)` **CUDA device-side assert (IndexKernel.cu):** ``` /pytorch/aten/src/ATen/native/cuda/IndexKernel.cu:111: operator(): block: [0,0,0], thread: [0,0,0] Assertion `-sizes[i] <= index && index < sizes[i] && "index out of bounds"` failed. (repeated for threads 0–7, multiple blocks) ``` **TP6 and TP7 crash traceback:** ```python torch.AcceleratorError: CUDA error: device-side assert triggered File "scheduler.py", line 2996, in run_batch self.future_map.resolve_seq_lens_cpu(batch) File "overlap_utils.py", line 249, in resolve_seq_lens_cpu self.fwd_prepare_d2h_stream.synchronize() ``` **NCCL trace PG status (PG 2):** ``` Rank 0: enqueued=2930, started=2929, completed=2929 Rank 1: enqueued=2930, started=2929, completed=2929 Rank 2: enqueued=2930, started=2929, completed=2929 Rank 3: enqueued=2930, started=2929, completed=2929 Rank 4: enqueued=2930, started=2929, completed=2929 Rank 5: enqueued=2930, started=2926, completed=2926 Rank 6: enqueued=2930, started=2927, completed=2926 Rank 7: enqueued=2930, started=2927, completed=2926 ``` **Scheduled (pending) ops at deadlock:** ``` Rank 0: seq=2930 op=nccl:_all_gather_base caller=_all_gather_into_tensor@parallel_state.py:861 Rank 5: seq=2927 op=nccl:broadcast caller=broadcast@parallel_state.py:1077 seq=2928 op=nccl:broadcast caller=broadcast@parallel_state.py:1077 seq=2929 op=nccl:broadcast caller=broadcast@parallel_state.py:1077 seq=2930 op=nccl:_all_gather_base caller=_all_gather_into_tensor@parallel_state.py:861 ``` Rank 0–4 completed through seq 2929 (all broadcasts done) and are waiting at the allgather (seq 2930). Rank 5–7 are stuck 3 broadcasts behind — the CUDA index-out-of-bounds assert poisoned their forward stream, preventing the broadcast kernels from executing. **Timeline:** - `11:53:19` — Last normal log (Prefill batch) - `12:03:19` — NCCL watchdog timeout (600000ms = 10 min, meaning hang started at ~11:53:19) - `12:04:19` — TP6/TP7 `device-side assert triggered` exception surfaced at `synchronize()` ## Relationship to #18744 This looks like the same class of bug fixed in PR #18958 (cross-stream tensor GC race condition with `future_indices`), but our build **already contains that fix**. The crash location is identical: - `_apply_cuda_graph_metadata (dsa_backend.py:1070)` — this is the `target_verify` branch which does `self.req_to_token[req_pool_indices, :max_seqlen_k]` Possible explanations: 1. The `record_stream` fix in #18958 doesn't fully cover all tensors involved in the DSA verify path 2. There's a similar race condition with `req_to_token` pool contents being freed/overwritten on another stream while `_apply_cuda_graph_metadata` is reading them 3. HiCache prefetch operations (running on background threads/streams) may introduce additional cross-stream interactions not covered by the existing `record_stream` calls ## Attachments Full artifacts available: - `stderr.log` (both cases): full server logs with NCCL timeout messages - `py-spy.log` (both cases): thread dumps of all TP workers at hang time - `nccl_trace0–7` (both cases): pickled NCCL flight recorder dumps (PyTorch `TORCH_NCCL_TRACE_BUFFER_SIZE` enabled)

signals.title: [Roadmap][DCP] Decode Context Parallelism & Helix Parallelism (2026 Q3)
signals.text: ## Current Status Decode Context Parallelism (DCP) shards the KV cache along the sequence dimension during decode, removing the redundancy pure TP incurs when `TP > num_kv_heads`. Helix Parallelism (arXiv 2507.07120) extends it with an All-to-All comm backend and decoupled attention/FFN parallelism. Measured on 16xGB300 with Qwen3.5-397B, TP16/DCP4 gives ~40% higher output throughput than DCP1 at concurrency 1024 (#32795). There has been some prior efforts on decode context parallelism: - DCP base for DeepSeek MLA on FlashInfer-MLA + FlashMLA #14194 - DCP for MHA/GQA on Triton / AMD-HIP #25090 - Consolidate DCP helpers into `layers/dcp/` and add DCP to the runtime parallel context #29365 #30478 - Helix A2A + FlashInfer-MNNVL comm backends and q-replicate #21637 - DCP for Kimi Linear, the first spec-decode x DCP unlock #32612 - Kimi-K3 day-0, landing the `kimi-k3` branch DCP work on `main` #32541 However, the current support only covers a few attention backends, half of Helix is unstarted, and several combinations are unguarded. To generalize the usage of DCP, we need to work on following features and tasks ## Communication Backend - [x] A2A + FlashInfer-MNNVL comm backends and query replication (Helix) #21637 @thanhhao98 - [ ] Reconcile three overlapping A2A follow-ups #33592 #33364 @Cerdore #32560 @MogicianWu - [ ] Decoupled attention/FFN parallelism (TPA vs KVP) #19436 ## Attention Backend ### MLA - [x] `flashinfer_mla`, the reference path with a CI gate at DSv3.1 TP8/DCP8, and `flashmla`, bf16 KV only #14194 - [x] `tokenspeed_mla` and`cutedsl_mla` #32612 - [ ] FA3 MLA decode #33325 @Vincent-bin - [ ] `flashmla` + fp8 KV — lift the `dcp_world_size == 1` assert #29760 @Aiziyou918 - [ ] `triton` MLA #30444 @Jiminator - [ ] `trtllm_mla` decode path ### GQA / MHA - [x] Fix the DCP KV head mapping #32858 @YAMY1234 - [x] `triton`, CUDA path untested #25090 - [ ] `trtllm_mha` decode #32795 @YAMY1234 - [ ] FA3 and flashinfer for GQA #26432 ### DSA - [ ] DSA DCP for DeepSeek-V3.2 / GLM-5.x #31821 @vincentzed ## Speculative Decoding x DCP (q_len > 1) Allowed only for Kimi Linear + DSpark on `tokenspeed_mla`/`cutedsl_mla` since #32612 and #32828 - [x] DCP x DSpark #32612 #32828 @Fridge003 @kpham-sgl - [ ] DCP x DFlash / EAGLE (general spec) #31785 @thanhhao98 ## PD Disaggregation and Hierarchical Cache - [x] PD disaggregation over Mooncake and NIXL #32837 @kpham-sgl - [x] HiCache L2 offload #33112 @Oasis-Git - [ ] PD + DCP + prefix-cache hit returns wrong output #33309 @ZhaiFeiyue - [ ] Reimplement the three `kimi-k3` PRs auto-closed by #32541 #33041 #33043 #33069 - [ ] Composability of DCP x DSpark x HiCache x PD Disagg ## Prefill CP See separate roadmap: #21788 ## Others - [x] Add a standalone document for DCP — `docs/` #34654 - [ ] DCP Phase 2 refactor, free functions to a strategy layer #30194 @thanhhao98 References: - CP roadmap (2026 Q3): #21788 - Helix feature request: #19436 - Additional attention backends for DCP: #26432 - Kimi K3 roadmap: #32607 - Helix paper: arXiv 2507.07120 @thanhhao98 @kpham-sgl @YAMY1234 @Fridge003

Otherwise, it will be closed. - [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed. ## Environment Collected inside the affected pod `kimi-k26-one` with: ```bash python3 -m sglang.check_env ``` Output: ```text Python: 3.12.3 (main, Mar 23 2026, 19:04:32) CUDA_COREDUMP_DIR=/tmp/crashdump CUDA_COREDUMP_FILE=/tmp/crashdump/cuda_coredump_%h.%p.%t CUDA_ENABLE_COREDUMP_ON_EXCEPTION=1 ``` SGLang launch command (from `crash_dump_2026-07-24_10-42-00.pkl`): ## Problem Summary A 523 MB CUDA coredump was produced by the worker for pod `kimi-k26-one`. The exception PC is inside FlashInfer's `RadixTopKRenormProbKernel_MultiCTA` sampling kernel. The pod where the dump file currently lives (`one-16`) is still `Running` with 0 restarts, so the fault was either caught by the CUDA crash-dump machinery or the affected worker was restarted transparently by Kubernetes. The process had `CUDA_ENABLE_COREDUMP_ON_EXCEPTION=1` configured, which explains why a dump was written. What we do not yet know is whether this was a recoverable error that SGLang handled, or whether it caused a hidden worker restart / request failure. ## Files Collected | File | Size | Note | |------|------|------| | `/tmp/crashdump/cuda_coredump_kimi-k26-one.148.1784556564` | 523.2 MB | CUDA GPU coredump (ELF `.nvcudmp`-style) | | `/tmp/crashdump/kimi-k26-one/crash_dump_2026-07-24_10-42-00.pkl` | 34.5 MB | SGLang crash snapshot: `server_args`, `requests` (778 reqs), `launch_command` | ## CUDA Coredump Analysis Results Analyzed with `cuda-gdb --batch -ex "target cudacore <file>" ...` on a pod with matching B300/sm_103 hardware. ### Faulting kernel ```cpp void flashinfer::sampling::RadixTopKRenormProbKernel_MultiCTA< 1024u, 4u, false, float, int>( float*, float*, int*, unsigned int, unsigned int, unsigned int, flashinfer::sampling::RadixRowState*, unsigned int, unsigned int) <<<(147, 1, 1), (1024, 1, 1)>>> ``` - `BLOCK_THREADS = 1024` - `VEC_SIZE = 4` - `SINGLE_CTA = false` → multi-CTA path - Data type `float`, index type `int` ### Fault location - **Device**: 0 (NVIDIA B300 SXM6 AC, PCI `1a:00.0`, sm_103) - **SM**: 21 (only SM 21 active: `Active SMs Mask = 0x00000000000000000000000000000000200000`) - **Block**: `(37, 0, 0)` - **Thread**: `(64, 0, 0)`, lane 0 - **PC**: `0x000070705b682050` - **Faulting SASS instruction**: ```asm => 0x70705b682050 <...RadixTopKRenormProbKernel_MultiCTA...+6992>: LDCU.128 UR16, c[0x0][0x380] ``` The faulting instruction is a **constant-memory descriptor load**. The immediately following instructions are generic-global loads/stores using descriptors (`LDG.E.128 desc[UR8][R18.64]`, `STG.E.128 desc[UR8][R16.64]`, etc.), so the crash is likely related to the descriptor for one of the kernel inputs (`probs`, `renormed_prob`) or for the multi-CTA `RadixRowState` buffer. ### Kernel context at crash ```text Kernel 0 (37,0,0) (0,0,0) (37,0,0) (0,0,0) 1 0x000070705b681fe0 0 (37,0,0) (1,0,0) (37,0,0) (31,0,0) 31 0x000070705b682030 0 * (37,0,0) (32,0,0) (37,0,0) (1023,0,0) 992 0x000070705b682050 0 ``` Most warps in block 37 are active at `0x70705b682050`; warp 2 is at the preceding instruction. This is a single-block, single-SM fault rather than a cross-GPU allreduce failure. ### Register snapshot (selected) ```text pc 0x70705b682050 <RadixTopKRenormProbKernel_MultiCTA...+6992> errorpc <unavailable> R0 0x3 R16 0x4a4 R42 0x0 R12 0x4ac R18 0x1b0eaac7 R43 0xe100 R21 0x1b0eafd7 R22 0x6a525960 R23 0x7070 UR8 0x0 UR12 0x66000000 UR16 0x66000000 P0 1, P3 1, P4 1, P6 1 ``` The `errorpc` register is unavailable, which is typical for a GPU coredump that captures the exception PC rather than a precise virtual-address fault. ### Source-code location (flashinfer) The kernel is defined in `include/flashinfer/topk.cuh`: - `RadixTopKRenormProbKernel_MultiCTA` (~L1602–L1835) - Host launcher `RadixTopKRenormProbMultiCTA` (~L1838–L1909) - Multi-CTA sync helpers `AdvanceRadixGroupBarrier` / `RadixGroupResetStateLastCTA` (~L174–L238) The same source file references issue #3610 concerning a race in the multi-CTA reset path on SM120/SM121, which suggests this synchronization code is subtle. ## Reproducer / Additional Notes **The crash has not been reproduced yet.** We did run a minimal sanity check of a related FlashInfer RadixTopK API (`top_k_page_table_transform`) in the same pod with the same B300 GPUs, and it completed without error. This only confirms the environment can execute FlashInfer sampling kernels; it does **not** reproduce the coredump. The coredump snapshot contains 778 in-flight requests, so the most promising next step is to extract the exact request/input that triggered `RadixTopKRenormProbKernel_MultiCTA` from the SGLang crash dump pickle (`crash_dump_2026-07-24_10-42-00.pkl`). ## Host / Node Observations `dmesg` on node `36.0.4.160` (via `agent`) shows an older Xid 31 on the same GPU device `0000:1a:00.0`: ```text NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:1a:00): 31, pid=301746, name=python3, channel 0x00000007 MMU Fault: ENGINE GRAPHICS GPC1 GPCCLIENT_T1_5 faulted @ 0x7509_cd600000. Fault is of type FAULT_PDE ACCESS_TYPE_VIRT_READ ``` This earlier fault (2026-06-15) is not necessarily the same incident, but the faulting device and MMU page-directory-entry read fault match the current coredump. ## Expected Behavior SGLang should either: 1. Not trigger a GPU exception in FlashInfer sampling, or 2. Surface the exception clearly to the operator (logs, metrics, exit code) so the root cause can be traced. ## Actual Behavior A coredump was produced in `/tmp/crashdump` while the pod appeared healthy, making it unclear whether the fault was transient, caught, or resulted in a hidden worker restart. ## What We Need Help With 1. How can SGLang expose whether a worker process was restarted and whether the crash dump corresponds to a now-dead worker? 2. Could SGLang's sampling/top-k invocation path be passing a stale / null pointer to FlashInfer under certain request patterns? 3. Guidance on extracting the exact failing request from the `.pkl` crash snapshot so we can reproduce it. 4. Whether SGLang should disable or gate the multi-CTA RadixTopK path on Blackwell until the kernel crash is resolved upstream. ## Additional Context - The coredump filename indicates the crash originated from pod `kimi-k26-one`, not `one`, even though the file was found in `one-16`'s `/tmp/crashdump`. This is consistent with `CUDA_COREDUMP_DIR=/tmp/crashdump` being a shared node path or the file being copied after the crash. - The filename timestamp `1784556564` corresponds to **2026-07-20 14:09:24 UTC**, while the `.pkl` and directory mtime are **2026-07-24 10:42 UTC**, indicating the dump was preserved/copied after the original crash.
