signals.title: [RFC] Replace the MLX runner-stub split with one Torch-owned SRT path and an exported whole-model MLX region
signals.text: This updates the original proposal (can be found in previous edited version) after the Torch/MLX interoperability work in [#32984](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/32984). The stub problem remains, but zero-copy access to Torch MPS storage gives us a smaller solution: keep one standard SRT serving path and use MLX or Metal only for computation. The architecture below has been implemented and validated behind a default-off flag in the accompanying draft PR, [noob-se7en/sglang#2](https://github.com/noob-se7en/sglang/pull/2) (branch `rfc-whole-region-mlx-clean`, stacked on the #32984 bridge): none of it is upstream yet; measured results are in the Evidence section. ## Why this matters MLX compatibility bugs have repeatedly reached users through startup failures, request-time attribute errors, incomplete feature paths, lifecycle leaks, and configuration drift. Examples include #26882, #29681, #30181, #30389, #30547, #32115, #32445, #32446 and #32447. The same split also creates review burden. A scheduler or `ModelRunner` change may not mention MLX, but an MLX reviewer still has to check whether the new path reaches the stub, whether the required field was initialized, whether the MLX worker intercepts the operation, and whether copied framework calculations still match core. In #30547, for example, MLX silently ignored the configured `max_running_requests` because its stub maintained a separate calculation. #32115 then had to update that copied behavior again. As long as SGLang has two owners for serving state, fixes in the standard path can continue to drift from MLX. ## Current flow Today Apple Silicon serving has two execution paths selected at the backend level: ```text Scheduler | +-- Standard Torch path | TpModelWorker | Torch ModelRunner | Torch model | Torch request tables and KV cache | +-- Native MLX path MlxTpModelWorker MlxModelRunnerStub: Torch-shaped bookkeeping MlxModelRunner: model execution mlx-lm model separate request and KV lifecycle ``` `MlxModelRunnerStub` exists because generic serving code still expects a Torch-shaped `ModelRunner`, while the actual model is loaded and executed by a separate MLX runner. The arrangement is safe only for fields and paths that have already been mirrored and reviewed. The problem is not simply that the stub is incomplete. The framework has two implementations of model loading, request state, KV ownership, feature handling, and lifecycle behavior. <!-- Add updated current-flow diagram here. --> ## Proposed flow Apple Silicon should use the standard Scheduler, worker, and Torch `ModelRunner` as the only owners of serving state: ```text Standard Scheduler Standard TpModelWorker Torch ModelRunner Torch-owned model, weights, requests and KV cache +-- eager Torch MPS forward (always available; also serves any | batch the region rejects before launch) +-- direct Metal AOT/JIT operators (existing fused-op dispatch) +-- exported whole-model MLX region (standard graph-runner slot; eligibility and export checked per batch before any device work) ``` Torch owns the model and storage. Metal and MLX are computation backends behind the two dispatch points SGLang already has: the fused-operation dispatch for individual operators, and the graph-runner slots for the exported region. They may read or update Torch-owned buffers through an explicit contract, but they do not load a second model or own another scheduler, request table, KV pool, sampler, or weight-update lifecycle. Models the region cannot serve continue to use the complete Torch MPS path. <!-- Add updated proposed-flow diagram here. --> ## Design ### One owner for serving state | Concern | Authoritative owner | | --- | --- | | Scheduling, batching, request lifecycle and Radix cache | Standard SGLang Scheduler | | Model loading, parameters, request tables and KV allocation | Torch `ModelRunner` | | Logits, sampling, logprobs, grammar, LoRA and weight updates | Existing standard SRT components | | Operator dispatch and region selection | Existing fused-op dispatch and the standard graph-runner slot | | Accelerated computation | Torch MPS, Metal AOT/JIT or MLX | Neither dispatch point introduces a second copy of framework state. New Scheduler and `ModelRunner` behavior is inherited automatically because Apple Silicon uses the standard implementations. ### Direct Metal for small operations Model-independent operations such as RMSNorm, fused add and RMSNorm, and SiLU-and-multiply should use the existing fused-operation dispatch mechanism: ```text SGLang operation +-- supported Metal AOT/JIT kernel +-- otherwise Torch implementation ``` These kernels operate directly on Torch MPS buffers and do not cross into MLX. A separate model registry is not needed for this level. ### Capture-and-lower MLX region MLX becomes useful when a sufficiently broad region can remain in MLX long enough to amortize framework dispatch and synchronization. The region is not assembled from per-model MLX blocks. It is captured from the standard Torch model and lowered to MLX. Support for a new architecture is gated by lowering coverage of the ATen ops in its graph. #### Region construction by torch.export Non-strict `torch.export` captures the loaded model's forward (transformer body plus LM head) as one ATen FX graph, traced with a real serving `ForwardBatch` for a given batch shape (decode batch size or a Prefill token bucket). Attention layers emit a semantic custom op, `sglang::unified_attention_with_output`, carrying `k_cache`, `v_cache`, `req_to_token` and `seq_lens`. The op is only emitted under `torch.compiler.is_exporting()`, so eager execution is unchanged. #### FX-to-MLX lowering The lowering (`python/sglang/srt/hardware_backend/mlx/fx_backend.py`) walks the exported graph once: - Generic ATen ops map to `mx` ops. The mapping is written per ATen op, not per model, so coverage added for one architecture carries over to any other that uses the same ops. - The attention op lowers to a deferred radix-attention Metal kernel (`python/sglang/kernels/ops/attention/_deferred_radix_attention_mlx.py`), templated on head counts and head dim taken from the KV-pool shapes. No per-model kernel code. - KV pool buffers bind as persistent zero-copy DLPack views of Torch MPS storage. Fusion (fused QKV post-processing, RMSNorm chains) belongs in the lowering, as ATen-subgraph pattern matches to custom MLX kernels. The hand-fused blocks in yeahdongcn/sglang#7 show the available headroom; a pattern match gives the same win to every model whose graph contains it. #### Execution and deferred KV commit Execution is one lazy MLX region per step. The step's new K/V leaves the region as small delta outputs rather than in-place pool writes; a Torch-side Metal-JIT commit kernel (`python/sglang/kernels/ops/kvcache/_deferred_kv_commit_metal_jit.py`) scatters the deltas into the Torch-owned pool. #### Serving runner `MlxRegionRunner` (`python/sglang/srt/hardware_backend/mlx/region_runner.py`) occupies both graph runner slots, selected in `model_runner_components/cuda_graph_setup.py` behind the env flag `SGLANG_ENABLE_MLX_WHOLE_REGION` (default off). - Export is lazy, one executor per batch size or prefill token bucket (about 1.9 s for Qwen3-0.6B); the executor is reused across steps. - Guards: decode batch size up to 16, and no LoRA (the region binds views of the base weights, so adapted requests must stay on Torch). Speculative decoding, encoder inputs, and hierarchical sparse attention are also rejected, though none of these are available on Torch MPS today anyway. - A batch size whose export fails is blacklisted and served transparently by eager Torch. A pool-identity check re-exports if the KV pool is reallocated. Export temporarily swaps fused custom ops for their plain-Torch forms and restores them afterwards, so the eager path is untouched. ### Executor lifecycle Operators route through the existing fused-operation dispatch. The exported region occupies the standard graph-runner slot and is built lazily, one executor per batch shape. An executor checks request eligibility before device work, invalidates its views when Torch weights change or the KV pool is reallocated, and releases compiled graphs and borrowed views on replacement or shutdown. Construction is atomic: views, lowering and a KV write-verify pass complete before the executor serves traffic, and a failed export rolls back and blacklists that batch size. An executor must never use a view after Torch replaces or releases the storage. ### Fallback behavior Torch is the complete correctness fallback. - Static model or runtime incompatibility leaves the graph-runner slot empty at startup. - Request-specific incompatibility (mode, batch size, speculative decoding, encoder inputs, LoRA) is rejected by the runner's eligibility check before any device work. - Export failure for a batch shape blacklists that shape; it is served by eager Torch from then on. - A Metal operator outside its kernel contract falls back to the Torch implementation through the fused-op dispatch. - Failure after the region launches or KV state is committed is surfaced; it must not retry the same forward through Torch. Which path executed should be visible through the fused-op trace and runner logs so tests can prove it. ## Why this removes the stub failure class This proposal removes the second runner instead of adding more fields or methods to its compatibility adapter. - Scheduler and `ModelRunner` state no longer needs to be copied into MLX. - Shared calculations such as request-capacity resolution have one implementation. - Radix caching, sampling, logprobs, grammar, LoRA and weight updates stay on their standard paths. - MLX and Metal review is limited to lowering coverage, numerical behavior, storage lifetime, and kernel performance. MPS testing remains necessary because core code can still introduce CUDA-only assumptions. The change removes the more fragile requirement to mirror ordinary serving behavior into a partial `ModelRunner` subclass and a parallel lifecycle. ## Evidence PR #32984 validates the Torch 2.13.x and MLX 0.32.x interoperability needed by this design: - Torch-owned MPS storage can be borrowed by MLX without payload-sized CPU copies; - owned copies and borrowed views have separate APIs and lifetime contracts; - producer synchronization, lazy MLX evaluation, and output export remain explicit; and - unsupported runtime combinations fail before model loading. The same work also shows that zero-copy does not mean zero overhead. Repeatedly routing small diffusion normalization operations through MLX was slower end to end because each call still paid framework dispatch and synchronization. This is why small operations should prefer direct Metal kernels and MLX should run a broad region rather than one operation at a time. The capture-and-lower region has been measured at serving level against every existing Apple Silicon path. End-to-end serving comparison for the same workload (Qwen3-0.6B bf16, 512 in / 65 out), four configurations on the same machine, all warm. The old implementations are measured at this branch's base commit: "Torch eager (base commit)" is the plain upstream Torch MPS path, and "MLX lane + overlap (base commit)" is the native MLX path with its shipped overlap scheduling engaged (the lane is removed on this branch, so both run from the base). "MLX region (this branch)" is the only column containing this proposal's code, enabled with `SGLANG_ENABLE_MLX_WHOLE_REGION=1`. Every SGLang column runs through the real scheduler via the engine's offline-throughput path (the lane's overlap lives in the scheduler, so `bench_one_batch`, which bypasses it, is not comparable), with exact-length random prompts, temperature 0, fresh prompts per run so the radix cache cannot short-circuit prefill, three runs per phase, and medians of the warm runs reported. The mlx-lm column is Apple's standalone generator (`mlx_lm generate`, same checkpoint) as an external reference. | Qwen3-0.6B, 512 in / 65 out, e2e output tok/s | SGLang Torch eager (base commit) | SGLang MLX lane + overlap (base commit) | SGLang MLX region (this branch) | mlx-lm (standalone) (not SGLang) | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | | Time to first token (ms) | 318 | 157 | 233 | 135 (prompt processing only) | | Batch 1 | 18.1 | 75.7 | 58.7 (3.2x) | 80.8 | | Batch 4 | 39.2 | 95.5 | 115.3 (2.9x) | — | | Batch 8 | 49.0 | 126.8 | 167.8 (3.4x) | 228.6 | | Batch 16 | 57.4 | 130.0 | 204.9 (3.6x) | 251.0 | Speedups in the region column are against base-commit eager. One-time export cost is about 1.9 s per batch shape, absorbed by the first run. This branch's own flag-off path (the region's eager fallback) sits above base eager at low batch and converges by batch 8: time to first token 270 ms, then 21.5, 42.8, 53.7, 57.2 tok/s down the same rows. That 10 to 19 percent low-batch gain comes from the PR's platform-dispatch fix and direct Metal operators; it is kept out of the main columns so it is not conflated with the region. The columns split honestly. The lane leads single-request serving where it runs (its `mx.async_eval` launch/finalize hides per-step host work the region path currently exposes; overlap for the unified path is a listed follow-up). The region leads from batch 4 up and keeps scaling through batch 16 while the lane goes flat; the lane's batched runs also showed intermittent stalls (batch-8 spread 104.8 to 148.9 tok/s across warm runs, medians reported). - Region-boundary medians (model forward only): exported MLX decode 12.19 ms, native `mlx_lm` 11.31 ms (about 93%), Torch region 42.8 ms. Prefill region 142.1 ms against 126.0 ms for `mlx_lm` (89%) after routing no-prefix prefill through `mx.fast` causal attention; the remaining gap is un-fused norm and rope chains in the lowering. - Server-level A/B through `launch_server` (greedy, 32 tokens): exact token match with decode-only region serving. With prefill also in the region, one output diverged at step 12 via a certified exact bf16 logit tie (both engines' top-1 margins 0.0625, near-tie classifier passes); padding was ruled out separately (padded and unpadded executors agree to one ulp with identical argmax). - The validation harness (`benchmark/mps_mlx/bench_export_region.py`) passes for decode and prefill: logit cosine and top-5 gates, exact KV commit, greedy match, and 17-step lockstep generation parity. The same path was then run on two more architectures with no model-specific changes. Serving decode compares the same server with the flag off (this branch's Torch MPS path, direct Metal operators included) and on (the exported region); both include sampling and scheduler overhead: | Model | Family | Q/KV heads | Head dim | Lockstep parity (17 steps) | Decode per step, batch 1 (flag off to on) | Speedup | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | ---: | ---: | | Qwen3-0.6B | qwen3 | 16/8 | 128 | match | 44.0 to 13.8 ms | 3.2x | | Qwen2.5-Coder-1.5B | qwen2 | 12/2 | 128 | match | 58.3 to 27.1 ms | 2.15x | | SmolLM2-360M-Instruct | llama | 15/5 | 64 | match | 31.6 to 8.7 ms | 3.6x | ## Suggested rollout The work splits into a core stack that should merge as one reviewed unit, and follow-ups that plug into stable seams of that stack and can proceed in parallel afterwards without touching its internals. ### Core stack (this RFC and its PR; the review unit) 1. Land the runtime and tensor-bridge contract from #32984. *(PR in review)* 2. Implement the capture-and-lower region and the serving runner for decode and single-request prefill. *(implemented in the branch, flag-gated behind `SGLANG_ENABLE_MLX_WHOLE_REGION`, default off; not yet upstream)* 3. Run the standard Torch serving path on MPS, replacing the native MLX lane. The same change removes `MlxModelRunner`, `MlxModelRunnerStub`, `MlxTpModelWorker`, the separate cache lifecycle, `mlx-lm` loading, and `SGLANG_USE_MLX`. Keeping both paths would preserve the dual-owner drift this proposal exists to end. *(implemented in the branch; not yet upstream)* 4. Add correctness-qualified direct Metal semantic operators. *(implemented in the branch; not yet upstream)* The region flag is off by default; every shape the region cannot serve is rejected before device work and served by Torch, and each gap below is a fallback. ### Follow-ups (independent items, each against one seam) - **Lowering fusion:** pattern-match RMSNorm and RoPE ATen subgraphs to `mx.fast` kernels. Seam: the op table in `fx_backend.py`. Target: prefill region 142 to about 126 ms; benefits every architecture at once. - **Packed multi-request prefill:** lift the single-request guard with per-request segmenting in the prefill graph. Seam: `region_runner.py` guards plus the prefill variants in `fx_backend.py`. - **Logits-path capture:** export through the standard `LogitsProcessor` instead of the raw LM-head matmul, lifting the logit-scale and softcapping rejection (Gemma-class models). Seam: the export wrapper in `export_validation.py`. - **New model mechanisms:** sliding-window and MLA attention, MoE routing, and SSM state; each is a kernel or lowering addition, never per-model code. Seam: the deferred-attention kernels for the attention variants, the op table in `fx_backend.py` for MoE and SSM ops. - **Weight-update lifecycle test:** exercise the update RPCs end to end against the storage-identity re-export. Seam: tests only. - **Overlap scheduling on MPS:** hide per-step host work behind device time; the largest remaining end-to-end decode lever. Seam: scheduler, independent of the region internals. - **Quantized serving:** restore quantized inference on Apple Silicon, the one capability lost with the native lane. Route: a Torch-side quantized checkpoint format plus a lowering to `mx.quantized_matmul`. Seam: model loading and the op table in `fx_backend.py`. - **CI:** model-free MPS tests run automatically; document a repeatable real-model path until Apple Silicon CI hardware exists. ## Alternatives considered ### Keep the native MLX runner behind a stronger worker contract This was the original proposal. It remains the fallback if the unified Torch-owned path cannot meet serving or performance requirements. It improves the boundary but preserves two model and KV lifecycles. ### Dispatch individual Torch operations through MLX This is generic but pays the framework boundary repeatedly. Direct Metal kernels are a better fit for small operations. ### Model adapters plus reusable MLX blocks An earlier revision of this proposal built the region from per-architecture adapters: a declarative model descriptor resolved through a registry, composing reusable MLX normalization, attention and MLP blocks. The adapter layer was introduced to cut the per-model duplication of the provider approach below. It has real advantages: block-level fusion is available immediately and nothing depends on `torch.export`. But the descriptor and blocks are still a second implementation of the model math, per architecture, which is the drift class this document exists to remove. The exported region keeps the Torch model as the single source of truth and moves fusion into the lowering. ### Per-model MLX and Metal implementations behind providers The parallel draft (yeahdongcn/sglang#7) takes this shape: a provider registry resolves a typed model-family plan, and each supported family carries its own MLX/Metal implementation. It produces a broad execution region and its hand-fused variants show the available fusion headroom (90%+ of `mlx_lm` prefill on M1), but common transformer logic is duplicated across architectures and every family is a separately maintained rewrite. The exported region preserves the broad region without either.

signals.title: [Bug] [Diffusion] Cache-first fast path returns weightless snapshots
signals.text: ### Checklist - [x] I searched related issues but found no solution. - [x] The bug persists in the latest version. - [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback. - [x] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed. - [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed. ### Describe the bug maybe_download_model() in python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/utils/hf_diffusers_utils.py resolves the cache with snapshot_download(..., local_files_only=True). On the force_diffusers_model=False component path it returned that snapshot unconditionally: # hf_diffusers_utils.py:873-874 (current main) if not force_diffusers_model: [return str(local_path)](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/utils/hf_diffusers_utils.py#L825) Offline there is no remote file list, so a resolved path cannot be told from a complete path. Two distinct cache states resolve as valid hits while holding no component weights: 1. The model_index.json-only probe stub (originally filed). maybe_download_model_index() probes a repo by fetching only model_index.json via hf_hub_download. That single-file fetch writes a full cache entry — blobs/, refs/main, snapshots/<sha>/model_index.json — so a later local_files_only=True resolve returns a directory containing exactly one file. 2. The snapshots/ parent on a corrupt ref (found while reproducing #1). When refs/<revision> is truncated to 0 bytes — an interrupted or out-of-disk ref write — the offline resolver reads the revision as "" and joins it onto snapshots/, returning the parent directory as a hit. That directory contains only per-revision subdirectories, so every component lookup below it misses. In both cases maybe_download_model() returns a path with no weights and skips the download. Cause 2 is the more confusing one in practice: it surfaces far downstream as a misleading FileNotFoundError: Could not resolve vae from model_index.json under .../snapshots/, which reads as missing weights when the weights are present one level down.. ### Reproduction Cause 1 — HF_HUB_CACHE=/tmp/repro_cache PYTHONPATH=/tmp/sgl_head/python python [repro_chache_fast_bug.py](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/30857466/repro_chache_fast_bug.py) ``` STEP1 probe ok, pipeline = StableDiffusionPipeline STEP2 returned: /tmp/repro_cache/models--hf-internal-testing--tiny-stable-diffusion-pipe/snapshots/3ee6c9f2... STEP2 contents: ['model_index.json'] ``` Cause 2 — python [repro_corrupt_ref_snapshots_parent.py](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/30889779/repro_corrupt_ref_snapshots_parent.py) ``` STEP1 healthy resolve: /tmp/repro_ref_cache/models--hf-internal-testing--tiny-stable-diffusion-pipe/snapshots/3ee6c9f225f088ad5d35b624b6514b091e6a4849 STEP1 contents: ['.gitattributes', 'README.md', 'feature_extractor', 'model_index.json', 'safety_checker', 'scheduler'] ... STEP2 refs/main size: 0 STEP2 returned: /tmp/repro_ref_cache/models--hf-internal-testing--tiny-stable-diffusion-pipe/snapshots/ STEP2 basename: STEP2 contents: ['3ee6c9f225f088ad5d35b624b6514b091e6a4849'] ``` ### Environment sglang commit: 06f32bab6baa12b8616a5260e6f2fa2597eb930e Python: 3.12.13 OS: Linux-6.17.0-41-generic-x86_64-with-glibc2.42 torch: 2.12.0+xpu huggingface_hub: 1.24.0 diffusers: 0.38.0 transformers: 5.12.1 modelscope: 1.38.1

signals.title: Cache-DiT silently remains disabled when breakable CUDA graphs are enabled
signals.text: ## What happens `DenoisingStage._maybe_enable_cache_dit` returns early when `--enable-breakable-cuda-graph` is set: ```python if self.server_args.enable_breakable_cuda_graph: # Cache-DiT wraps transformer.forward with step-skipping control # flow that must not be baked into a captured CUDA graph. return ``` The early return is deliberate and the reason is sound. The problem is that it is silent: enabling both `--enable-breakable-cuda-graph` and `SGLANG_CACHE_DIT_ENABLED=1` yields no caching, no error and no warning. The only symptom is a 1.00x speedup, which is easy to misread as "Cache-DiT does not help on this model". This produces the same user-visible symptom as #33827 — a silent 1.00x result — but requires a different diagnostic, since in that case Cache-DiT was mounted successfully and the cache simply never hit. The warning proposed here addresses the BCG configuration conflict specifically. ## Suggested behaviour Emit an explicit warning when Cache-DiT is requested but suppressed because breakable CUDA graphs are enabled. A startup-time check alone is not sufficient. Cache-DiT can also be requested per request — MiniMax-H3 mounts it dynamically for `quality="high"` batches in `minimax_h3/stages/denoising.py::_maybe_enable_cache_dit` — so the warning should also fire the first time a request asks for Cache-DiT while BCG suppresses it. Once per process is enough; this should not log per request.

signals.title: [RFC] Remove the torchao integration (`--torchao-config`)
signals.text: ## Summary `--torchao-config` has been **broken since 2026-04-19** — every accepted value raises `ImportError` — and the breakage went undetected for ~4 months. The feature has had no new capability since 2024-09-28, no commit from its upstream author since 2024-12-20, and no CI coverage at any point. I propose we remove it outright — no deprecation period — and drop `torchao` from the core dependency block of `python/pyproject.toml`. A deprecation window exists to give working behavior time to migrate; there is no working behavior here, so it would only delay the cleanup. ## 1. It is currently broken, not merely unused `python/sglang/srt/layers/torchao_utils.py:47-56` imports five snake_case factory functions. torchao renamed all of them to `*Config` dataclasses and removed the old names — and that landed **before** the version we pin, not in a later one: ```console $ python -c "import torchao; print(torchao.__version__)" 0.17.0+cu130 $ python -c "from torchao.quantization import int4_weight_only" ImportError: cannot import name 'int4_weight_only' from 'torchao.quantization' ``` The import block pulls all five names at once, so this is not a partial breakage — every documented value fails identically: | `--torchao-config` | result | | --- | --- | | `int8wo` | `ImportError` | | `int8dq` | `ImportError` | | `int4wo-128` | `ImportError` | | `fp8wo` | `ImportError` | | `fp8dq-per_row` | `ImportError` | <details> <summary>Reproduction</summary> ```python import torch from sglang.srt.layers.torchao_utils import apply_torchao_config_to_model m = torch.nn.Sequential() m.add_module("proj", torch.nn.Linear(64, 64)) for cfg in ["int8wo", "int8dq", "int4wo-128", "fp8wo", "fp8dq-per_row"]: try: apply_torchao_config_to_model(m, cfg) print(cfg, "OK") except Exception as e: print(cfg, "FAIL:", type(e).__name__, str(e)[:80]) ``` All five print `FAIL: ImportError`. </details> ### How it broke, and why nobody noticed ``` 2026-04-19 #23119 "[CI] Add per-job uv venv isolation and upgrade CI version to Cuda 13" - "torchao==0.9.0", + "torchao==0.17.0", ``` The pin jumped eight minor versions as **collateral of a CUDA-13 CI upgrade**, not as a deliberate torchao upgrade, so nobody audited the API surface. Two things kept it silent afterwards: - **No CI coverage.** The only tests are `test/manual/quant/test_torchao.py` and the torchao case in `test/manual/test_srt_engine_with_quant_args.py`. `test/README.md:15` documents `manual/` as "Non-CI tests for local debugging or special setups." - **#17626 (2026-01-22, "Lazy import torchao")** moved the `if torchao_config == "": return` guard *above* the import block. Intended to suppress import-time warnings, it also means the `ImportError` only fires for users who actually pass the flag, rather than at startup. No issue has been filed in those four months. That is the usage signal. ## 2. Development history Full history of `torchao_utils.py` — 16 commits: | Period | What happened | | --- | --- | | 2024-09-09 → 2024-12-20 | Real development. 6 of 8 commits by Jerry Zhang (torchao maintainer), who built it upstream-in. | | **2024-09-28** | `Add float8 dynamic quant to torchao_utils` (#1528) — **last time the feature gained a capability.** The `int8dq/int8wo/int4wo/fp8wo/fp8dq` menu has been frozen for ~23 months. | | **2024-12-20** | #2528 (gemlite) — **last commit by torchao upstream.** | | 2025-01-22 → 2026-01-22 | Three maintenance commits, net **negative** LOC: layered-loading plumbing (#3061, generic on-the-fly quant, not torchao work), a Conv3d skip for VLMs (#13508, +14/−3), and `clean up gemlite usage` (#14444, **−41 lines, pure deletion**). | | 2026-01-22 | `Lazy import torchao` (#17626), +4/−3 — see above. | The two most recent commits are a backend removal and an import deferral. Nothing has been added since 2024. ## 3. It was never a first-class quantization path - **Not registered.** `torchao` is absent from `QUANTIZATION_METHODS` (`python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/__init__.py:72`). It is a bolt-on flag that rewrites modules after load, selecting layers by substring match (`"proj" in fqn`) rather than by any checkpoint-declared config. - **Dead branch.** `python/sglang/srt/models/paddleocr_vl.py:293` tests `quant_config.get_name() in ["bitsandbytes", "torchao"]` — unreachable, since no such name is registered. - **No checkpoint support.** sglang cannot load torchao-serialized HF checkpoints (the `pytorch/*` org). That is vLLM's torchao backend; sglang never had an equivalent. ## 4. At the current frontier (NVFP4 / MXFP8 / MXFP4), torchao offers nothing we lack This is the decisive point. The `--torchao-config` menu is int8/int4/fp8 only — **no fp4, no mx formats at all.** torchao's work on those formats lives elsewhere in the library and is behind what we already ship (checked against torchao `main`, v0.19.0): | | torchao | sglang today | | --- | --- | --- | | status | `torchao/prototype/mx_formats/` — not exported from `torchao.quantization` | registered: `modelopt_fp4`, `nvfp4_online`, `petit_nvfp4`, `mxfp4`, `mxfp8`, `mxfp_w4a8`, `quark_mxfp4` | | NVFP4 linear | `torch._scaled_mm` (cuBLAS) + mslk triton quant | flashinfer `mm_fp4`, trtllm-gen, cutlass, marlin fallback | | MXFP8 / MXFP4 | `_addmm_mx_dispatch` → `_scaled_mm` | flashinfer / trtllm-gen, `triton_kernels`, aiter on ROCm | | MoE | `aten._grouped_mm` → `scaled_grouped_mm` only | flashinfer-cutlass + trtllm-gen fused MoE runners | torchao's genuine state-of-the-art contributions are **training-side** — float8/MXFP8 pretraining, MXFP8 MoE training, QAT, PARQ. None of that is reachable from an inference server. **Most importantly, owning these paths is what lets us write faster kernels.** Every row above where sglang wins is a row where we call a kernel we can tune, autotune, and specialize per shape and per architecture — flashinfer, trtllm-gen, cutlass, cute-dsl. torchao's inference path bottoms out in `torch._scaled_mm` / `_addmm_mx_dispatch`, which hands the shape to cuBLAS and ends the conversation: no tactic selection, no epilogue fusion, no per-model tuning, no ability to fix a bad shape without waiting on an upstream release. A dependency that can only ever be as fast as the default cuBLAS kernel is not a quantization backend we want on the critical path. And this is where the hardware is going, not a niche: **future architectures prioritize NVFP4 / MXFP8 / MXFP4** — Blackwell and beyond put the block-scaled 4- and 8-bit formats in the tensor cores as the first-class datapath, with hardware scale-factor handling, and that is where the remaining perf is. **int8 and int4 are legacy formats.** They were the answer when tensor cores had no sub-8-bit float support and quantization had to be integer; that constraint is gone. On current and future hardware int8/int4 are emulated or de-prioritized paths, they carry accuracy penalties that block-scaled fp4 does not, and no frontier checkpoint ships in them. The entire `--torchao-config` menu — `int8wo`, `int8dq`, `int4wo-128`, plus per-tensor `fp8wo`/`fp8dq` — is the previous generation's frontier, and where users still want int4 we already serve it better through AWQ and GPTQ-marlin. Carrying a broken dependency for legacy formats while the formats that matter are served by kernels we control is exactly backwards. ## 5. What keeping it costs - **`torchao==0.17.0` is a hard pin in the core `dependencies` block** of `python/pyproject.toml:80` — every CUDA install pays ~21 MB and a version constraint for a feature that raises `ImportError`. - **The pin drags others.** `python/pyproject_other.toml` pins `peft>=0.18.0,<0.19.0 # Pin to <0.19.0 due to torchao incompatibility` in two places. - **Dedicated noise suppression** exists only to hide torchao's import-time warnings: `python/sglang/srt/utils/hf_transformers_patches.py:76-88` and `:224-230`, plus `python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/utils/logging_utils.py:565`. - `python/sglang/check_env.py` lists `"torchao"` twice (lines 29 and 43). ## 6. Prior art: how vLLM handles it Worth comparing, because vLLM's integration is the one people cite — and it is a different thing, built differently. **vLLM does not depend on torchao.** No occurrences in `requirements/`, `setup.py`, `pyproject.toml`, or `docker/`. It is a lazily-imported optional backend gated on `find_spec("torchao")`; the docs instruct users to install it themselves. | | sglang | vLLM | | --- | --- | --- | | entry point | `--torchao-config` flag, on-the-fly quant post-load | `quant_method: "torchao"` in HF config | | in quant registry | ✗ | ✓ `"torchao": TorchAOConfig` | | checkpoint loading | none | `is_checkpoint_torchao_serialized`, safetensors, `ModuleFqnToConfig` regex | | layer skipping | substring `"proj" in fqn` | `modules_to_not_convert` + `should_skip()` | | API drift handling | pinned, broken | `torchao_version_at_least("0.15.0")` runtime gates | | dependency | hard pin, core deps | not a dependency | That last row is why theirs still works and ours does not. **But vLLM's backend is also in maintenance mode.** Last substantive change: `update torchao safetensors impl` (2025-12-08). The ~8 months since are janitorial — typo fixes, `Optional[X]` → `X | None`, torch-version cleanup, one error-message bugfix (2026-05-23), and a ROCm CI skip (2026-07-27). Jerry Zhang's last vLLM torchao commit was 2025-11-04. Notably, the one idea that grew out of it — `Support RL online quantization with torchao` (2025-10-01) — was generalized into vLLM-wide **layerwise reload / QeRL** infra, actively developed through 2026-07-25 and no longer torchao-specific. The reusable concept outlived the backend. ## 7. Proposal Remove it in the next release. No deprecation window — every code path already raises `ImportError`, so there is nothing working to give users time to migrate off. **Remove:** - `python/sglang/srt/layers/torchao_utils.py` - the `torchao_config` server arg (`python/sglang/srt/server_args.py:2015-2019`) - `python/sglang/srt/model_executor/model_runner.py:83` and `:752-755` - the layered-loading torchao branch, `python/sglang/srt/model_loader/loader.py:907-960` - the dead `"torchao"` name at `python/sglang/srt/models/paddleocr_vl.py:293` - `test/manual/quant/test_torchao.py` and the torchao case in `test/manual/test_srt_engine_with_quant_args.py` - the duplicate `check_env.py:43` entry **Dependencies:** move `torchao` out of the core `dependencies` block. The diffusion path keeps it transitively — `cache-dit==1.3.0` declares `torchao>=0.14.1; extra == "quantization"`, backing the `quantize_config` YAML documented in `docs/docs/sglang-diffusion/cache_dit.mdx`. Nothing in sglang calls torchao directly there. This should also let us revisit the `peft<0.19.0` pins. **Docs:** drop the torchao section in `docs/docs/advanced_features/quantization.mdx:829-848` and the flag rows in `docs/docs/advanced_features/server_arguments.mdx:2600` and `docs/docs/hardware-platforms/ascend-npus/reference/support_features.mdx:2250`.

signals.title: [Bug] [Diffusion] Attention backend fallback change introduced errors on most models
signals.text: ### Checklist - [x] I searched related issues but found no solution. - [x] The bug persists in the latest version. - [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback. - [x] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed. - [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed. ### Describe the bug Hi! Previously, if the desired attention backend was not part of any of the supported attention backends for the component, it defaulted to SDPA. PR #33707 changed the behavior so that it raises an error instead. Most text encoders (and some other components) have attention in them, but it's only supported via FAv3 or SDPA due to the input tensor dimensions. On ROCm, the default requested attention backend is AITER, so this now raises an error for pretty much all models. Most models don't outright crash entirely, they just revert to the diffusers version of the component instead of using the optimized sgl-d version, though MiniMax-H3 crashes fully (diffusers versions are not allowed). This is not limited to ROCm only - any desired backend that is not FA or SDPA will run into this issue (SageAttention, NPU etc). While it is possible to overcome this by adding `--component-attention-backends.text_encoder torch_sdpa`, this is not signaled to the user nor is it really that nice UX. I made this into a ticket instead of PR, as I'm not sure what's the best fix instead of just reverting it. It seems there's currently some attention backend related refactoring going on, maybe this is included in it. signals.title: [Bug] /v1/responses: `created_at` is a float in streaming events but an int in non-streaming responses
signals.text: ### Checklist - [x] I searched related issues but found no solution. - [x] The bug persists in the latest version. - [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback. - [x] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed. - [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed. ### Describe the bug The `/v1/responses` endpoint serializes `created_at` in two different wire formats depending on the request mode: - **Non-streaming** response body: `"created_at": 1786587534` (integer) - **Streaming** snapshot events (`response.created`, `response.in_progress`, `response.completed`): `"created_at": 1786588600.0` (float with a trailing `.0`) Root cause (from reading current `main`): - The non-streaming path serializes SGLang's own pydantic model, which types the field as an int: [`protocol.py` — `ResponsesResponse.created_at: int = Field(default_factory=lambda: int(time.time()))`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/openai/protocol.py) - The streaming path wraps the snapshot in the official `openai` SDK event types (`ResponseCreatedEvent` / `ResponseInProgressEvent` / `ResponseCompletedEvent`, see [`serving_responses.py`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/openai/serving_responses.py)). The SDK's [`Response.created_at` is typed `float`](https://github.com/openai/openai-python/blob/main/src/openai/types/responses/response.py), so pydantic coerces the int to a float and `event.model_dump_json()` emits `1786588600.0`. So the same field on the same endpoint has two formats, and neither matches the other. For reference, the real OpenAI API emits an integer here in both modes. Impact: downstream consumers that parse `created_at` strictly as an integer work fine against non-streaming responses, then fail to deserialize exactly the three streaming snapshot events. In our case (a Go API gateway in front of SGLang) the dropped `response.completed` event silently broke usage accounting for every streaming request. We have since made our parser tolerant, but the inconsistency inside SGLang remains a compatibility trap. Suggested fix: emit an integer consistently in the streaming path as well (e.g. normalize `created_at` when building/serializing the snapshot events, since the field type lives in the `openai` SDK and cannot be changed there). ### Reproduction **Minimal demonstration — no server or GPU needed.** The coercion happens entirely inside the pydantic models, so it can be shown with just the `openai` SDK (openai 2.48.0, pydantic 2.13.4): ```python from openai.types.responses import Response, ResponseCreatedEvent resp = Response( id="resp_123", created_at=1786588600, # int in error=None, incomplete_details=None, instructions=None, metadata=None, model="test", object="response", output=[], parallel_tool_calls=True, temperature=None, tool_choice="auto", tools=[], top_p=None, ) event = ResponseCreatedEvent(response=resp, sequence_number=0, type="response.created") print(type(event.response.created_at).__name__) # => float (coerced by the SDK's `created_at: float`) print(event.model_dump_json()) # => ... "created_at":1786588600.0 ... ``` This is exactly what the streaming path in `serving_responses.py` does (`event.model_dump_json()` on SDK event types), while the non-streaming path serializes SGLang's own `ResponsesResponse` with `created_at: int` — hence the two formats on the wire. **Against a live server** — any model reproduces it; nothing model-specific. ```bash python3 -m sglang.launch_server --model-path Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct --port 30000 ``` ```bash # Non-streaming: integer curl -s http://127.0.0.1:30000/v1/responses \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"model": "Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct", "input": "hi", "max_output_tokens": 16}' \ | grep -o '"created_at":[0-9.]*' # => "created_at":1786587534 # Streaming: float with trailing .0 in response.created / response.in_progress / response.completed curl -sN http://127.0.0.1:30000/v1/responses \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"model": "Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct", "input": "hi", "max_output_tokens": 16, "stream": true}' \ | grep -o '"created_at":[0-9.]*' | sort -u # => "created_at":1786588600.0 ``` ### Environment Apologies — I cannot provide `python3 -m sglang.check_env` output: the affected deployment is a managed GPUStack cluster (NVIDIA RTX Pro 6000D GPUs) serving DeepSeek-V4-Flash, and I have no shell access to the serving nodes. The bug should be environment-independent, though: it is a pure serialization/typing issue, root-caused above with source references to current `main`, and the float coercion is fully reproducible with the client-side snippet in the Reproduction section (run on macOS, Python 3.9, openai 2.48.0, pydantic 2.13.4 — output matches our production capture byte for byte).

signals.title: [Bug] DeepSeek-V4 sparse attention indexer (`fp8_paged_mqa_logits`) illegal memory access with long-context requests
signals.text: ### Checklist - [x] I searched related issues but found no solution. - [x] The bug persists in the latest version. - [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback. - [x] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed. - [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed. ### Describe the bug ## Summary Serving DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 on sglang 0.5.17 (8x H100, TP=8), the server reliably crashes with `CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS` inside the sparse attention indexer's `fp8_paged_mqa_logits` DeepGEMM kernel when a long-context request (roughly 80K–130K input tokens) reaches its first decode step. It looks related to #26427 and #21532, but those are filed under HiSparse specifically; this reproduces without it. All 8 TP ranks crash simultaneously with the identical traceback, and the bug is 100% reproducible by sending a single long-context request to a freshly started server — no concurrency needed. ## Investigation notes (ruling out other causes) We went through several false leads before isolating this, noting them here in case they're useful: - **Not speculative decoding**: reproduces with `--speculative-algorithm` entirely unset (no DSpark/EAGLE). - **Not CUDA graphs, structurally**: with CUDA graphs enabled (default), the crash is instead first detected inside `decode_cuda_graph_runner.py` → `full_cuda_graph_backend.py:129` (`self._graphs[shape_key].replay()`), and in other runs at essentially random subsequent CUDA API calls (`torch.cat`, `TensorImpl::~TensorImpl()` during a stream-capture-status check, `result.copy_done.synchronize()`), consistent with CUDA's async error reporting ("CUDA kernel errors might be asynchronously reported at some other API call"). This made it look like a CUDA-graph-replay or radix-cache bug. Only after combining `CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1` with `--disable-cuda-graph` did the traceback resolve to the true origin below — and the crash still occurs with `--disable-cuda-graph`, ruling out CUDA graphs as the root cause. ## Traceback (with `--disable-cuda-graph`) ``` File ".../sglang/srt/managers/scheduler.py", line 3594, in run_batch batch_result = self.model_worker.forward_batch_generation( File ".../sglang/srt/managers/tp_worker.py", line 593, in forward_batch_generation out = self.model_runner.forward( File ".../sglang/srt/model_executor/model_runner.py", line 1614, in _forward_raw ret = self.eager_runner.execute( File ".../sglang/srt/model_executor/runner/eager_runner.py", line 244, in _execute_decode return model_runner.model.forward( File ".../sglang/srt/models/deepseek_v4.py", line 2423, in forward hidden_states, prev_residual, prev_post, prev_comb = layer( File ".../sglang/srt/models/deepseek_v4.py", line 1698, in forward hidden_states = self.self_attn( File ".../sglang/srt/models/deepseek_v4.py", line 1241, in forward q, kv = self._forward_prepare( File ".../sglang/srt/models/deepseek_v4.py", line 1157, in _forward_prepare self.indexer( File ".../sglang/srt/layers/attention/dsv4/indexer.py", line 961, in forward return attn_backend.forward_c4_indexer( File ".../sglang/srt/layers/attention/dsv4/indexer.py", line 774, in forward_c4_indexer logits = fn( File ".../deep_gemm/__init__.py", line 207, in fp8_paged_mqa_logits return _C.fp8_paged_mqa_logits(q, kv_cache, weights, context_lens, block_table, schedule_meta, max_context_len, clean_logits, indices) File "python/tvm_ffi/cython/function.pxi", line 968, in tvm_ffi.core.Function.__call__ tvm.error.InternalError: CUDA driver error (/deepgemm/csrc/apis/../jit_kernels/impls/runtime_utils.hpp:144): 700 (CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS, an illegal memory access was encountered) ``` One of the 8 ranks instead surfaced a secondary/cascading symptom (the CUDA context on that rank was likely already poisoned by the same root fault before its next CUDA call): ``` File ".../sglang/srt/layers/attention/dsv4/indexer.py", line 679, in forward_c4_indexer q_indexer, weights = self._forward_prepare_normal( File ".../sglang/srt/layers/attention/dsv4/indexer.py", line 468, in _forward_prepare_normal weights = c4_indexer.compute_weights(x, skip_scale=True) File ".../sglang/srt/layers/attention/dsv4/indexer.py", line 946, in compute_weights out, _ = self.weights_proj(x) File ".../sglang/srt/layers/linear.py", line 282, in forward output = self.quant_method.apply(self, x, bias) File ".../sglang/srt/layers/quantization/unquant.py", line 255, in apply return F.linear(x, layer.weight, bias) RuntimeError: CUDA error: CUBLAS_STATUS_EXECUTION_FAILED when calling `cublasGemmEx(...)` ``` ## Expected behavior Long-context single requests (well within the configured `--context-length 262144`) should not crash the server via illegal memory access in the sparse attention indexer. ## Related issues - #26427 — DeepSeek-V4 HiSparse crashes/wedges with multiple long-context requests (same `fp8_paged_mqa_logits` / C4 indexer path, but filed with `--enable-hisparse` on; this report reproduces without it) - #21532 — CUDA illegal memory access when enabling HiSparse on disaggregated decode node with long prompts ### Reproduction ## Launch command ```bash sglang serve --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000 \ --model-path /path/to/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 \ --tp-size 8 --max-running-requests 256 \ --tool-call-parser deepseekv4 --reasoning-parser deepseek-v4 \ --mem-fraction-static 0.82 --moe-runner-backend marlin \ --model-loader-extra-config '{"enable_multithread_load": true, "num_threads": 16}' \ --chunked-prefill-size 8192 --context-length 262144 --allow-auto-truncate \ --served-model-name deepseek-v4-flash-0731 --trust-remote-code --log-level debug --enable-metrics ``` ### Environment - sglang: 0.5.17 - Model: DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 - Hardware: 8x H100, single node - `flashinfer` version: 0.6.15.post1 1. Start the server fresh (cold start). 2. Send a single request (concurrency = 1) with ~80K+ input tokens. 3. The server crashes on all 8 TP ranks as soon as the request transitions from prefill to its first decode step. Observed with real production traffic (a single ~130K-token request, first request after server startup).

signals.title: [Bug] [XPU] Qwen3.5 GDN + speculative decode: causal_conv1d_update_xpu() got an unexpected keyword argument 'intermediate_conv_window'
signals.text: ### Checklist - [x] I searched related issues but found no solution. - [x] The bug persists in the latest version. - [ ] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback. - [ ] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed. - [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed. ### Describe the bug On --device xpu, any speculative-decoding run on a hybrid GDN/linear-attention model (Qwen3.5) crashes in the target-verify path during the server's own warmup generation, before any user request. gdn_backend.py:43-48 binds the XPU kernel as-is: elif is_xpu(): from sgl_kernel import causal_conv1d_fn_xpu, causal_conv1d_update_xpu causal_conv1d_update = causal_conv1d_update_xpu but the is_target_verify branch at gdn_backend.py:539 calls it with five spec-only kwargs that the XPU op schema does not have — intermediate_conv_window, intermediate_state_indices, retrieve_next_token, retrieve_next_sibling, retrieve_parent_token. The XPU signature stops at conv_state_indices / pad_slot_id. File "python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/linear/gdn_backend.py", line 539, in forward_extend mixed_qkv_processed = causal_conv1d_update( TypeError: causal_conv1d_update_xpu() got an unexpected keyword argument 'intermediate_conv_window' The scheduler dies, and the client then reports a downstream ConnectionError (secondary noise). Non-spec decode on the same model/backend is unaffected — only TARGET_VERIFY takes this branch. The NPU and CPU bindings a few lines below (gdn_backend.py:49-60) are wired the same way and look exposed to the identical gap; unverified. Issue is induce #31250 fix. ### Reproduction With simple below steps able to reproduce issue ``` python -m sglang.benchmark.one_batch_server \ --model-path Qwen/Qwen3.5-9B --trust-remote-code \ --device xpu --tp-size 4 \ --mem-fraction-static 0.8 --disable-radix-cache --chunked-prefill-size -1 \ --max-total-tokens 8192 --max-prefill-tokens 4096 --max-running-requests 1 \ --batch-size 1 --input-len 512 --output-len 8 \ --speculative-algorithm NEXTN TypeError: causal_conv1d_update_xpu() got an unexpected keyword argument 'intermediate_conv_window' ``` Note : #34712 is required to reproduce the above error using shell command. ### Environment Intel Environment - sglang : 0.5.18.dev364+g667e18d99 torch : 2.12.0+xpu | cuda: None | hip: None | xpu: 20250302 python : 3.12.13 | Linux-6.14.0-37-generic-x86_64-with-glibc2.41 device : 8 x Intel(R) Arc(TM) Pro B60 Graphics driver : 1.14.36300+8 | mem GB: 22.7

signals.title: [Bug] SGLANG_SIMULATE_ACC_LEN silently degrades detokenization to O(n²) — `predict.fill_(100)` emits a byte-fallback token, and the `endswith("\ufffd")` commit gate then never advances the incremental-detokenization offsets
signals.text: ### Checklist - [x] I searched related issues but found no solution. - [ ] The bug persists in the latest version. - [ ] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback. - [ ] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed. - [ ] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed. ### Describe the bug Two independent defects that compose into one failure mode. **Defect A (benchmark path).** `generate_simulated_accept_index()` overwrites every accepted token id with the hardcoded constant `100`: ```python num_correct_drafts.fill_(simulate_acc_len - 1) predict.fill_(100) # some legit token id ``` The comment only establishes that `100` is *in range*; it does not establish that id `100` **decodes to a complete character**. In any byte-fallback vocabulary the low ids are single-byte tokens. On DeepSeek-V4-Pro (`len(tokenizer) == 129280`) ids **97–111 all decode to U+FFFD** (`�`), and `100` sits inside that range: ``` 90:'x' 91:'y' 92:'z' 93:'{' 94:'|' 95:'}' 96:'~' 97:'�' 98:'�' 99:'�' 100:'�' 101:'�' ... ``` So with `SGLANG_SIMULATE_ACC_LEN` enabled, the entire model output becomes a run of `�`. **Defect B (production path).** `DetokenizerManager` decides whether incremental detokenization may *commit* using a character-level heuristic: ```python new_text = read_texts[i][len(surr_texts[i]) :] if recv_obj.finished_reasons[i] is None: if new_text and not new_text.endswith("\ufffd"): s.append_decoded_text(new_text) s.surr_offset = s.read_offset # only place the left edge advances s.read_offset = len(s.decode_ids) ... else: printable = find_printable_text(new_text) # no commit; offsets frozen ``` `endswith("\ufffd")` is used as a proxy for "the trailing bytes form an incomplete character". These are **not** the same condition: U+FFFD is also a perfectly legal, complete character that a model can emit, or that can survive from the input. When the two are conflated, the commit gate can be held shut indefinitely. `surr_offset` is the *only* left edge from which a window may be decoded, because it marks the last position known to be a character boundary. Freezing it means the window `decode_ids[surr_offset:]` grows to cover the entire generated sequence, and — since `tokenizer.decode()` is a stateless API with no resumable decoder state — **every output step must re-decode the whole history from the beginning**. Per-request detokenization cost goes from O(n) to O(n²). **Composed effect.** Defect A manufactures exactly the input that trips Defect B: an output stream whose tail is `\ufffd` forever. The result is a single-process CPU bottleneck that back-pressures the whole engine. #### Impact measured Same server config (graph128 / `mem-fraction 0.92` / `max-running-requests 1024` / `tokenizer-worker-num 32` / EAGLE 3-4 / tp8 dp8 dp-attention), same client (concurrency 1024, 16384 requests, input 60000 / output 1000, `ignore_eos`), only `SGLANG_SIMULATE_ACC_LEN` and `--detokenizer-worker-num` varied: | acceptance | `detokenizer_worker_num` | client throughput (tok/s) | server throughput (tok/s) | running-req / rank | median TTFT | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | natural | 1 | 36,591 | 38,893 | 108.12 | 148.6 ms | | natural | 32 | 37,151 | 41,525 | 125.54 | 161.3 ms | | fixed 0.92 (`SIMULATE_ACC_LEN=3.76`) | 1 | 28,699 | 29,538 | **59.60** | **18,013.8 ms** | | fixed 0.92 (`SIMULATE_ACC_LEN=3.76`) | 32 | 39,264 | 43,917 | 126.42 | 154.5 ms | Reading: 1. Turning on the simulation switch costs **−21.6% client throughput** and inflates median TTFT **121×** (148.6 ms → 18.0 s), purely from detokenization. 1. Raising `--detokenizer-worker-num` to 32 recovers it entirely (+36.8% over the degraded run, and above the natural-acceptance baseline). On the natural side the same change is worth only +1.5%, i.e. the amplification is specific to the simulated path. 1. The engine is *starved*, not saturated: during the degraded run GPU was 96% busy, KV usage only 43%, and `num_prealloc_queue_reqs` / `num_transfer_queue_reqs` / `num_queue_reqs` were 0 throughout. Requests finish decoding on the GPU but their text cannot reach the client, so a closed-loop client never frees slots. 1. Client-visible symptom: **all 16,384 responses came back with `generated_text` empty** while `meta_info` reported 1000 generated tokens each, because `find_printable_text()` returns `""` for a run of `�` (no space to break on). The natural-acceptance run returned non-empty text for all 16,384 (median 998 chars). #### Why the cost is O(n²) With output length 1000 and accept length 3.76 there are ~266 output events per request. | | window decoded per event | times each output token is re-decoded | total token-decodes per request | |---|---:|---:|---:| | offsets advance (normal) | ~11 tokens (constant) | ~3 | ~2,900 | | offsets frozen (this bug) | 5 → 1,005 tokens | ~136 average, 266 for the first token | ~136,000 | `5×266 + 3.76×(266×267/2) ≈ 134,900` — the `1+2+…+n` term is the O(n²). The ratio is ≈45× at 1000 output tokens and **grows linearly with output length**. The same factor applies to the Python-side work per event: the `read_texts[i][len(surr_texts[i]):]` slice, the `rfind(" ")` inside `find_printable_text()`, and the `decode_ids[surr_offset:]` list copy all scale with the window. Secondary risk: `decode_status[rid].decode_ids` never stops growing, so detokenizer memory grows with output length, and entries evicted under `SGLANG_DETOKENIZER_MAX_STATES` pressure raise the `RuntimeError` at `detokenizer_manager.py:339-346`. ### Reproduction Environment: DeepSeek-V4-Pro, tp8 / dp8, `--enable-dp-attention`, EAGLE MTP (`--speculative-num-steps 3 --speculative-num-draft-tokens 4`), `--tokenizer-worker-num 32`, `--detokenizer-worker-num 1` (default). 1. Start the server with `SGLANG_SIMULATE_ACC_LEN=3.76` and `SGLANG_SIMULATE_ACC_METHOD=match-expected`. 1. Drive a closed-loop streaming load (input 60000, output 1000, `ignore_eos`, concurrency 1024) against `/generate`. 1. Observe: median TTFT in the tens of seconds, `#running-req` roughly half of the KV-permitted batch, `full token usage` well below 1.0, all queue depths 0, GPU busy — and every response's `text` empty. 1. Restart with `--detokenizer-worker-num 32`, change nothing else: throughput and TTFT return to the natural-acceptance level. Defect B can also be reproduced without the simulation switch, using the tokenizer alone — this mirrors the exact two-window arithmetic in `_decode_batch_token_id_output`: ```python from transformers import AutoTokenizer tk = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(MODEL) FFFD = "\ufffd" def commits(tid, rounds=4, per_round=4, tail=(100000, 20, 300, 4000, 50)): ids, surr, read = list(tail), 0, len(tail) for r in range(rounds): ids.extend([tid] * per_round) new = tk.decode(ids[surr:], skip_special_tokens=True)[ len(tk.decode(ids[surr:read], skip_special_tokens=True)):] if not (new and not new.endswith(FFFD)): return False, r + 1 # offsets frozen from here on surr, read = read, len(ids) return True, None commits(100) # -> (False, 1) byte-fallback token: never commits commits(67) # -> (True, None) 'a': commits every round ``` Full-vocabulary scan on DeepSeek-V4-Pro (129,280 ids, `skip_special_tokens=True`), classified by the commit gate's two requirements (non-empty and not ending in U+FFFD): | class | count | share | trips the bug? | |---|---:|---:|---| | decodes to a string ending in U+FFFD (byte-fallback) | 1,279 | 0.99% | yes — 0/100 sampled ids were safe | | decodes to `""` (special tokens skipped) | 1,230 | 0.95% | yes — `new_text` is falsy, same else-branch | | decodes to a complete visible character | 126,771 | 98.06% | no — 0/300 sampled ids were unsafe | ## Expected behavior 1. `SGLANG_SIMULATE_ACC_LEN` should change *how many* draft tokens are accepted, without changing the cost profile of the return path. Today it silently makes the measurement it exists to enable unreliable. 1. Incremental detokenization should keep its window bounded regardless of output content, so that a stream containing U+FFFD does not stall streaming or degrade to O(n²). ### Proposed fixes **Fix A — do not hardcode the simulated token id** (`python/sglang/srt/speculative/spec_utils.py:337`). A safe id is vocabulary-dependent (here `100` is a byte token while `67` is `'a'`; another tokenizer may invert that), so a constant cannot be correct in general. Derive it from the tokenizer, e.g. `tokenizer.encode("a", add_special_tokens=False)[0]`, or pick the first id whose single-token decode is non-empty and does not end in U+FFFD. **Fix B — test byte completeness, not the U+FFFD character** (`python/sglang/srt/managers/detokenizer_manager.py:354`). Compare bytes consumed versus bytes decoded, or use a tokenizer API that reports trailing incomplete bytes, instead of `new_text.endswith("\ufffd")`. This is the more important fix: it is reachable on production traffic whenever real output contains U+FFFD (in our natural-acceptance run, 17 of 16,384 responses contained it). **Fix C — bound the window defensively.** Even with Fix B, cap how far `surr_offset` may lag (a complete character cannot span more than a handful of tokens). Force-commit once the uncommitted tail exceeds that bound, so no input can drive this path quadratic. Note that `find_printable_text()` (`python/sglang/utils.py:369-385`, borrowed from HF `TextStreamer`) participates in the symptom: for a run of `�` with no space it returns `""`, so streaming clients receive empty chunks. In `TextStreamer` this heuristic only delays printing; using it behind a *commit* gate turns a display delay into unbounded state growth. ### Environment - sglang v0.5.14 (`SGLANG_BUILD_COMMIT=49e384ce9d304648e9959666ecb8ce8cd98d0deb`), torch 2.11.0+cu130, CUDA 13.0, NVIDIA driver 580.126.09 - Model: DeepSeek-V4-Pro, weights and KV cache `fp8_e4m3`, attention backend `dsv4`, MoE via MegaMoE - 8×GPU single node, tp8 / dp8 / ep8, `--enable-dp-attention`, PD-disaggregated decode node (`--disaggregation-mode decode --disaggregation-transfer-backend fake`) - `--tokenizer-worker-num 32`; `--detokenizer-worker-num` 1 (default) versus 32 ### Note on the mitigation and its precondition `--detokenizer-worker-num 32` fully absorbs the amplification, but it only works because request routing supplies enough distinct keys. `MultiDetokenizerRouter._pick()` shards on `zlib.crc32(recv_obj.http_worker_ipc) % num_workers` (`python/sglang/srt/managers/multi_tokenizer_mixin.py:500-501, 521, 540`) — the key is the owning **tokenizer** worker, not the request id. Effective parallelism is therefore capped by `--tokenizer-worker-num`; with `--tokenizer-worker-num 1`, every request hashes to the same detokenizer worker and `--detokenizer-worker-num 32` has no effect at all. This is worth documenting alongside the flag.

signals.title: [Feature] Router GEMM should keep fp32 output under deterministic inference (DeepSeek V3/V4)
signals.text: ### Checklist - [x] If this is not a feature request but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed. - [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed. ### Motivation The DeepSeek router GEMM should output fp32 under deterministic inference too. Today it falls back to bf16, and that is not needed for batch invariance. `python/sglang/srt/models/deepseek_v2.py:512`: ```python if get_exec().deterministic.enable_deterministic_inference: return F.linear(hidden_states, self.weight, None) # -> bf16 logits ``` Every other branch in the same function returns fp32: `dsv3_router_gemm(out_dtype=torch.float32)`, `linear_bf16_fp32`, and the prefill-CP path. **fp32 output does not break batch invariance.** Batch invariance is about reduction order, not output dtype. Deterministic `F.linear` runs `matmul_kernel_persistent`, which accumulates in fp32 and already has an fp32 store branch (`batch_invariant_ops.py:167`) that is never reached. It is the same kernel with the same reduction; only the final store differs. The branch is unreachable because `_matmul_persistent_triton` allocates output as the input dtype (`batch_invariant_ops.py:185`). Same for the JIT `dsv3_router_gemm` kernel, where `kOutFloat` only changes `cast<OutT>(final_sum)`. **Impact.** Router logits feed `noaux_tc` top-k over 256/384 experts with an fp32 correction bias. bf16 has 8 mantissa bits, so adjacent expert scores often sit within one ULP and rounding can change which experts are selected — a different answer, not a small numeric difference. **Related bug.** `_mm_dtype_compat` (`batch_invariant_ops.py:967`), registered for `aten::mm.dtype`, does `matmul_persistent(...).to(out_dtype)`, i.e. fp32 -> bf16 -> fp32. Callers asking for fp32 get bf16 values. ### Proposed change 1. Add `out_dtype` (or a preallocated `output`) to `matmul_persistent` / `_matmul_persistent_triton` so the existing fp32 store branch is reachable. Tiling and accumulation order are unchanged. 2. Use it in `_mm_dtype_compat` instead of `.to(out_dtype)`. 3. In `DeepseekV2MoEGate.forward`, request fp32 out from the batch-invariant matmul instead of returning bare `F.linear`. 4. Keep one kernel for all M under deterministic mode — the normal path switches kernels at `max_router_gemm_tokens` (4 on SM100/103, else 16), and a token-count-dependent switch is batch-variant on its own. 5. `_matmul_persistent_deepgemm` allocates `out` as `a.dtype` for `deep_gemm.bf16_gemm_nn`; either find an fp32-out entry point or route fp32 requests to Triton. Cost should be negligible — the GEMM is `[M, 7168] x [7168, 256]` and this only changes the store dtype. ### Related resources - `python/sglang/srt/models/deepseek_v2.py:512` - `python/sglang/srt/batch_invariant_ops/batch_invariant_ops.py:167,185,275,967` - `python/sglang/kernels/jit/csrc/gemm/dsv3_router_gemm.cuh` — `kOutFloat` - #12095 — added the `F.linear` fallback

signals.title: [Bug] macOS: shared-memory names can exceed the 31-char POSIX limit, deadlocking `in_the_same_node_as` with no error output
signals.text: ### Checklist - [x] I searched related issues but found no solution. - [x] The bug persists in the latest version. - [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback. - [x] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed. - [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed. ### Describe the bug ## Summary On macOS, `make_shm_name()` can produce a name longer than the platform's POSIX shared-memory limit. When that happens inside `in_the_same_node_as()`, the resulting `OSError` is swallowed by a `contextlib.suppress(OSError)` that also wraps a **collective operation** — so rank 0 skips its `broadcast_object_list` while the other ranks block on theirs. The process group deadlocks permanently with **no exception, no log line, and no timeout**. This is not a single mistyped name: `make_shm_name()` has no length budget and no validation, so the limit is silently 7 characters of `kind` on macOS. Two of the three current call sites happen to fit; the third does not. ## Impact - Any future `make_shm_name("<kind longer than 7 chars>")` will reintroduce the same silent hang, on any call site — including on paths that *are* covered. - Any macOS run with `world_size > 1` hangs at startup, indefinitely and silently. - The path is outside current CI coverage. The macOS lane (`.github/workflows/pr-test-mlx.yml`, `runs-on: macos-26`) does run real end-to-end server launches in `stage-b-e2e-mlx`, but all three MLX e2e tests pin `--tp-size 1`, and no test in the repo starts a `world_size > 1` process group on macOS. On Linux the shm name limit is 255 characters, so the same code path cannot fail there either — the bug is reachable only in a configuration nothing currently exercises. I hit this via the MLX backend with `--tp 2`. Note that this is not an unreasonable thing for a user to try: MLX itself documents tensor parallelism across machines, with JACCL described as "necessary for things like tensor parallelism" (https://ml-explore.github.io/mlx/build/html/usage/distributed.html). ### Reproduction ```bash SGLANG_USE_MLX=1 python -m sglang.launch_server \ --model Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B --disable-cuda-graph --host 0.0.0.0 --tp 2 ``` Last output before the hang: ``` [TP0] Init torch distributed begin. [TP1] Init torch distributed begin. [TP0] Setup Custom allreduce failed with . [TP1] Setup Custom allreduce failed with . <hangs forever; both processes at 0.0% CPU> ``` ## Stacks `py-spy dump` on TP0 (requires `sudo` on macOS): ``` barrier (torch/distributed/distributed_c10d.py:5037) in_the_same_node_as (distributed/parallel_state.py:2900) create_from_process_group (shm_broadcast.py:495) __init__ (distributed/parallel_state.py:514) init_model_parallel_group (distributed/parallel_state.py:1835) initialize_model_parallel (distributed/parallel_state.py:2289) _init_parallel_groups (distributed/bootstrap.py:222) init_torch_distributed (distributed/bootstrap.py:82) ... ``` `py-spy dump` on TP1 times out (`os error 60`) — consistent with it being blocked in `broadcast_object_list` rather than at the later barrier. The asymmetry is the tell: **TP0 is already past the broadcast and waiting at the barrier, while TP1 never got past the broadcast.** ## Root cause `make_shm_name()` builds: ```python f"{_SGL_SHM_PREFIX}_{kind}_{os.getpid()}_{uuid.uuid4().hex[:8]}" # sgl_shm(7) + _ + kind + _ + pid + _ + hex8(8) = 18 + len(kind) + len(pid) ``` CPython prepends `/` on POSIX before calling `shm_open()` (`multiprocessing/shared_memory.py`, `_prepend_leading_slash = True if _USE_POSIX`, and `name = "/" + name` in `__init__`), so the kernel sees one more character than the caller passed. Measured limit on macOS (Python 3.12.13, arm64): ```python >>> shared_memory.SharedMemory(create=True, size=128, name="0"*30) # ok (31 with slash) >>> shared_memory.SharedMemory(create=True, size=128, name="0"*31) OSError: [Errno 63] File name too long: '/0000000000000000000000000000000' ``` So the usable budget is **30 characters**, i.e. `len(kind) + len(pid) <= 12`. With a 5-digit pid, `kind` may be at most **7** characters: | call site | `kind` | len | total | status | |---|---|---|---|---| | `mm_utils.py` | `"mm"` | 2 | 25 | ok (5 spare) | | `shm_broadcast.py` | `"mq"` | 2 | 25 | ok (5 spare) | | `parallel_state.py` | `"nodecheck"` | **9** | **32** | **over by 2** | ## Why it deadlocks instead of erroring `in_the_same_node_as()`: ```python with contextlib.suppress(OSError): if rank == source_rank: shm = shared_memory.SharedMemory(create=True, size=128, name=make_shm_name("nodecheck")) # <-- raises here shm.buf[:len(magic_message)] = magic_message torch.distributed.broadcast_object_list([shm.name], src=..., group=pg) # <-- collective, skipped ... else: torch.distributed.broadcast_object_list(recv, src=..., group=pg) # <-- collective, blocks ... except Exception as e: logger.error("Error ignored in is_in_the_same_node: %s", e) # <-- never reached for OSError ``` Two problems compound: 1. **`contextlib.suppress` aborts the entire `with` body**, not just the failing statement — so the collective inside it is skipped on the failing rank only. A collective that one rank skips is an unconditional deadlock. 2. The inner `suppress(OSError)` shadows the outer `except Exception -> logger.error`, so the error is never logged. That is why the hang produces zero diagnostic output. The intent of the suppression is clearly reasonable — treat this as a best-effort probe and degrade gracefully when shared memory is unavailable. The problem is only its **scope**: it covers the collectives too. 1. **Shorten the `kind` at the call site** (`"nodecheck"` -> `"ndchk"`). Smallest possible change, zero risk. Fixes this instance only; the next long `kind` reintroduces it. 2. **Give `make_shm_name()` a length budget** — truncate `kind`, or shorten the `sgl_shm_` prefix / the 8-char random suffix, and assert the result fits. Fixes the class. Touches name generation, so `cleanup_stale_shm`'s parsing (`sgl_shm_<kind>_<pid>_<rand>`) must stay compatible. 3. **Narrow the `suppress` so every rank always reaches the collective** — on failure, rank 0 broadcasts `None` and all ranks fall back to "not same node". This is the only option that fixes the deadlock *shape* rather than this one trigger, and it protects every platform, not just macOS. It is also the largest change and touches a path that runs on all backends. (1) and (3) are orthogonal and could both apply: (1)/(2) removes the trigger, (3) removes the failure mode. ## What I'd like to know Which layer do you want the fix at — the call site, `make_shm_name()`, or the `suppress` scope? I have no strong opinion; (2) and (3) both look defensible to me and (3) is the one I'd be least comfortable proposing unilaterally. ## Out of scope for this issue Fixing the name length does **not** make `--tp 2` work on the MLX backend — it only replaces the silent hang with whatever comes next. No parallelism parameters reach `MlxModelRunner`, and each rank independently sizes its KV pool against the same unified memory. I'll file that separately so this one stays a single decision. I'd like to take this one. Once you pick a direction I can have a PR up within a day, with a regression test — a length assertion on `make_shm_name()` is cheap and platform-agnostic, while a test that actually exercises a `world_size > 1` group on macOS would need the MLX lane. ### Environment Python: 3.12.13 (main, Jun 23 2026, 15:44:24) [Clang 22.1.3 ] MPS available: True macOS Version: 26.5.2 macOS Build: 25F84 Apple Silicon: Apple M5 Unified Memory: 16.0 GB CPU Cores (Total): 10 CPU Cores (Performance): 4 CPU Cores (Efficiency): 6 Metal Support: Metal 4 GPU Cores: 8 PyTorch: 2.11.0 sglang: 0.5.17 sglang-kernel: 0.4.5 flashinfer_python: Module Not Found flashinfer_cubin: Module Not Found flashinfer_jit_cache: Module Not Found triton: Module Not Found transformers: 5.12.1 torchao: 0.9.0 numpy: 2.3.5 aiohttp: 3.14.3 fastapi: 0.141.1 huggingface_hub: 1.27.0 interegular: 0.3.3 modelscope: 1.39.1 orjson: 3.11.9 outlines: 0.1.11 packaging: 26.3 psutil: 7.2.2 pydantic: 2.13.4 python-multipart: 0.0.32 pyzmq: 27.1.0 uvicorn: 0.52.1 uvloop: 0.22.1 vllm: Module Not Found xgrammar: 0.2.1 openai: 2.6.1 tiktoken: 0.13.0 anthropic: 0.121.0 litellm: Module Not Found torchcodec: Module Not Found mlx: 0.32.0 mlx-lm: 0.31.3 mlx-metal: 0.32.0 ulimit soft: 1048575
