signals.title: [Feature] Realtime ASR: encoder-aligned windowing for long audio items
signals.text:
## Summary This PR follows the realtime-ASR profiling work in RFC #22474 with an experimental long-item path for `/v1/realtime`. It goes beyond the RFC's original low-risk M2 boundary by adding encoder-window reuse and decoder-suffix continuation. M1, the WebSocket transport, landed in #22848. Before this PR, every 2 s audio append re-ran ASR on all PCM received for the current item. Per-request work therefore grows with item length, and total work grows roughly quadratically. For adapters that opt in, this PR adds a windowed path after a model-specific activation gate: - split audio into model-aligned complete encoder windows plus a mutable tail; - reuse complete-window encoder outputs through SGLang's existing multimodal embedding cache; - keep a bounded amount of recent acoustic context; - pass recent emitted text back as a bounded decoder prefix and decode only the new suffix; - compact PCM only after an accepted windowed result. Qwen3-ASR keeps cumulative inference through 60 s. The windowed path is operator opt-in through `--asr-long-audio-strategy encoder_window`; the item cap must also be raised above its 60 s default. Short and mid-length items therefore keep the existing behavior even when the strategy is enabled. The current windowed policy is intentionally narrow: it is experimental, Qwen3-ASR-specific, local single-GPU only, and activates only when the client explicitly configures English (`language="en"`). Other languages and unsupported runtime topologies keep cumulative inference with the effective item cap limited to the 60 s activation gate. This PR does **not** implement M3 token-level generation. Each ASR backend request still uses `stream=False`; the realtime endpoint publishes a delta after that request completes. Token-level streaming within a 2 s inference step remains future work. ### Qwen3-ASR defaults | Setting | Value | Purpose | |---|---:|---| | Inference cadence | 2 s | Existing chunked-ASR update interval | | Windowed activation gate | 60 s | Keep normal turns cumulative | | Encoder window | 8 s / 104 encoder tokens | Resolved from the model processor | | Retained acoustic context | 8 windows / 64 s | Accuracy-first result of the context sweep | | Decoder prefix | 192 tokens | Carries recent text context for discarded audio | | Suffix holdback | 1 word | Avoid committing an unstable trailing word | Terms used below: - **chunk**: the fixed audio step that triggers a realtime inference; Qwen3-ASR uses 2 s. - **cumulative path**: re-send all audio received for the current item and reconcile a cumulative transcript hypothesis. - **windowed path**: send encoder-aligned rolling audio context plus a bounded decoder prefix. - **complete window**: one full encoder-aligned span. For Qwen3-ASR-0.6B this is 8 s and maps to 104 encoder tokens. - **mutable tail**: the incomplete final window. It changes after each append, so it is always re-encoded and never inserted into the embedding cache. - **decoder prefix**: recently emitted transcript text added to the prompt so the model generates a continuation instead of repeating the whole transcript. - **delta**: incremental text published to the realtime client. - **attempted audio**: audio covered by an inference request, including a result that was intentionally deferred. - **accepted audio**: audio whose inference result was committed to transcript state and can therefore participate in PCM compaction. ## Motivation In the cumulative path, request `n` contains all audio from requests `1..n`. The growing audio is represented as one multimodal item, so its hash changes on every append and the existing MM embedding cache cannot reuse its encoder output. The transcript also follows the audio in the prompt, so normal token-prefix reuse does not solve the repeated encoder work. Qwen3-ASR's processor exposes block-aligned 8 s encoder geometry. Representing each complete block as an independent multimodal item gives stable cache identities across requests. The incomplete tail remains mutable and is always encoded normally. ## Design ### Capability split Windowing policy and encoder geometry come from different layers: ```mermaid flowchart LR A["Transcription adapter
gate, context windows,
prefix and holdback"] --> R["RealtimeASRProcessor"] P["Model processor
window frames and alignment"] --> B["BaseMultimodalProcessor
generic audio-window builder"] R --> B B --> I["Independent complete-window items
plus one uncached mutable tail"] I --> C["Existing MM embedding cache"] ``` The adapter decides when long-audio continuation is allowed. A compatible multimodal processor declares only its encoder-window geometry; the base processor performs feature extraction, placeholder expansion, item creation, and cacheability decisions. Models without both capabilities remain cumulative. ### Request lifecycle ```mermaid flowchart TB A["Append PCM audio or commit"] --> B{"Inference required?"} B -- "No" --> H["Keep buffering or flush held text"] B -- "Yes" --> D["Drain one fixed 2 s step"] D --> M{"Window strategy enabled,
model capable, and past gate?"} M -- "No" --> C["Cumulative step
all accumulated audio + committed text"] M -- "Yes" --> W["Windowed step
aligned windows + mutable tail + bounded prefix"] C --> G["Stateless ASR request"] W --> G G -- "finish_reason=length" --> X["Fail the item as truncated"] G -- "stop" --> R["Reconcile transcript"] R -- "First windowed result is unsupported CJK" --> C R --> Q{"Usable outcome?"} Q -- "First empty non-final
window continuation" --> K["Advance attempted cursor only
keep audio for one retry"] Q -- "Yes" --> P["Advance attempted and processed cursors
compact accepted windowed PCM"] P --> O["Emit transcript delta, if any"] ``` A client may send more than one chunk in a single append. The session drains it through the same 2 s inference cadence, and each non-final step caps its end at `last_attempted + chunk_size`; a 90 s append therefore cannot become one 90 s model request. `input_audio_buffer.commit` runs one final step when unprocessed audio remains. Otherwise it flushes held transcript text, emits the completed event, and resets the item. ### Windowed request The first request past the gate includes all accumulated audio and establishes the decoder-suffix state. Later requests retain at most eight complete windows plus the mutable tail: ```text steady-state absolute audio timeline (8 s windows) |<-- discarded -->|<------------- request N sends ------------->| +----+----+----+ +----+----+----+----+----+----+----+----+ +------+ | w0 | w1 | w2 | | w3 | w4 | w5 | w6 | w7 | w8 | w9 |w10 | | tail | +----+----+----+ +----+----+----+----+----+----+----+----+ +------+ complete windows are cacheable ^ retained entries reuse encoder output | evicted entries safely re-encode | mutable tail changes on every append and is never cached recent emitted transcript -> bounded decoder prefix provides text context for audio that is no longer present in the request ``` There is no timestamp or audio-to-text alignment in this path. The decoder prefix is a recent text context, not a claim that particular words belong to specific windows. ### Encoder-output reuse ```mermaid flowchart LR W["Complete audio windows"] --> F["Extract as a separate feature batch"] F --> H["Hash feature + mask + modality + placeholder span"] H --> C{"Embedding cache"} C -- "Hit" --> R["Reuse encoder output"] C -- "Miss or eviction" --> E["Encode window"] --> S["Insert cache entry"] T["Mutable tail"] --> TF["Extract separately"] --> X["Encode without caching"] ``` The cache remains best effort. A complete window can be encoded again after eviction or restart, so correctness does not depend on a hit. The mutable tail uses `use_embedding_cache=False`, so one-use entries do not evict reusable complete windows. Complete windows and the mutable tail are feature-extracted separately. This is required for Whisper-style frontends, which pad waveforms before STFT: batching a tiny tail with complete windows can otherwise change a complete window's final mel frame and therefore its cache identity. A tail shorter than `n_fft` is kept with the preceding window; that combined mutable item is uncached. A standalone short tail is padded only enough for the feature extractor. ### Scheduler integration The window items opt into two per-item scheduling controls. The shared per-image scheduler was mechanically split into collection, cache-resolution, and miss-encoding phases so those controls can be applied without a parallel ASR-only scheduling pipeline: ```mermaid flowchart TB R["Chunked multimodal request"] --> S{"All items have one offset?"} S -- "No" --> F["Existing full / EVS path
policy items rejected"] S -- "Yes" --> C["Collect overlapping items
and merge duplicate hashes"] C --> H["Resolve eligible embedding-cache hits"] H --> G["Group misses by encoder_batch_key"] G -- "None" --> D["Default group
one encoder call, normal caching"] G -- "Producer key" --> P["Compatible window group
tail bypasses cache"] D --> E["Encode misses"] P --> E E --> O["Clone cached multi-item splits when required"] O --> A["Assemble chunks in request order"] ``` Items with the default `use_embedding_cache=True` and `encoder_batch_key=None` retain the previous behavior: their misses remain in one encoder group and use the embedding cache normally. Encoder-window items set a producer batch key, while the mutable tail additionally sets `use_embedding_cache=False`. Multi-offset policy items are rejected rather than silently entering the full path. The existing full/EVS path and the default HIP/NPU per-item path are otherwise unchanged. These fields are internal `MultimodalDataItem` metadata with backward-compatible defaults. They use the existing tokenizer-manager-to-scheduler item transport and are not part of the public request schema. Default items do not opt into a new batch group or bypass the embedding cache. ### Transcript continuation Windowed requests use the adapter prompt plus a bounded prefix of recently emitted text. The decoder returns a continuation rather than retranscribing all earlier text. Reconciliation is keep-biased: - one agreed trailing word remains pending until the next result; - the first empty non-final continuation with new audio defers once so the next request re-covers it; a second empty result is accepted so context cannot grow without bound; - `finish_reason=length` fails closed in both cumulative and windowed modes instead of publishing a truncated completed transcript; - an exact replay of the short decoder prefix is trimmed at the one-way cumulative-to-windowed handoff; - no fuzzy phrase deletion is used; - no-whitespace CJK stays cumulative because word-based suffix reconciliation is not safe for it. If the first windowed result reveals unsupported no-whitespace CJK, no transcript state has been committed yet, so the same audio is retried cumulatively. ### PCM accounting and compaction The realtime buffer uses absolute byte offsets: - `last_attempted_offset_bytes` advances after every inference attempt so a deferred result cannot cause a busy loop; - `last_processed_offset_bytes` advances only when the result enters transcript state; - after an accepted non-final windowed step, PCM before the next rolling range is discarded. A deferred or failed inference does not advance the accepted cursor and does not compact PCM, so its audio remains available for retry. ### ASR embedding-cache identity Whisper-style feature extractors can zero-pad different audio inputs to byte-identical mel tensors while producing different encoder-token counts. A feature-only cache key can therefore return an embedding with the wrong length. On main this reproduces as: ```text RuntimeError: Insufficient multimodal embedding length: num_mm_tokens_in_input_ids=26 vs num_mm_tokens_in_embedding=0 ``` The fix is scoped to ASR inputs. Cumulative realtime and HTTP streaming requests provide a raw-audio `mm_hash`, so different valid audio lengths cannot alias only because their padded mel values match. Encoder-window items use `hash_mm_item`, which binds feature content, modality, and placeholder-token geometry into their cache identity. Unrelated multimodal requests retain their existing automatic hash behavior. ## Implementation Key files under `python/sglang/srt/`: | File | Status | Role | |---|---|---| | `entrypoints/openai/realtime/asr_processor.py` | New | Connection-scoped application service outside the WebSocket transport. `process()` builds a `_TranscriptionStep`, executes it through `_execute_step()`, reconciles cumulative or decoder-suffix text without mutating audio cursors, and applies `_TranscriptionOutcome` in `_commit_outcome()`. | | `entrypoints/openai/realtime/audio_buffer.py` | New | PCM store addressed by absolute item offsets. `snapshot()` remains correct after `discard_before()` compacts the resident prefix. Attempted and processed cursors encode retry/compaction safety. | | `entrypoints/openai/realtime/session.py` | Modified | Handles protocol events, patch-style `session.update`, append/commit/clear lifecycle, buffer limits, and publishing. It drains batched appends through fixed-size inference steps and delegates ASR state transitions to `RealtimeASRProcessor`. | | `entrypoints/openai/realtime/decoder_suffix.py` | New | Owns windowed continuation state: bounded decoder prefixes, exact prefix-echo trimming, one-word holdback, suffix reconciliation, and final flush. | | `entrypoints/openai/streaming_asr.py` | Modified | Retains the cumulative word/CJK reconciliation path and shared stateless ASR generation helpers. Windowed suffix state is kept separate in `decoder_suffix.py`. | | `entrypoints/openai/transcription_adapters/base.py` | Modified | Declares the optional typed `realtime_encoder_window_policy` capability. No policy keeps existing adapters cumulative. | | `entrypoints/openai/transcription_adapters/qwen3_asr.py` | Modified | Supplies Qwen3-ASR's 60 s gate, eight-window acoustic context, 192-token text prefix, and one-word holdback. Window geometry itself is not duplicated here. | | `multimodal/audio_encoder_windowing.py` | New | Model-neutral builder that resolves encoder geometry, extracts stable complete-window features separately from the mutable tail, expands the placeholder run, and creates one `MultimodalDataItem` per window. | | `multimodal/processors/base_processor.py` | Modified | Owns the generic window feature-extraction/item-building path and preserves the processor's normal `audio_config`. Window preparation is entered only with an explicit resolved capability; errors fail the request instead of silently changing strategy. | | `multimodal/processors/qwen3_asr.py` | Modified | Declares only `window_frames` and `alignment_frames` from `thinker_config.audio_config`; the base processor performs window construction. | | `managers/mm_schedule.py` | Modified | Refactors the shared per-image miss path into collection, cache-resolution, and encoding phases, then threads two opt-in item controls through those phases. Default items retain one encoder group and normal cache behavior; window items group by producer batch key, bypass tail cache reads/writes, and clone cacheable multi-item tensor splits when needed. The full/EVS path remains unchanged. | | `managers/mm_utils.py` | Modified | Adds `hash_mm_item`, which combines feature identity, modality, and placeholder-token geometry. | | `managers/schedule_batch.py` | Modified | Carries `use_embedding_cache` and `encoder_batch_key` with each multimodal item and preserves processor-supplied hashes. | | `managers/tokenizer_manager.py` | Modified | Threads internal multimodal processor arguments from the realtime request to the model processor. | | `server_args.py` | Modified | Adds the explicit `--asr-long-audio-strategy encoder_window` opt-in and clarifies that `--asr-max-buffer-seconds` is a total per-item duration limit. Both the strategy and a cap above the adapter gate are required. | | `utils/common.py` | Modified | Lets the multimodal loader accept the realtime path's decoded NumPy audio directly, avoiding an extra PCM/WAV round trip. | | `test/registered/...` | New/modified | Focused tests cover cumulative/windowed state transitions, fixed-step large appends, handoff echo, partial session updates, compaction, real-frontend tiny-tail stability, processor-config forwarding, item hashing, and policy-path cache behavior. | ## Validation ### Method - Model: `Qwen/Qwen3-ASR-0.6B` - Hardware: one RTX 4090 - Audio: original 16 kHz mono PCM16 recordings, not synthesized text fixtures - Realtime cadence: 2 s WebSocket `input_audio_buffer.append` frames followed by `input_audio_buffer.commit` - Baseline: merge-base main at `990a446773` - Latest full GPU rerun: the round-4 working tree captured as `fe2b3a4ecb592fe4b4c090ccf6d22ccceb6eb81a` plus working-tree changes, subsequently organized into `760a5663e0` - Matrix: 29 scenarios across HTTP JSON, HTTP SSE, and WebSocket realtime (87 planned request cells per build) - Scaling runs: append frames were sent in flood mode, without realtime sleeps, to measure server throughput and per-request response time Main completed 70 matrix cells before the padded-mel cache collision above terminated its scheduler during `paused_en_4s` HTTP SSE. The latest PR rerun completed 86 of 87 request cells and both same-session lifecycle scenarios. The only failed cell was WebSocket `repeat_zh_70s`, a pathological repeated no-whitespace Chinese input: its decode reached `max_new_tokens`, so the endpoint returned `inference_failed` instead of publishing a truncated completed item. The corresponding HTTP JSON/SSE requests followed their existing non-realtime path and returned capped text. Of the 70 successful main cells, 66 were byte-identical and 67 were word-for-word equal after punctuation normalization. The remaining differences were bounded model variation on repeated or cut-at-boundary inputs; no successful comparable cell had a scrambled or truncated tail. The full round-4 GPU rerun was performed after the shared scheduler refactor. It covered all 29 scenarios, both lifecycle cases, and four one-item TED talks from 187 s through 1105 s. A later cleanup restored main's first-occurrence behavior for duplicate legacy hashes without changing the encoder-window policy; a focused 90 s WebSocket run on that cleanup completed with 299 deltas and no error. The reduced scheduler unit suite passes 10 focused tests, including both legacy split-storage behavior and opt-in window cache ownership. The final review-fix working tree also reran the exact 20 s cumulative case and the 77.9 s paused-English windowed case on the GPU. Both completed with full tails and no boundary duplication. A proposed change that preserved provisional pending text alongside a disagreeing final decode was rejected after E2E testing showed it duplicated the final phrase; the final decode continues to supersede unconfirmed pending text. Public audio sources: - Qwen3-ASR demo: [English](https://qianwen-res.oss-cn-beijing.aliyuncs.com/Qwen3-ASR-Repo/asr_en.wav) and [Chinese](https://qianwen-res.oss-cn-beijing.aliyuncs.com/Qwen3-ASR-Repo/asr_zh.wav) - [Narsil/asr_dummy](https://huggingface.co/datasets/Narsil/asr_dummy): [MLK](https://huggingface.co/datasets/Narsil/asr_dummy/resolve/main/mlk.flac), [LibriSpeech](https://huggingface.co/datasets/Narsil/asr_dummy/resolve/main/1.flac), [Spanish](https://huggingface.co/datasets/Narsil/asr_dummy/resolve/main/4.flac), [Hindi](https://huggingface.co/datasets/Narsil/asr_dummy/resolve/main/hindi.ogg), and [MP3-decode](https://huggingface.co/datasets/Narsil/asr_dummy/resolve/main/i-know-kung-fu.mp3) - [distil-whisper/tedlium-long-form](https://huggingface.co/datasets/distil-whisper/tedlium-long-form): real 3-18 minute TED talks from the validation split. Brian Cox, 187 s - full output of the single realtime item Last year at TED, I gave an introduction to the LHC, and I promised to come back and give you an update on how that machine worked. So this is it. For those of you that weren't there, the LHC is the largest scientific experiment ever attempted—27 kilometers in circumference. Its job is to recreate the conditions that were present less than a billionth of a second after the universe began, up to 600 million times a second. So nothing you've not ambitious. This is the machine below Geneva. We take the pictures of those mini-bangs inside detectors. This is the one I work on. It's called the Atlas detector—44 meters wide, 22 meters in diameter. Spectacular picture here of Atlas under construction. So you can see the scale. On the 10th of September last year, we turned the machine on for the first time, and this picture was taken by Atlas. It caused immense celebration in the control room. It's a picture of the first beam particle going all the way around the LHC, colliding with a piece of the LHC deliberately and showering particles into the detector. In other words, when we saw that picture on September 10th, we knew the machine worked, which is a great triumph. I don't know whether this got the biggest cheer or this when someone went on to Google and saw the front page was like that. It means we made cultural impact as well as scientific impact. About a week later, we had a problem with the machine, related actually to these bits of wire here, these gold wires. Those wires carry 13,000 amps when the machine is working at full power. Now the engineers among you will look at them and say, no, they don't. They small wires. They can do that because when they're very cold, they what's called superconducting wire. So at minus 271 degrees colder than the space between the stars, those wires can take that current. In one of the joints between over 9,000 magnets in LHC, there was a manufacturing defect, so the wire heated up slightly, and its 13,000 amps suddenly encountered electrical resistance. This was the result. Now that's more impressive when you consider those magnets weigh over 20 tons and they moved about a foot. So we damaged about 50 of the magnets. We had to take them out, which we did. We've reconditioned them all, fixed them. They're all on their way back underground now. By the end of March, the LHC will be intact again. We will switch it on and we expect to take data in June or July. And continue with our quest to find out what the building blocks of the universe are. Now of course in a way those accidents reignite the debate about the value of science and engineering at the edge. It's easy to refute. I think that the fact that it's so difficult, the fact that we're overreaching is the value of things like the LHC. I will leave the final word to an English scientist Humphrey Davy who I suspect when defending his Protais useless experiments. His Protais was Michael Faraday said said this: Nothing is so dangerous to the progress of the human mind than to assume that our views of science are ultimate, that there are no mysteries in nature, that our triumphs are complete, and yet there are no new worlds to conquer.

### Inference cost vs item length `Inference time` is model-inference time summed across the item's requests. `PR per-chunk response p95` is the 95th percentile from sending one 2 s append to receiving its delta on the current PR. Below the gate both builds use the same cumulative policy, so their small differences are run-to-run noise and are not claimed as a speedup. For 15-90 s, the table reports the median of two compiled, cache-flushed runs; the range is shown in parentheses. Each build was warmed with a different real 90 s recording before measurement. A first main 90 s pass that spent 149 s in new-shape compilation is excluded from the steady-state comparison. | Item audio | Main inference time | Current PR inference time | PR per-chunk response p95 | Result | |---:|---:|---:|---:|---| | 15 s | 1.24 s (0.87-1.62) | 0.81 s (0.80-0.82) | 0.14 s | Same cumulative policy | | 30 s | 1.67 s (1.40-1.93) | 1.43 s (1.35-1.52) | 0.16 s | Same cumulative policy | | 45 s | 2.17 s (1.96-2.38) | 2.21 s (2.02-2.40) | 0.15 s | Same cumulative policy | | 60 s | 2.87 s (2.62-3.11) | 2.84 s (2.56-3.11) | 0.15 s | Gate has not opened | | 90 s | 9.50 s (7.78-11.23) | 4.49 s (4.22-4.76) | 0.17 s | Windowed; median inference time -52.7% | | 300 s | Prior run DNF | 15.63 s | 0.16 s | Main previously stopped after 5 min at about 70 s of input | | 900 s | Not run | 45.33 s | 0.16 s | Windowed | | 1105 s | Not run | 53.12 s | 0.16 s | Windowed | At 90 s, median uncached prefill fell from 33,680 tokens on main to 21,923 on this PR (-34.9%). Median flood wall time fell from 10.90 s to 5.86 s (-46.2%). The 300/900/1105 s PR items completed in 20.55/60.17/71.95 s end to end in flood mode, including transport. Through the tested 1105 s item, per-chunk response p95 remained about 0.16 s after the windowed path reached steady state. After the fixed-step append and stable tiny-tail fixes, a fresh rerun measured 4.466 s model time and 5.878 s wall time at 90 s, and 15.767 s model time and 20.266 s wall time at 300 s. These remain within the earlier windowed ranges. A separate 90 s single-append request completed in 5.837 s and produced the same normalized transcript as 45 individual 2 s appends. Internally it still executed 45 cadence steps and kept the steady-state acoustic request at the configured 64 s context bound. ### Resident PCM Below the gate both paths retain the same uncommitted buffer. Once windowed mode is active, the endpoint retains roughly the rolling 64 s context plus the mutable tail: | Item length | Main resident PCM | Current PR resident PCM | Reduction | |---:|---:|---:|---:| | <=60 s | <=1.83 MiB | <=1.83 MiB | 1.0x | | 120 s | 3.66 MiB | about 2.2 MiB | 1.7x | | 300 s | 9.16 MiB | about 2.2 MiB | 4.2x | | 600 s | 18.31 MiB | about 2.2 MiB | 8.3x | | 900 s | 27.47 MiB | about 2.2 MiB | 12.5x | ### Repeated-audio HTTP SSE behavior Highly repetitive audio exposes a separate, pre-existing issue in the HTTP SSE cumulative path. On the latest 119 s repeated clip, the expected transcript has 147 words. Current HTTP JSON and windowed WebSocket each emitted 147 words, while current HTTP SSE emitted 2,801. A separate main run also emitted 2,801 words over HTTP SSE; its cumulative WebSocket path emitted 3,998. HTTP chunked transcription still submits cumulative audio and reconciles cumulative text, so this result is not attributed to encoder windowing. The over-production remains a known limitation rather than a performance or quality claim for this PR.
Configuration sweeps behind the defaults #### Earlier text-slicing experiments The earlier branch revision sent a bounded PCM tail with left overlap and then deduplicated the resulting text. The first sweep used a 60 s input built by repeating the 15 s Qwen English demo four times. This is deliberately difficult for text overlap because each slice boundary falls inside nearly identical speech. | Left overlap | Output words | WER | End-to-end time | |---:|---:|---:|---:| | 2 s | 168 | 0.135 | 2.87 s | | 3 s | 201 | 0.358 | 3.29 s | More overlap gave the model more boundary audio to reword and made the stitched transcript worse. A realtime-paced rerun reproduced the same class of artifact, so append pressure was not the cause. The second sweep moved the activation gate from 16 s to 45 s: | Test audio | 16 s gate | 45 s gate | |---|---|---| | `reviewer_libri_mlk_en_35s`, 39.1 s | WER 0.069; duplicated `And I started listening to him` (3 duplicate runs) | WER 0.000; word-for-word with HTTP SSE | | `long_en_39s`, 39.3 s | WER 0.047; inserted `Flour, fat, and sauce.` | WER 0.000; word-for-word with HTTP SSE | | `long_nosilence_38s`, 38.5 s | WER 0.081; duplicated `And fat mutton pieces` (4 duplicate runs) | WER 0.000; word-for-word with HTTP SSE | | `repeat_en_30`, 39.8 s | Nondeterministic repetition drops across reruns | WER 0.000; all three repetitions retained | The higher gate fixed those cases by preventing slicing, not by making the seam safe. Under the 60 s item cap it bounded only the final 15 s: per-chunk prefill still grew from 32 to 731 tokens over the first 45 s before falling to about 58. The text-slicing path was therefore removed rather than kept as a second long-form policy. #### Retained encoder context The windowed sweep used TED-LIUM inputs at 300 s, 900 s, and 1105 s, each sent as one realtime item. Candidate settings were also checked on three critical cases: 75 s mixed-language speech switching language after the gate, 78 s speech containing 4 s pauses, and 119 s repeated audio. The final setting was selected for correctness rather than minimum inference time: | Config | 300 s | 900 s | 1105 s | Decision | |---|---|---|---|---| | 2 windows, 192-token prefix | 12.8 s, WER .323 | 31.2 s, WER .791 | 49.9 s, WER .022 | Reject: severe deletions | | 3 windows, 192-token prefix | 15.9 s, WER .016 | 43.3 s, WER .045 | 51.9 s, WER .022 | Reject: insufficient accuracy margin | | 4 windows, 192-token prefix | 15.0 s, WER .017 | 44.1 s, WER .042 | 51.6 s, WER .021 | Reject: lost mixed-language words and one repetition | | 4 windows, 512-token prefix | Critical cases only | | | Reject: more text did not replace missing audio context | | 6 or 7 windows, 192-token prefix | Critical cases only | | | Reject: lost a repetition or paused speech | | **8 windows, 192-token prefix** | **15.5 s** | **47.3 s** | **55.3 s** | **Only setting that passed all critical cases** | The 192-token prefix also matched the 512-token prefix on the long-form A/B. The larger prefix sent 320 additional prompt tokens per request without recovering acoustic information missing from smaller audio contexts.
## Conclusions ### Operator behavior Windowing is explicit opt-in. With the default `--asr-long-audio-strategy cumulative`, Qwen3-ASR always keeps the original full-audio path. To accept one longer windowed item, the operator sets `--asr-long-audio-strategy encoder_window` and raises `--asr-max-buffer-seconds` above the maximum expected item duration. The adapter policy then activates after 60 s. This makes the cap an explicit product decision: - leave the strategy cumulative and the cap at 60 s for unchanged behavior; - opt into `encoder_window` and raise the cap when a client needs one uninterrupted long item and accepts the model-specific windowed policy. ### Why encoder windows replaced text slicing Text slicing tried to make requests cheap by dropping old audio and matching overlapping decoded words. It had no reliable signal for distinguishing acoustic overlap from a user intentionally repeating the same phrase. More overlap made rewording worse, while a later gate restored quality only by making slicing rarely execute. The current design removes explicit text-overlap slicing. It reuses complete acoustic windows through stable multimodal identities and asks the decoder for a continuation from recent text context. Suffix reconciliation still exists, so this is not a claim that all text-boundary ambiguity has disappeared; it is a move from heuristic acoustic replay to model-aligned encoder reuse. ### Accuracy-first defaults The eight-window context is not the fastest tested setting. At 900 s, two windows finished in 31.2 s versus 47.3 s for eight windows, but the two-window run had WER 0.791 and severe deletions. Contexts from three through seven windows each failed at least one long, paused, repeated, or mixed-language case. For transcription, missing speech is a correctness failure, so the slower eight-window setting is the shipped default. The 192-token decoder prefix matched 512 tokens in the A/B while avoiding 320 extra prompt tokens per request. Increasing text context also did not recover speech omitted by smaller acoustic contexts. Both cumulative and windowed requests use the adapter's normal generation budget. If either reaches `max_new_tokens`, the item fails instead of marking a known-truncated transcript complete. **Behavior change:** realtime WebSocket transcription now reports a failed item when a cumulative or windowed decode reaches `max_new_tokens`, rather than publishing a known-truncated transcript as completed. HTTP JSON and SSE retain their OpenAI-compatible capped-text behavior because they do not use the realtime transcription failure-event lifecycle. ### Measured tradeoff This PR does not claim lower WER than segmented main. On the four TED-LIUM talks, the one-item PR path was better on two and worse on two, with a maximum absolute WER difference below 0.02. It provides a different capability: one uninterrupted 187-1105 s realtime item, bounded steady-state per-request work, bounded resident PCM, and no client-side 55 s segmentation. The strongest performance result is beyond the gate. At 90 s, median summed inference time fell 52.7%, uncached prompt tokens fell 34.9%, and flood wall time fell 46.2%. Main did not finish the previous 300 s flood run, while the current path completed 300/900/1105 s in 20.55/60.17/71.95 s end to end. Below the gate both builds use the same policy and identical token accounting, so no short-item performance gain is claimed. ## Known Limits 1. **This is not token-level M3 streaming.** Each 2 s ASR request completes before its delta is published. 2. **Windowed continuation is not timestamp aligned.** A model can still echo or reword recent prefix text. Reconciliation trims exact echoes and remains keep-biased; removing reworded text safely would require token/timestamp alignment or native streaming model state. 3. **No-whitespace CJK long audio stays cumulative.** The current decoder-suffix reconciliation is word based, so it does not receive bounded windowed performance even when the strategy is enabled. Pathological repeated input can reach `max_new_tokens` and fails closed rather than reporting a truncated completed transcript. 4. **Windowed mode requires model support.** The adapter must opt in and the multimodal processor must provide compatible independent encoder-window geometry. 5. **Window cache hits are not guaranteed.** Complete-window entries share the existing multimodal embedding cache with other workloads. Each active Qwen3-ASR item may retain up to eight windows, so concurrent long sessions can reduce the hit rate or evict image entries when that cache is undersized. Eviction or restart remains correctness-safe and causes re-encoding; operators should size the cache for their expected realtime and multimodal concurrency. 6. **Per-window mel is not bit-identical to contiguous mel at every STFT seam.** The measured long-form runs did not show a systematic transcript regression, but this PR does not claim exact full-context equivalence. 7. **Empty continuation output remains model dependent.** One non-final empty result is retried with retained audio; a second empty result is accepted so the request context cannot grow without bound. 8. **Repeated-audio HTTP SSE accumulation is pre-existing and remains.** The cumulative HTTP streaming path can over-produce on highly repetitive audio; this is separate from the windowed WebSocket path. 9. **The current windowed runtime is single-GPU only.** TP, DP, PP, multi-node, language-only, and disaggregated deployments fall back to cumulative ASR and restore the adapter's 60 s activation gate as the effective item limit, even if the operator configured a larger windowed item cap. ## Related - RFC: #22474 - Realtime WebSocket transport: #22848 - Current PR: #32682 --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): :x: [Run #31830334134](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31830334134) Latest PR Test (Extra): :x: [Run #31830334069](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31830334069)

signals.title: [Feature] MXFP4 KV Cache Decode for DSV4 on Hopper
signals.text: ## Summary MXFP4 KV cache for DeepSeek V4 on Hopper (SM90/H20), end to end: codec + memory pool + fused decode attention kernel + backend integration. The decode kernel is a JIT-compiled port of the FlashMLA three-stage split-KV design (scheduler metadata kernel + persistent WGMMA main kernel + combine kernel), covering all 44 layers (SWA + C4/C128 + attn_sink) in one call. The PR is self-contained: the kernel and its vendored dependencies live under `python/sglang/kernels/jit/` and compile at first use via `load_jit` — no sgl-kernel wheel changes required. ## MXFP4 Layout (368 B/token) ``` [224 B packed E2M1 | 14 B E8M0 + 2 B pad | 128 B BF16 RoPE] ``` - E2M1 (4-bit FP: 1S+2E+1M) nope data, block-size 32 (14 groups) - E8M0 8-bit exponent-only scale per group (dequantized in-register via `bits << 23`) - BF16 RoPE (unquantized) - Row-major contiguous, no page tail padding; no global scale needed (unlike NVFP4) - 16-byte-aligned row (368 B = 16×23) enables 128-bit loads; the NVFP4 reference's 380 B is only 4-byte aligned Memory capacity gain vs FP8: ~+37% full-token capacity (bytes/token 7705 → 5609; the NVFP4 reference gains +31.75%). ## Decode Kernel (`kernels/jit/csrc/mxfp4_dsv4_decode_sm90/`) FlashMLA-style fused split-KV decode for MXFP4: 1. **Scheduler metadata kernel** — 1 CTA × 1 thread computes per-SM split assignments with device-side length clamping (CUDA-graph safe: runs inside the captured graph, re-executes with replayed top-k lengths) 2. **Persistent main kernel** — 384 threads (3 warp groups: producer dequant→SMEM, QK+PV local, PV remote), WGMMA 64×64×16 / 64×256×16; E8M0 block-32 dequant via bit-shift, E2M1 via LUT+PRMT (4 instructions per 16 elements) 3. **Combine kernel** — merges split-K partials with PDL (programmatic dependent launch) Entry point: `entry.cuh` (TVM-FFI single translation unit, explicit instantiations for h_q 64/128). Python wrapper: `kernels/ops/attention/mxfp4_dsv4_decode_sm90.py` (FlashMLASchedMeta, per-geometry scratch reuse, C++-side stream resolution via `TVMFFIEnvGetStream`). ### Vendored dependencies (provenance) | Component | Source | |---|---| | `params.h`, `defines.h`, `utils.h`, `flashmla_utils.h`, `kerutils/`, `combine` | FlashMLA upstream @ 05e26647 | | `config.h`, `dequant.h`, `layout.h`, `components/helpers.h`, splitkv skeleton | SGLang reference PR #31269 (NVFP4) | | `splitkv_mla.cuh` (MXFP4 variant), `entry.cuh` | This PR | CUTLASS/CUTE headers come from the JIT build's `extra_dependencies=["cutlass"]` (pinned cutlass @ 147f5673, matching the reference PR). `kerutils` includes were converted to relative paths during vendoring. ## Changes - **Codec** (`srt/layers/attention/dsv4/mxfp4_k_cache.py`): quantize/dequant for the 368 B row (Triton), paged variants - **Compressor** (`compressor_v2.py`): `_forward_mxfp4` covering all 44 layers (C0/C4/C128), decode-plan boundary semantics - **Memory pool**: parameterized enablement via `--kv-cache-dtype fp4_e2m1 --fp4-kv-cache-recipe mxfp4` (env alias with deprecation warning); pool sizing/accounting unified - **Startup guards**: HiSparse + MXFP4 combination rejected at init (incompatible sparse layout); DeepseekV4 + fp4_e2m1 on non-SM90 fails fast with a clear error - **Backend** (`deepseek_v4_backend.py`): `_forward_mxfp4_decode_flashmla` — one fused call per layer; scheduler metadata shared per geometry across layers, re-created during CUDA-graph capture (top-k lengths are replayed device inputs) - **Tests**: `test/registered/kernels/ops/attention/test_mxfp4_dsv4_decode.py` (17 kernel cases: C0/C4/C128 × flash/profiling geometries, graph replay + length clamping, invalid contracts, scheduler-refresh regressions) + `test_mxfp4_k_cache.py` (5 codec cases) + `test_dsv4_hisparse_pool.py` (3 pool-guard cases) + `test_dsv4_compress_write_pad.py` (3 restored cases); benchmark in `test/registered/kernels/benchmark/attention/bench_mxfp4_dsv4_decode.py` - **E2E**: `test/registered/kernels/e2e/test_mxfp4_dsv4_e2e.py` — 8-GPU H200 server + gsm8k, exercising pool configurator → compressor → CUDA-graph capture (CI stage extra-b) - Removed the first-generation standalone JIT kernel (`mxfp4_decode.cuh` + `_forward_mxfp4_decode`) superseded by the FlashMLA port ## Validation - Kernel SASS was byte-identical to the AOT (cmake) build of the same sources at port time; the subsequent refactors (V32 path removal, aligned 128-bit row loads) are instruction-level changes covered by the same unit suite - Unit: 28/28 kernel + codec + pool-guard tests pass; 8-GPU e2e integration test passes locally - End-to-end on 8×H20 (TP8, `DeepSeek-V4-Flash`), FP8 (`--kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3`) vs MXFP4 (`--kv-cache-dtype fp4_e2m1 --fp4-kv-cache-recipe mxfp4`), identical server flags otherwise: | Metric | FP8 baseline | MXFP4 (this PR) | Δ | |---|---|---|---| | Decode throughput (server-side, 4k×256, conc 32) | 1013 tok/s | 980 tok/s | −3.3% | | GSM8K (1319, greedy, max_tokens 1024; truncated samples excluded) | 96.89% | 96.89% | 0.0pt | | AIME25 (480 = 30×16, greedy, max_tokens 32768; 73 truncated samples excluded from both) | 99.57% pass@1 | 99.78% pass@1 | +0.2pt | ## Known gaps / follow-ups - Small-batch (b≤8) kernel-level latency vs FP8: +8–12% (kernel-inherent scheduling granularity; end-to-end TPOT already within 5%) - Prefill-path throughput: −6.8% vs FP8 (out of scope for this PR; triton-based MXFP4 prefill) - Deep-context + high-concurrency decode (64 concurrent, 8k ctx, no rolling prefill): decode TPOT +17% vs FP8 (33.1 vs 28.3 ms); end-to-end 8k→8k throughput on par (1677 vs 1652 tok/s). One full AIME25 eval run showed −44% throughput vs FP8, but four controlled reruns (5-question replica, rolling short-prompt, 8k×8k fixed) could not reproduce it and measured MXFP4 at parity or faster — attributed to environment, not the kernel. - sm_90a-only (Hopper); no SM100 support (non-SM90 + fp4_e2m1 is rejected at startup) - HiSparse (sparse KV cache) not supported with MXFP4 — rejected at startup ## References - PR #31269 — NVFP4 KV cache for DSV4 in sgl-kernel (reference implementation for the FlashMLA three-stage decode) - FlashMLA upstream @ 05e26647 — scheduler/combine kernels and kerutils - This PR takes the jit_kernel approach (JIT CUDA via TVM-FFI) instead of AOT CUTLASS in sgl-kernel, keeping the PR self-contained --- **Status**: Ready for review — kernel + integration complete, end-to-end validated on 8×H20. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #31670942627](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31670942627)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #31670942449](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31670942449)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [Fix][AMD] MoRI EP: drop record_stream in TBO dispatch/combine (HSA out-of-resources)
signals.text: ## Motivation MoRI EP prefill with `--enable-two-batch-overlap` on MI355X aborts with `HSA_STATUS_ERROR_OUT_OF_RESOURCES`. The traceback blames whichever kernel needed scratch at that moment (for us, aiter `per_1x32_mx_quant_hip`), which is a victim, not the cause. The MoRI EP TBO path calls `record_stream(comm_stream)` on every dispatch/combine tensor. That parks each block in the caching allocator's deferred-free list until a comm-stream event retires, and with `async_finish` the compute stream never blocks on comm — so the deferred frees accumulate across layers. `reserved` grows far past the live set until allocations fail, the allocator dumps its cache via `release_cached_blocks()`, and eventually ROCr cannot find scratch and aborts the queue. On one DeepSeek-V4 rank (TP8/EP8/DP8, TBO on) a `hipMalloc`/`hipFree` replay showed **283.89 GiB of 288 GiB** at the abort. The non-EP DP TBO path already fixed exactly this — see `_TBO_PERSIST_BUF` in `layers/dp_attention.py`: > per-layer `torch.empty` churn ... kept alive by the comm-stream record_stream ballooned `reserved` to ~270GB and tripped HSA_STATUS_ERROR_OUT_OF_RESOURCES ... even though the live (allocated) working set was only ~10GB. The EP path never got the equivalent treatment. ## Modifications `python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/token_dispatcher/moriep.py` only: - Remove the four `record_stream(comm_stream)` calls in `_MoriEPDispatcherImplNormal` (`_dispatch_core` inputs/outputs, `_combine_core` inputs/output). - Add `_CROSS_STREAM_SAFETY_NOTE` documenting the failure mode and the safety argument. Unlike the DP path, `record_stream` is *removable* here rather than needing a keep-alive replacement: `dispatch_b`/`combine_b` launch on the comm stream and then run `compute_stream.wait_event(done_event)` in the same call, with no TBO yield between, so existing event ordering already covers both directions — inputs stay referenced by that frame until after the wait, and outputs are gated by the `previous_event` / `wait_stream(compute_stream)` before the next comm launch. Scope: only the dual-stream branch, which exists solely under TBO (`enable_dual_stream = is_tbo_enabled()`). Non-TBO MoRI and `_MoriEPDispatcherImplLowLatency` are unaffected. ## Accuracy Tests Not run — no numerics change, only when the allocator may recycle a block. Would appreciate a reviewer with MoRI EP CI access running the TBO accuracy job; I can run gsm8k on 2×MI355X if preferred. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Not benchmarked. Expected neutral to slightly positive — `record_stream` is off the critical path, and removing it should drop the `release_cached_blocks()` stalls (two within 40 s in the trace above). ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). (black, isort, `ruff --select=F401,F821,UP037`, codespell clean; full-ruleset ruff findings unchanged from base.) - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). (Needs a multi-GPU MoRI EP TBO prefill to surface; suggestions for a cheaper check welcome.) - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). (No user-facing change; rationale is in-code.) - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). (See above.) - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process). 2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers. 3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so. - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci` 4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #31560569469](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31560569469)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #31560569402](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31560569402)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [AMD] Enable gfx1250 Support
signals.text: ## Motivation AMD gfx1250 is a new GPU architecture that differs substantially from the existing gfx95x and gfx942 targets SGLang already supports. Several components require gfx1250-specific paths due to architectural differences: - **No MFMA/WMMA FP4 scale instructions** (`V_WMMA_SCALE_F32_32X16X128_F4`): the existing CK/ASM `fused_moe` and fp4 dense GEMM paths produce garbage or crash. - **Triton `tl.dot(fp8, fp8)` miscompiles** for contraction dim ≥ 128 on gfx1250 (verified correct at K=64, broken at K≥128), requiring bf16 upcasting in the MLA attention Triton kernels. - **`llvm.amdgcn.raw.buffer.*` buffer instructions are absent** on RDNA4 (gfx12): the `quick_all_reduce` kernel would fail to compile. - **aiter CK-backed kernels (rope, QK RMSNorm, etc.) do not build** against the gfx1250 ROCm 7.15 image's composable_kernel. - **TileLang CK-backed buffer addressing does not compile** on gfx1250, blocking the Sinkhorn/MHC path. - **`num_stages > 1` Triton pipelines miscompile** on gfx1250, causing NaN in block-FP8 matmuls. - **ROCm SDK is pip-installed** (not at `/opt/rocm`) on this new image, requiring build and runtime path fixups for AITER, TileLang, MORI, and SGLang itself. This PR brings up gfx1250 support for DSv4, DSR1, and GPT-OSS-120B models with MXFP4/FP8 quantization. ## Modifications ### Infrastructure & Docker (`docker/rocm.Dockerfile`, `scripts/ci/amd/amd_ci_install_dependency.sh`, `python/pyproject_other.toml`) - Added a new `gfx1250-rocm7_15` Docker build stage starting from `ubuntu:24.04` with pip-installed ROCm 7.15 SDK, PyTorch 2.11, and Triton 3.7. Includes path and symlink workarounds for a pip-based (non-`/opt/rocm`) ROCm SDK. - Added `GPU_ARCH_LIST_ARG` build-arg and made `PYTORCH_ROCM_ARCH` configurable; per-arch `TRITON_COMMIT_DEFAULT` env vars. - Added gfx1250-specific AITER build path (`ENABLE_CK=0`, pip `--no-build-isolation`) and MORI build path using `CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH` for the ROCm SDK. - Added gfx1250-aware TileLang `ROCM_PATH` override during CMake build. - Updated Triton rebuild logic to preserve the installed version string (workaround for ROCm 7.15 / [rocm-systems#7643](https://github.com/ROCm/rocm-systems/issues/7643)). - Renamed `SETUPTOOLS_SCM_PRETEND_VERSION` → `SGLANG_VERSION` to avoid leaking SGLang's nightly version into AITER's version. - Added `compressed-tensors==0.16.0` pin to `runtime_common` (supports torch ≥ 2.10) and dropped the old per-`srt_hip` `==0.15.0` pin. - CI install script: ROCm-version-aware AITER rebuild (`pip --no-build-isolation` for ROCm ≥ 7.15), MORI `CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH` fix, and MORI commit extraction validation. ### Core utility (`python/sglang/srt/utils/common.py`) - Added `is_gfx1250_supported()` (cached) to detect AMD RDNA4 by `gcnArchName`. - Extended `mxfp_supported()` to include `"gfx1250"`. ### sgl-kernel (`sgl-kernel/setup_rocm.py`, `sgl-kernel/csrc/allreduce/quick_all_reduce_base.h`) - Added `gfx1250` to the allowed arch list in `setup_rocm.py`; gfx1250 shares the `E4M3` FP8 type and the 128KB dynamic smem budget with gfx950. - Guarded `llvm.amdgcn.raw.buffer.load/store.v4i32` declarations behind `#if !defined(__gfx1250__)`, providing stub no-ops for RDNA4 where those intrinsics don't exist. ### Attention kernels (`python/sglang/kernels/ops/attention/`) - **`decode_attention.py`**: Do not downcast `q` to `fp8` before the QK dot; instead upcast K to `q`'s dtype (`bf16`) for the dot product, avoiding the gfx1250 fp8 dot bug at K≥128. Also keep softmax weights `p` in fp32 for the P·V accumulation (recovers GSM8K accuracy ~0.82 → ~0.92 on gfx1250 R1). - **`extend_attention.py`**: Same fp8 upcast fix and fp32 P·V fix for the prefill extend/unified kernels. - **`dsv4/unified_kv_kernels/paged_decode.py`**: On gfx1250, dispatch DSv4 sparse decode attention to `aiter.ops.triton.attention.pa_decode_sparse.pa_decode_sparse` (the triton path) instead of the custom Triton implementation. - **`dsv4/unified_kv_kernels/paged_prefill.py`**: Disable the OPUS (gfx950 ASM) prefill path on gfx1250. ### MoE gate JIT kernel (`python/sglang/kernels/jit/csrc/moe/moe_fused_gate.cuh`) - Widened `__shfl_down_sync` mask from `0xFFFFFFFF` to a 64-bit `0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFULL` on gfx1250 (which requires a 64-bit sync mask), while staying 32-bit on all other arches. ### Layernorm (`python/sglang/kernels/ops/layernorm/mhc.py`, `python/sglang/srt/layers/layernorm.py`) - On gfx1250, use aiter's Triton RMSNorm and `rmsnorm2d_fwd_with_add` instead of the CK-backed aiter equivalents (which do not build). - Added pure-torch (`_hc_split_sinkhorn_torch`) and Triton (`_hc_split_sinkhorn_triton`) implementations of the Sinkhorn MHC kernel, dispatched on gfx1250 since TileLang's CK-backed addressing does not compile there. ### Quantization – FP8 (`python/sglang/kernels/ops/quantization/fp8_kernel.py`, `python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/fp8.py`, `python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/fp8_utils.py`) - **`fp8_kernel.py`**: Added `_w8a8_block_fp8_matmul_gfx1250`, a gfx1250-specific block-FP8 matmul that: (1) upcasts fp8 operands to bf16 before `tl.dot`, (2) uses only `num_stages=1` (no SW pipelining), and (3) avoids modulo-wrap index tricks that miscompile on gfx1250. Selected automatically when `_is_gfx1250` is set. - **`fp8_utils.py`**: Force `_use_aiter = False` on gfx1250 (CK/MFMA-dependent aiter quant/GEMM kernels cannot run), directing gfx1250 to the pure-Triton block-FP8 path. Extended `triton_w8a8_block_fp8_linear` to accept pre-quantized `(input, input_scale)` from gfx1250's fused quant ops (skipping re-quantization). - **`fp8.py`**: On gfx1250, use `moe_shuffle_scale` (n32k4 layout) instead of the gfx950 `shuffle_scale` (e8m0 layout) for FP8 MoE weight scales. Respect the `AITER_FORCE_A8W4` flag to select the triton a8w4 kernel shuffle layout. ### Quantization – MXFP4 Quark schemes (`python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/quark/schemes/`) - **`quark_w4a4_mxfp4.py`**: On gfx1250 with `AITER_FORCE_A8W4=1`, dequantize FP4 weights to bf16 at load time (since no dense fp4 GEMM is available) and run a plain bf16 linear forward. Includes a pure-Python MXFP4 e2m1 → bf16 dequantization LUT. - **`quark_w4a4_mxfp4_moe.py`**: On gfx1250, use `moe_shuffle_scale` (n32k4 layout) for W4A4 MoE weight scales (instead of `e8m0_shuffle`). Shuffle weights with the (16,16) aiter layout when `AITER_FORCE_A8W4` is set. - **`quark_w4a8_mxfp4_moe.py`**: Added a dedicated gfx1250 W4A8 MoE path (`_use_gfx1250_w4a8`): bypasses the aiter CK/ASM fused_moe entirely; uses aiter's triton `moe_gemm_a8w4` kernel with a contraction-major, gate/up-interleaved, unshuffled weight layout. Weight preparation (`_process_weights_gfx1250`) and forward (`aiter_w4a8_gfx1250_forward` in new file `aiter_mxfp4_w4a8_moe.py`) are implemented separately from the gfx950 path. ### New file: `python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/fused_moe_triton/aiter_mxfp4_w4a8_moe.py` - Implements MXFP4 W4A8 GPT-OSS MoE forward for gfx1250 via `moe_gemm_a8w4`: routing, manual activation gather (in-kernel TDM gather disabled on gfx1250), static-FP8 downcast, two-GEMM (gate_up + down) execution with fused SwiGLU, and scatter back to token order. ### RoPE (`python/sglang/srt/layers/rotary_embedding/factory.py`) - Fall back from aiter's CK rope kernels to SGLang's native rope on gfx1250 (aiter rope does not build on this arch). ### Communicator / fused quant (`python/sglang/srt/layers/communicator.py`) - On gfx1250, use `fused_rms_fp8_group_quant` (triton, group_size=hidden_size = per-token) instead of aiter's CK `rmsnorm_quant` / `add_rmsnorm_quant` kernels. ### Sampler (`python/sglang/srt/layers/sampler.py`) - Disable aiter's greedy sample kernel on gfx1250 (not supported), falling back to `torch.argmax`. ### Capture mode (`python/sglang/srt/model_executor/runner_utils/capture_mode.py`) - Disable `torch.compile` during CUDA graph capture on gfx1250 (compilation + capture together triggers issues on this arch). ### MLA attention (`python/sglang/srt/models/deepseek_common/attention_forward_methods/forward_mla.py`, new `triton_qk_rmsnorm.py`) - On gfx1250 (`AITER_FORCE_A8W4=1`), substitute the aiter `fused_qk_rmsnorm` (CK-backed, doesn't build) with a self-contained Triton RMSNorm or pure-torch fallback from the new `triton_qk_rmsnorm.py`. - Fixed the RoPE skip condition to check membership in `FORWARD_ABSORB_CORE_ATTENTION_BACKENDS` (not a string equality check), preventing an incorrect empty-K bug on non-aiter backends. ### DSv4 decoder layer (`python/sglang/srt/models/deepseek_v4.py`, `deepseek_common/utils.py`, `amd/deepseek_v4_fused_mhc.py`) - Extended all `_is_gfx95_supported` guards that gate MXFP4 fused quant, MQA q/k-norm, post-attention layernorm fused rmsnorm, and the fused MHC post/pre path to also include `_is_gfx1250_supported`. - On gfx1250, the fused MHC path is enabled by `SGLANG_OPT_FUSE_MHC_POST_PRE` alone (no TileLang dependency), and the aiter Triton `try_fused_hc_post_pre` is used at all token batch sizes (no M-threshold cap, since there is no TileLang fallback). - gfx1250 does not skip the post-layernorm step after the Triton MHC kernel (since `norm_fused=False` for the aiter path). ### C4 attention indexer (`python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/dsv4/indexer.py`) - Added `_use_torch_fn` guard so the `SGLANG_FP8_PAGED_MQA_LOGITS_TORCH` env var correctly prevents the 1D c4sl unsqueeze on gfx1250. ### Server args (`python/sglang/srt/server_args.py`) - Track `_mem_fraction_static_set_by_user`: when the user explicitly sets `--mem-fraction-static`, skip the automatic 0.85 scaling for `aiter` backend with long contexts (instead, emit a warning so the user knows what is happening). ## Accuracy Tests Passed E2E accuracy tests of DSv4, DSR1, and GPT-OSS-120B. GPT-OSS-120B > AITER_FORCE_A8W4=1 ENABLE_CK=0 SGLANG_USE_AITER=1 SGLANG_USE_AITER_MOE_GU_ITLV=1 SGLANG_USE_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN=1 python3 -m sglang.launch_server --model-path /dockerx/model/gpt-oss-120b-w-mxfp4-a-fp8/ --trust-remote-code --tp 1 --prefill-attention-backend triton --decode-attention-backend aiter --max-running-requests 1024 --mem-fraction-static 0.9 --disable-radix-cache --page-size 64 DSR1 > ENABLE_CK=0 SGLANG_USE_AITER=1 AITER_FORCE_A8W4=1 AITER_GROUPED_FORCE_SPLIT_K1=1 SGLANG_MOE_SHUFFLE_GFX1250=1 ROCM_QUICK_REDUCE_QUANTIZATION=NONE SGLANG_AITER_FP8_PREFILL_ATTN=0 SGLANG_AITER_MLA_PERSIST=0 SGLANG_INT4_WEIGHT=0 SGLANG_MOE_PADDING=1 SGLANG_SET_CPU_AFFINITY=1 SGLANG_ROCM_FUSED_DECODE_MLA=0 SGLANG_USE_ROCM700A=1 AITER_GROUPED_CONTIGUOUS_TOKEN_THRESHOLD=16 python3 -m sglang.launch_server --model-path /dockerx/model/DeepSeek-R1-0528-MXFP4 --tensor-parallel-size 1 --trust-remote-code --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000 --mem-fraction-static 0.90 --chunked-prefill-size 16384 --attention-backend triton --max-running-requests 128 --kv-cache-dtype auto --page-size 64 DSv4-Flash > SGLANG_DEFAULT_THINKING=1 AITER_GROUPED_CONTIGUOUS_TOKEN_THRESHOLD=16 SGLANG_DSV4_REASONING_EFFORT=max SGLANG_USE_ROCM700A=0 SGLANG_HACK_FLASHMLA_BACKEND=unified_kv_triton AITER_BF16_FP8_MOE_BOUND=0 AITER_FORCE_A8W4=1 SGLANG_USE_AITER_MOE_GU_ITLV=0 SGLANG_OPT_FUSE_MHC_POST_PRE=0 ENABLE_CK=0 SGLANG_USE_AITER=1 AITER_GROUPED_FORCE_SPLIT_K1=1 python3 -m sglang.launch_server --model-path /dockerx/model/DeepSeek-V4-Flash --trust-remote-code --tp 1 --attention-backend dsv4 --page-size 256 --mem-fraction-static 0.60 --swa-full-tokens-ratio 0.15 --disable-shared-experts-fusion --tool-call-parser deepseekv4 --reasoning-parser deepseek-v4 --chunked-prefill-size 8192 --cuda-graph-max-bs 256 --max-running-requests 256 --disable-radix-cache --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 ## signals.title: [PD] Fix reasoning token accounting for the handoff token
signals.text: ## Motivation Fixes #32897. In PD disaggregation, the prefill worker samples the first output token and the decode worker commits it to the request. The colocated prefill path updates reasoning-token accounting at the same point, but the PD handoff path previously only appended the token to `output_ids`. This undercounts reasoning usage by one for a normal handoff. If the handoff token is the think-end token, it can also leave the accounting state in the reasoning phase and count later answer tokens incorrectly. ## Modifications - Update reasoning-token accounting when decode commits a newly sampled PD handoff token. - Skip the update when true-retraction rebootstrap replays an already emitted boundary token, because its accounting state is retained and must not be counted twice. ## Accuracy Tests This change does not alter model outputs, sampling, or KV transfer behavior. It only updates usage metadata for the handoff token. Live PD validation passed: with the change applied, reasoning-token usage was correct for a response stopped by `max_tokens` during the reasoning phase. Validation performed: - `black --check python/sglang/srt/disaggregation/decode.py` - `ruff check --no-cache python/sglang/srt/disaggregation/decode.py` - Python syntax compilation of `decode.py` - `git diff --check` The existing decode-queue CPU test file could not be collected locally because Triton is unavailable in the CPU-only environment. No new test file is included in this minimal patch. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Not applicable. The change adds one scalar accounting check once per PD request handoff and does not affect the model-forward or per-token decode path. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). (No new test file is included in this minimal patch.) - [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). (Not applicable: no configuration or public API change.) - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). (Not applicable; explained above.) - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process). 2. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so. - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci` 4. signals.title: [MoE] Fuse swiglu moe up gemm epilogue
signals.text: ## Motivation **What the MoE activation costs today.** The triton fused-MoE path runs three steps per layer: an up-GEMM that writes `intermediate_cache1` at the full gate+up width `N`, a standalone `silu_and_mul` that reads that buffer and writes `intermediate_cache2` at width `N/2`, and a down-GEMM. The middle step is pure data movement dressed as compute — it round-trips the entire intermediate tensor through HBM to apply an elementwise function whose inputs the up-GEMM already had sitting in registers. **Why that is worth removing at small batch.** At batch 1 a MoE layer's GEMMs degenerate into `M=4..8` slivers, so the step is bound by weight bandwidth and by the intrinsic latency floor of several hundred tiny kernels rather than by arithmetic. In that regime an extra launch plus a full round trip of the intermediate buffer, paid once per MoE layer per decode step, is a visible fraction of the step. It is also a link in the dependency chain — `GEMM1 -> act -> GEMM2` — that no amount of overlap can shorten while the activation stands between the two GEMMs. **Why it cannot simply be folded in.** The activation needs `gate[i]` and `up[i]` together, but the checkpoint stores W13 as two contiguous halves, so those two values come out of output columns `i` and `i + N/2` — different tiles of the up-GEMM. A tile holding `gate[i]` does not hold `up[i]`, and vice versa. **The fix.** Permute the rows of W13 once at load so gate and up of the same intermediate channel become adjacent columns. Each GEMM output column is an independent dot product of the input with one row of W13, so reordering rows can only reorder columns — the permute is value-neutral. After it, every `(gate[i], up[i])` pair lands in the *same* output tile as an even/odd column pair, the epilogue applies `silu(gate) * up` in-register, and only the half-width result is stored. `intermediate_cache1` and the standalone activation launch disappear, and the chain shortens to `GEMM1 -> GEMM2`. ## Modifications - `python/sglang/kernels/ops/moe/fused_moe_triton_kernels.py`: `FUSE_SWIGLU` constexpr on `fused_moe_kernel`, plus the epilogue that splits the accumulator into even/odd column pairs, applies the activation, and stores the half-width result. `invoke_fused_moe_kernel` gains a `fuse_swiglu` argument and asserts the output flavors it is incompatible with. - `python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/moe_runner/triton_utils/fused_moe.py`: allocates the half-width buffer as the up-GEMM destination, skips the standalone activation, and threads the flag through `fused_experts` / `fused_experts_impl` / `_fused_moe_kernel_sequence`. - `python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/moe_runner/triton.py`: `TritonMoeQuantInfo.fuse_swiglu_interleaved` carries the layout fact from the weight owner to both `fused_experts` entry points. - `python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/unquant.py`: `_maybe_interleave_w13_for_fused_swiglu` performs the load-time permute, per expert so the gather temporary stays at one expert's slice. - `python/sglang/srt/environ.py`: `SGLANG_OPT_FUSE_SWIGLU_INTERLEAVED`, default off. ### Bit parity is instruction-level, not approximate The kernel being replaced is compiled with `-use_fast_math`, so matching it means matching the instructions it emits. The epilogue uses `tl.inline_asm_elementwise` to do exactly that: `mul + ex2.approx.ftz` for `__expf`, `div.approx.ftz` for the division, and `mul.ftz.f32` for the product, with a single final rounding to bf16. The accumulator is already `compute_type` at that point, which matches the reference's bf16 store to `intermediate_cache1` followed by a reload. One detail is easy to get wrong and invisible from the call site: the reference instantiates its activation functor at `float`, so silu never lands in bf16 before the multiply. An implementation that rounds silu to bf16 first double-rounds and diverges on a large fraction of inputs. The first version of this change did exactly that, and only an element-wise bit comparison caught it. ### Why this is opt-in The permuted layout is understood by the fused epilogue and by nothing else, so every consumer that reads W13 — or the pre-activation buffer — in the checkpoint's halves layout has to be excluded at load rather than trapped later. The gate requires CUDA, the plain triton runner, standard a2a, no bias, bf16, and gated silu without `alpha` / `clamp_limit` / `swiglu_limit`, and additionally excludes: - **LoRA.** `_add_lora_gate_up_delta` adds its delta into the full-width pre-activation buffer this path eliminates, and indexes gate/up as contiguous halves of it — both assumptions break. Excluding it at load matters more than asserting at run time: permuting first and asserting later would turn `--enable-lora` into a crash after warmup instead of a clean fallback. The virtual-experts LoRA path is unaffected, since it consumes `lora_a` / `lora_b` and never the base W13. - **EPLB**, which rearranges experts by copying checkpoint-layout weights into the parameter. - Runtime weight updates, for the same reason; this one is documented on the env var rather than detected. Two further guards fail loudly rather than silently: `_fused_moe_kernel_sequence` asserts the call carries no hooks and no quantization, and `invoke_fused_moe_kernel` asserts that none of `fuse_add_to_output` / `mask_output` / `fuse_sum_all_reduce` / `lora_preserve_base` are set — those address `C` at the full width `N` and would write past the row end of the half-width buffer. Filtered (`-1`) expert blocks skip the store entirely for the same reason. Under the unfused path those rows are zero-filled at full width; here the row is only `N/2` wide, so an `N`-wide zero store would run into the next token's data. The rows are never read, because the down-GEMM CTA for such a block early-exits before loading its input. ## Accuracy Tests New: `test/registered/kernels/ops/moe/test_fused_swiglu_epilogue.py`, registered `base-b-kernel-unit` / `1-gpu-large`. Both cases assert **bitwise** equality; a tolerance would defeat their purpose, since the failure mode this change risks is a plausible-looking few-ULP drift that no `assert_close` would flag. - `test_fused_matches_unfused_bitwise` drives the real `fused_experts` entry point twice — halves layout with the standalone activation, then interleaved layout with the epilogue — and requires the final MoE output to be bit-identical. Shapes cover a bs=1 decode row and a ragged token count that forces the `BLOCK_SIZE_M` tail. It also covers the filtered-expert claim: if those unwritten rows were ever read, the comparison would fail immediately. - `test_epilogue_matches_silu_and_mul_bitwise` isolates the epilogue arithmetic against `silu_and_mul` over random values plus the saturating tails and signed zeros. This is the guard against a future "simplification" to `tl.sigmoid` or an early bf16 cast. All three pass on H20-3e (sm90). End-to-end on `Kimi-Linear-48B-A3B-Instruct` (256 experts, `moe_intermediate_size` 1024, bf16, TP4, H20-3e): six greedy prompts at 128 new tokens each, served once with the flag off and once with it on. The two output sets are **byte-identical** (equal md5). The fused run logs `Interleaved w13 gate/up: ...` on all four TP ranks and the baseline run logs it zero times, so the comparison is not vacuously passing on an inactive fast path. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Removed, per MoE layer per forward: | | before | after | |---|---|---| | kernel launches | up-GEMM, activation, down-GEMM | up-GEMM, down-GEMM | | intermediate traffic | `intermediate_cache1` written at width `N`, read back at width `N` | none | | dependency chain | `GEMM1 -> act -> GEMM2` | `GEMM1 -> GEMM2` | Measured on `Kimi-Linear-48B-A3B-Instruct`, TP4 on H20-3e (sm90), `bench_serving --dataset-name random --num-prompts 24 --random-input-len 512 --random-output-len 256 --max-concurrency 1`, four runs per configuration: | | mean TPOT (4 runs) | output throughput | |---|---|---| | baseline | 2.49 / 2.49 / 2.49 / 2.49 ms | 362.2 - 368.6 tok/s | | fused | **2.46 / 2.46 / 2.46 / 2.46 ms** | 364.5 - 372.4 tok/s | **-1.2% mean TPOT**, with the two sets fully separated — no overlap across four runs each. Throughput moves the same way but its run-to-run spread (~1.8%) is wider than the effect, so only the TPOT column supports a conclusion here. The win scales with how launch-bound the step is, so it is largest at small batch and shrinks toward zero once the GEMMs grow big enough to dominate. sm90 with a 27-layer model at 512/256 is a conservative setting for it; the shape this was originally built for is batch-1 decode on Blackwell with a deeper MoE stack, which is not measured here. That asymmetry is the other reason this ships opt-in rather than on by default. ## Checklist - [ ] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): :x: [Run #31776581047](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31776581047) Latest PR Test (Extra): :white_check_mark: [Run #31776580851](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31776580851)

signals.title: docs(cookbook): Qwen3.6 config-driven deployment + measured speed benchmarks
signals.text: Migrates the Qwen3.6 cookbook page to the **config-driven Deployment/Playground engine** (as for DeepSeek-V4 / Qwen3.5) and adds **measured speed benchmarks**. The legacy `qwen36-deployment.jsx` generator is removed. ## Config — `configs/qwen/qwen3.6.jsx` (44 cells) `h100/h200/b200/b300` × `{35B-A3B (MoE), 27B (Dense)}` × `{bf16, fp8, +nvfp4 on Blackwell}` × `{low-latency, high-throughput}`, plus **Xeon `balanced`** (27B/35B-A3B × bf16/fp8). low-latency = MTP/EAGLE + mamba radix-cache v2; high-throughput = MTP off; Xeon = spec unsupported → single `balanced` recipe (`--device cpu`, tp 3/6). GPU cells tp=1 single-node. ## Faithfulness - Cells reproduce the generator command **verbatim** — verified by executing `generateCommand()` across the matrix: **42/44 exact**. Parsers (`--reasoning-parser`/`--tool-call-parser`) omitted (Playground-only; DSv4 convention). - The 2 non-verbatim cells are **b300 35B-A3B NVFP4**, adding `--moe-runner-backend flashinfer_cutlass`: the generator's default moe runner crashes on that model on 0.5.16, and this is exactly how b300 was measured. - Bench = `bench_serving` random isl 8192 / osl 1024, `--random-range-ratio 1.0 --warmup-requests 64 --flush-cache`; LL @ conc 1+16, HT @ conc 1024+4096. `tokens_per_sec_per_gpu = output_throughput / tp × (isl+osl)/osl`. ## Coverage — 32/44 measured - Measured: **B200 (12) @ 0.5.15, H200 (8) + B300 (12) @ 0.5.16**. - Pending (render "pending"): **H100 (8)** — no 8×H100 capacity this run; **Xeon (4)** — no CPU box (Deploy command shown, no speed). - Blackwell NVFP4 version note: b200 on 0.5.15 (default moe runner works → plain command), b300 on 0.5.16 (needs the flag) — **each cell matches its own bench**. ## Follow-ups - Bench H100 (8) once capacity frees. - Re-bench b200 35B-A3B NVFP4 on 0.5.16 with `flashinfer_cutlass` to unify the Blackwell backend. - Apply the +13% mem0.92 tune to h200 35B-A3B bf16 HT (clean conc 1024+4096 re-bench). Supersedes the prose-table approach in #23798. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #31840436754](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31840436754)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #31840436167](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31840436167)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->
