signals.title: Split ragged TRTLLM MHA decode batches by sequence length
signals.text: ## Motivation TRTLLM-GEN decode attention can pay a large tail-latency tax when a full batch contains requests with very different KV sequence lengths. In an AgentX-style Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-NVFP4 workload on GB300, keeping batch size, average context length, draft settings, and request count fixed while changing the per-batch ISL distribution from uniform 92k to 30k/70k/110k/170k increased the steady decode step from about 49.7 ms to 57.5 ms (+16%). A matched 50-step Nsys comparison localized 8.377 ms of the 9.822 ms step delta (85.3%) to full attention. The main SM100 variable-sequence FMHA kernel alone contributed 7.601 ms. At BS44/rank on a 148-SM GB300, the TRTLLM-GEN selector has only `floor(148 / (2 * 44)) = 1` KV CTA per request and selects the persistent kernel. Long requests then form the tail of the shared wave. This PR adds an opt-in way to sort requests by KV length and execute fixed-query-length TRTLLM MHA decode in equal-sized groups. With two groups, each BS22 launch admits three KV CTAs per request and moves this workload into the multi-CTA static regime while separating short and long requests. ## Modifications - Add `SGLANG_TRTLLM_MHA_DECODE_SEQ_LEN_SPLITS` (default: `1`). The default preserves the existing single-call path. - For values above one, sort requests by KV sequence length, split them into equal-sized groups, gather query/page-table/length metadata, invoke TRTLLM MHA once per group, and scatter outputs back to request order. - Share this path between normal decode and fixed-query-length speculative target verification, including NVFP4 KV-cache scale handling. - Reject values below one and cap the number of groups at the request count. - Add CUDA-graph correctness coverage for regular decode and Frozen-KV MTP with two sequence-length groups. ## Accuracy Tests Configuration: `nvidia/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-NVFP4`, 8x GB300, ModelOpt FP4 weights, FP8 KV cache, TP8/DP8/EP8, TRTLLM MHA, NEXTN with 5 speculative steps / 6 draft tokens, page size 64, and `SGLANG_TRTLLM_MHA_DECODE_SEQ_LEN_SPLITS=2`. | Test | Result | Gate | |---|---:|---:| | GSM8K | **0.985** (197/200) | >= 0.95 | | Examples completed | **200/200** | 200/200 | | Natural request-weighted accepted length | **4.569** | > 3.3 | | Natural weighted acceptance rate | **0.7137** | informational | | Evaluation latency | 108.232 s | informational | | Output throughput | 5,010.3 token/s | informational | Acceptance was not simulated. It was aggregated from 1,533 Decode log rows across all eight ranks with a request weight of 11,828. The model evaluation completed and saved all 200 results; the original wrapper then exited nonzero in its post-eval `/server_info` check because that endpoint returned the router summary. The corrected log-based post-check was run on the saved artifacts and passed both gates. The same implementation also completed the full target-verify and draft CUDA-graph warmup used by the performance and accuracy runs. Targeted unit tests in this PR cover CUDA-graph replay for regular decode and Frozen-KV MTP. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Hardware/model configuration: `nvidia/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-NVFP4` on 8x GB300, ModelOpt FP4 weights, FP8 KV cache, TP8/DP8/EP8, TRTLLM MHA, NEXTN draft length 6, OSL 600, 352 global requests (44/rank), and one request wave. ### End-to-end steady decode iteration latency The metric is the mean wall-clock latency per SGLang speculative decode scheduler iteration, derived from generation throughput over each decode logging interval. With 44 running requests and a fixed accepted length of 4.808 output tokens/request/iteration: `decode iteration time (ms) = 44 requests * 4.808 accepted tokens/request / generation throughput (token/s) * 1000` Each iteration includes the NEXTN draft and target-verification work and emits 4.808 output tokens per request on average. | Workload | Splits=1 (ms/iteration) | Splits=2 (ms/iteration) | Delta | |---|---:|---:|---:| | Mixed ISL: 30k/70k/110k/170k | 57.485 ms | **51.639 ms** | **-5.846 ms (-10.17%)** | | Uniform 92k, exact matched `(DP, full_tokens)` points | 49.907 ms | 50.008 ms | +0.101 ms (+0.20%) | - Mixed comparison: 92 steady BS44/rank, queue-zero samples per arm. Mean context was 95,352.3 tokens for baseline and 95,374.9 for split-2 (+0.024%). Split-2 closes 75.5% of the original mixed-ISL tax. - Uniform comparison: 64 exact matched points across all eight DP ranks. Median delta was **-0.472 ms**. The first common logging window contributed +3.017 ms; the remaining seven windows averaged -0.316 ms, so there is no material steady-state regression. ### Attention microbenchmarks | Fixed query length | Splits=1 | Splits=2 | Delta | |---|---:|---:|---:| | q_len=1 | 0.757 ms | **0.637 ms** | **-15.9%** | | q_len=6 | 1.066 ms | **0.711 ms** | **-33.3%** | Split-4 was slower than split-2 in both microbenchmarks, so this PR does not enable splitting by default and exposes the group count as an opt-in tuning knob. ### Nsys attribution The matched mixed/uniform profile windows contained only Decode/running44/queue0 steps on every rank: | Metric | Uniform | Mixed | Mixed - uniform | |---|---:|---:|---:| | Overlap-safe step span | 51.537 ms | 61.359 ms | +9.822 ms | | Full attention | 11.827 ms | 20.204 ms | +8.377 ms | | Main SM100 VarSeq FMHA kernel | - | - | +7.601 ms | | GPU idle | - | - | +0.020 ms | Full attention explains 85.3% of the measured step tax. The profile and the selector's CTA budget both support the persistent-wave tail as the mechanism addressed by the split. ### Local validation on the upstream-main commit - `pre-commit` on all three changed files: formatting, AST, isort, ruff, black, codespell, registered-test checks, bare-`pytest.main` check, and static runtime ratchets passed. - `python3 -m py_compile` on all three changed files passed. - `git diff --check origin/main...HEAD` passed. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). (The opt-in environment variable is documented inline next to its declaration.) - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #31851519805](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31851519805)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #31851519673](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31851519673)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [WIP] Localize HiCache DCP indices once per transfer, not per layer
signals.text: ## Motivation Under DCP, `MLATokenToKVPoolHost.load_to_device_per_layer()` translated the widened logical slots into this rank's physical rows on every call: ```python host_indices = self.dcp_kernel_indices(host_indices) device_indices = self.dcp_kernel_indices(device_indices) ``` The result is layer-independent, but the load loop calls the method once per layer. The cost is worse than the launch count suggests. `indices[indices % dcp_size == dcp_rank]` is boolean-mask indexing, which goes through `nonzero` — and `nonzero` must read the selected count back to the host to size its output. That is a **device→host sync**, and it runs inside `with device_module.stream(self.load_stream)`, so each layer's translation blocks on the previous layer's transfer kernel. The loop serialises. `start_loading()` is called from the scheduler thread (`scheduler.py`, `get_new_batch_prefill` → `ready_to_load_host_cache`), so the stall lands directly in front of the forward launch. Measured below: **2.75 syncs per translation, 54 translations per load, 5.2 ms per load.** ## Modifications - `HostKVCache.dcp_localize_indices(host_indices, device_indices)` translates a transfer's index pair once. - `load_to_device_per_layer()` now *takes* this rank's physical rows — the translation is gone from the MLA implementation. This makes explicit the precondition `_backup_from_device_per_layer` already relies on ("Indices arrive already translated…"). - `HiCacheController.start_loading()` localizes once ahead of its layer loop. - `backup_from_device_all_layer()` keeps translating internally: it owns its own layer loop, so it already paid the cost once per write-back. Pools that are not DCP-sharded return the inputs unchanged, so nothing changes unless `--dcp-size > 1`. ### Deliberately untouched Three other paths reach `load_to_device_per_layer`, and none needs to localize, because none can run under DCP: - **draft KV** — `_resolve_hicache_dcp_compatibility` rejects `speculative_algorithm` with `--dcp-size > 1`, and the draft host pool is built without `dcp_size`. The draft KV is replicated, so it wants logical slots anyway. - **HiSparse** — the same guard rejects `--enable-hisparse` with `--dcp-size > 1`, citing that the HiSparse host pool is constructed without DCP translation. - **`HostPoolGroup`** (hybrid) — forwards to per-entry pools, every one of which is `dcp_size == 1`. All three are correct with un-localized indices, since the translation is the identity at `dcp_size == 1`. ## Benchmarking and Profiling **Setup.** 8×B300, DeepSeek-V2-Lite-Chat (MLA, 27 layers), `--tp-size 8 --dcp-size 8 --page-size 64 --enable-hierarchical-cache --hicache-ratio 4 --hicache-io-backend kernel`, `--max-total-tokens 16384` per rank (→ 131072 logical radix slots under DCP). Workload `generated-shared-prefix`: 96 groups × 8 prompts, 4096-token system prompt, 768 requests, concurrency 16 — ~393k tokens of unique shared prefix, ≈3× logical device capacity, so prefixes evict to L2 and are pulled back constantly. Both arms moved an identical **14,352,384 tokens** through the load path. Fresh server per arm, no profiler attached, 2 reps each. ### `sglang:load_back_duration_seconds` — the load loop itself | arm | loads | sum (s) | **per load** | |---|---|---|---| | base rep1 | 1232 | 6.384 | 5.18 ms | | base rep2 | 1224 | 6.300 | 5.15 ms | | patched rep1 | 1216 | 2.120 | **1.74 ms** | | patched rep2 | 1240 | 2.116 | **1.71 ms** | **5.16 ms → 1.73 ms per load, a 2.99× reduction.** Spread within each arm is ≤1%, so the effect is ~100× the run-to-run noise. ### End-to-end (mean of 2 reps) | metric | base | patched | | |---|---|---|---| | Request throughput | 23.64 req/s | 24.78 req/s | **+4.8%** | | Total token throughput | 104,326 tok/s | 109,372 tok/s | **+4.8%** | | Mean TTFT | 470.99 ms | 445.79 ms | **−5.4%** | | Median TTFT | 455.22 ms | 431.24 ms | −5.3% | | P95 TTFT | 533.73 ms | 494.62 ms | −7.3% | | Mean E2E latency | 673.92 ms | 642.68 ms | −4.6% | ### Torch profiler, TP-0, ~6 s window, 12 load loops in each arm `transfer_hicache` 324 (base) vs 326 (patched) confirms both windows did the same transfer work. | op | base | patched | Δ | |---|---|---|---| | `aten::nonzero` | 661 / 51.4 ms | 40 / 3.7 ms | −621 calls, **−93% time** | | `aten::index` | 1387 / 86.1 ms | 772 / 26.8 ms | −615 calls, **−69% time** | | `aten::floor_divide` | 1374 | 718 | −656 | | `aten::eq` | 799 | 179 | −620 | | `cudaStreamSynchronize` | 14825 | 13108 | **−1717** | | `Memcpy DtoH` | 14975 | 13260 | **−1715** | 12 loops × 52 eliminated translations = 624, which matches every op-count delta. The sync hypothesis holds: removing 624 translations removed ~1717 stream syncs and ~1715 device→host copies — **~2.75 syncs per translation**, exactly the `nonzero` readback. Caveat: V2-Lite is a small model, so the *relative* e2e gain is favourable to the change; on a larger MLA model the forward dominates more, though the absolute per-load saving grows with layer count (Kimi-K2's 61 layers ⇒ 122 translations vs 54 here). ## Accuracy Tests No numerical change: the indices handed to the transfer kernels are identical, only computed once per transfer instead of once per layer. Unit tests in `test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_hicache_dcp_host_pool.py`: - `test_load_forwards_localized_rows_unchanged` — the per-layer path passes localized rows to the kernel untouched. This guards a *silent* failure: re-translating at `dcp_size=8` turns 64 rows into 8 **and passes** the `numel` assert inside `dcp_kernel_indices`, so a reintroduced translation would quietly read the wrong slots rather than crash. - `test_localization_is_hoisted_out_of_the_layer_loop` — drives `start_loading` with a 24-layer fake pool and asserts `dcp_localize_indices` is called exactly once and that every layer receives those exact tensors. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Code Formatting with Pre-Commit](https://docs.sglang.ai/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-formatting-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests. - [x] Provide accuracy results. - [ ] Update documentation / docstrings / example tutorials if this PR changes the behavior of the code. - [ ] For reviewers: If you haven't made any contributions to this PR and are only assisting with merging the main branch, please remove yourself as a co-author when merging the PR. - [x] Please feel free to join our Slack channel at https://slack.sglang.ai to discuss your PR. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

signals.title: [Diffusion] Add MiniMax H3 cube sparse attention
signals.text: ## Summary - add a FlexAttention-based cube sparse attention backend for MiniMax H3's 3D visual streams - wire H3 packed-sequence metadata and denoise-step sparsity schedules into the native pipeline - keep text, audio, standalone reference images, and the text-only token refiner on dense attention - document the component-scoped command and add numerical, CUDA, admission, and parallelism coverage ## Behavior Select the backend only for the H3 transformer: ```bash --component-attention-backends transformer=cube_sparse_attn \ --attention-backend-config '{"local_cube_size":[4,4,4],"topk_ratio_list":[1.0,1.0,0.8,0.7,0.6,0.5,0.5]}' ``` A ratio of `1.0` uses H3's native FlashAttention path. Ratios below `1.0` use approximate cube sparsity. Ring parallelism is rejected because its attention exchange does not compose with this backend; Ulysses remains supported. ## Performance On 2×H100 with the 1344×768, 4-second, 8-step TP2 workload: - dense FlashAttention denoise: 16.51s - aggressive all-`0.05` sparse schedule: 13.32s (19.3% faster) - mixed `[1.0, 1.0, 0.8, 0.7, 0.6, 0.5, 0.5]` schedule: 19.67s The mixed schedule is slower on this short sequence because FlexAttention routing overhead outweighs the sparse-kernel savings, so the feature remains opt-in and the cookbook calls out the tradeoff. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #31856755676](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31856755676)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #31856755577](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31856755577)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [Tokenizer] Keep dispatched request state so the delayed abort can fire
signals.text: ## Motivation When a streaming client disconnects, SGLang may leave the request running on the scheduler. `create_abort_task` waits 2 seconds before sending the abort. On the failing path, `generate_request` handles cancellation first and `_discard_pending_req_states(obj)` removes the request from `rid_to_state`. In single-tokenizer mode, `abort_request` then treats the missing state as already finished and returns without dispatching an `AbortReq`. The cleanup was intended for failures before scheduler IPC enqueue, such as input-length validation. Removing the state after dispatch instead strands a request that the scheduler is still running. The same guard can also make `/abort_request` return 200 without dispatching an abort. This was observed on one TP4 replica in a four-replica deployment, with each replica using the default `--tokenizer-worker-num 1`. A client disconnected after 3 seconds, but the request continued for another 71.4 seconds and generated 1,803 tokens before finishing normally. During a 1,800-second observation window on that replica, 16 abandoned requests averaged 477 seconds of observed post-disconnect decoding; one remained active for the full window. This corresponds to approximately 4.24 continuously occupied slots, or ~13% of the configured `--max-running-requests=32`. At one sampled instant, abandoned requests occupied 5 of the 32 slots. ## Modifications 1. Add `ReqState.dispatched`, set after successful scheduler IPC enqueue. 2. Make `_discard_pending_req_states` remove only requests that were never dispatched. Dispatched states remain until `_handle_batch_output` or `_handle_abort_req` removes them. 3. Add `expect_obj` to `abort_request` so delayed aborts target the request instance that created them. 4. Pass the originating object from `create_abort_task`, including the cached `obj[i]` objects for batched requests. The identity check prevents a delayed abort from killing a newer request that reused the same rid. It applies in both single- and multi-tokenizer modes. Explicit `/abort_request` calls do not pass `expect_obj`. In multi-tokenizer mode they still dispatch when the rid is absent locally, since the request may belong to another tokenizer worker. ## Accuracy Tests Not applicable. No kernel or model-forward code is changed, and tokens delivered before a disconnect are unaffected. ## Speed Tests and Profiling No throughput impact is expected. The change recovers scheduler capacity occupied by abandoned requests. A 12-hour A/B run on the same machine produced: | | Patched | Unpatched | |---|---:|---:| | Decode batches | 26,119 | 25,258 | | Disconnected rids | 142 | 333 | | Post-disconnect decode lines per rid | 17 | 6,262 | Post-disconnect decoding per rid fell by 99.7%. This run used a simplified version that removed the guard outright, rather than the exact implementation in this PR. It demonstrates the capacity benefit of delivering aborts to the scheduler; request-identity safety is covered by unit tests. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Tests Added 13 test cases to `test/registered/unit/managers/test_tokenizer_manager_rid_cleanup.py`: ```console $ python3 -m pytest test/registered/unit/managers/test_tokenizer_manager_rid_cleanup.py -q 31 passed, 2 warnings in 25.78s ``` Coverage includes: - cleanup of dispatched, undispatched, and partially dispatched batches - delayed abort delivery after client disconnect - protection against rid reuse in single- and multi-tokenizer modes - explicit `/abort_request` behavior across tokenizer workers - request identity for single and batched background aborts Eight of the new cases are regression tests that fail when their corresponding change is reverted. The other five preserve existing compatibility and implementation invariants. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #31857985953](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31857985953)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #31857985880](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31857985880)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: Return expert routing info to support MoE routing replay
signals.text: <!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.ai to discuss further. --> ## Motivation Today SGLang can record MoE expert utilization, but it’s hard to attribute per-token routing decisions back to individual user requests when batching, prefill, and decode are interleaved. For training (e.g., GRPO), debugging, and routing analysis, we need a precise 1:1 mapping from recorded tokens to the originating request id (RID), and we want that routing info returned with the response. In this way, training MoE models with routing replay can be implemented easily with SGLang. This PR enables SGLang to return per-token expert routing in meta_info along with the responses generated. ## Modifications - Add a new `return_expert_routing` arg to the `async_generate()` function signature. - Add rids in forwardbatch so that recorders can get access to it and later re-map to each request accurately. - This function can be easily extended to more entropy points apart from the `async_generate()`. ## Accuracy Tests No numerical kernel changes; model outputs are unaffected unless return_expert_routing=True is requested, in which case only metadata is added. ## Benchmarking and Profiling We are using the existing recorder, and change the dtype of the expert routing info matrix from int32 to uint8 to further optimize the memory usage. So nothing should slow down the recorder in any manner. ## Checklist - [ ] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.ai/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.ai/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.ai/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.ai/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.ai/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).

signal.title: [JIT Kernel] Fused Add+RMSNorm+per-token FP8 quant: enable for checkpoint-quantized models, wire RMSNorm, validate (revives #22005)
signal.text: ## Motivation Resubmission of #22005 against the current tree, per @hnyls2002's review there. The gap that PR identified is still open on main: `python/sglang/kernels/jit/csrc/elementwise/fused_add_rmsnorm.cuh` is a plain add+rmsnorm with no quant fusion, so an FP8 linear doing **dynamic per-token** activation quant still pays a separate quant launch that re-reads the row the norm just wrote. The two existing quant fusions are a different granularity: | path | scale granularity | device | |---|---|---| | flashinfer `fused_add_rmsnorm_quant` | static per-tensor (scale is an input) | CUDA | | aiter fused AR+RMSNorm+quant | per-group 1x128 | ROCm | | **this PR** | **dynamic per-token** | CUDA | ## Changes vs #22005 **1. New tree layout.** Kernel at `python/sglang/kernels/jit/csrc/elementwise/fused_add_rmsnorm_per_token_quant.cuh`, wrapper at `python/sglang/kernels/ops/layernorm/fused_norm_quant.py`, registered in the layernorm op inventory. **2. No tensor-attribute stamping.** #22005 handed the fp8 tensor and scale to `apply_fp8_linear` by setting `_sglang_fp8_data` / `_sglang_fp8_scale` on the bf16 output. That channel is invisible to CUDA-graph capture, and dynamo resolves the `getattr` at trace time on a FakeTensor, so the fused path silently never fires under `torch.compile`. **There are zero occurrences of those attributes in the diff.** Instead this rides the pre-quantized-activation contract that already exists for the static per-tensor fusion: `RMSNorm.forward_with_per_token_quant_fusion` returns the same `(fp8_out, scale, orig_dtype)` tuple as `forward_with_per_tensor_quant_fusion`, so `Fp8LinearMethod.apply` and the compressed-tensors W8A8-FP8 scheme need no new entry point. The only pre-existing code this touches is `apply_fp8_linear`'s prequantized branch, where the `input_scale.numel() == 1` assert is widened to also accept one scale per row; for a scalar scale that path is unchanged line for line. **Gating:** `SGLANG_FUSED_NORM_FP8_QUANT` (opt-in), CUDA, and a new `_is_dynamic_per_token_fp8_linear(quant_linear)` — the mirror of the existing `_is_static_per_tensor_fp8_linear`. That predicate is also why the original never activated: #22005 gated on `server_args.quantization == "fp8"`, which is unset for checkpoint-quantized models. **Reduction bug fixed.** #22005 both launched `blockDim.x == vec_hidden_size` verbatim *and* counted warps with a truncating `blockDim.x / 32`. Both are fixed here, and they are redundant — a 2x2 revert shows either alone is sufficient and only reverting both fails. Reverting both fails 57/111 cases concentrated exactly on hidden sizes 264/520/1032/3080/5128 (vector widths 33/65/129/385/641), with scale error up to 5.2e-01, while the exact-warp sizes stay green. ## ⚠️ Limits - **`hidden_size <= 8192`** (one CTA per token, one thread per 16B vector). Llama-3.1-405B-FP8-dynamic and Nemotron-Ultra-253B-FP8-dynamic are both hidden 16384 and silently take the unfused path. - **Not bit-identical to the unfused path**, by construction: the per-token absmax comes from the fp32 values still in registers rather than the rounded activation-dtype value the unfused path reads back from HBM. One fewer rounding step — the fused scale is the *more* accurate of the two — but greedy decoding diverges. The residual stream is bit-identical. ## Test plan / results Measured on **1xH100 80GB (SM90)**, torch 2.13.0+cu130 / sgl-kernel 0.4.6.post1 / flashinfer 0.6.17, `Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct-FP8-dynamic` (compressed-tensors, dynamic per-token), TP=1, input_len=1024 / output_len=64, 3 repeats: - kernel tests: **111 passed**, 0 skipped - activation-quant launches: **128 -> 64 per forward (-50.0%)**, eager - decode throughput: **+1.89%** (bs=1) / **+2.90%** (bs=8) / **+2.17%** (bs=32) / **+1.77%** (bs=64) — the 3-repeat ranges do not overlap - prefill throughput: **+1.8% .. +2.3%** at bs>=8, also non-overlapping - GSM8K 5-shot greedy, 1314 scored: **0.75647** unfused vs **0.76408** fused (single-arm SE ~1.18pp, i.e. indistinguishable) - scale max relative difference grows with M: 1.6e-3 (M=1) .. 7.1e-3 (M=2048); ~3.0-3.2% of fp8 code points differ - `--enable-torch-compile`: 17 graph breaks with and without, identical locations — none from this PR CUDA-graph capture was verified separately: the fused call is recorded into every captured graph (282 forwards x 64 calls), and the dedicated capture+replay unit test is the regression guard for the design change in (2). Original kernel authorship preserved via `Co-authored-by: narutolhy`. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #31859146665](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31859146665)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #31859146432](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31859146432)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [WIP] Localize HiCache DCP indices once per transfer, not per layer
signal.text: ## Motivation Under DCP, `MLATokenToKVPoolHost.load_to_device_per_layer()` translated the widened logical slots into this rank's physical rows on every call: ```python host_indices = self.dcp_kernel_indices(host_indices) device_indices = self.dcp_kernel_indices(device_indices) ``` The result is layer-independent, but the load loop calls the method once per layer. The cost is worse than the launch count suggests. `indices[indices % dcp_size == dcp_rank]` is boolean-mask indexing, which goes through `nonzero` — and `nonzero` must read the selected count back to the host to size its output. That is a **device→host sync**, and it runs inside `with device_module.stream(self.load_stream)`, so each layer's translation blocks on the previous layer's transfer kernel. The loop serialises. `start_loading()` is called from the scheduler thread (`scheduler.py`, `get_new_batch_prefill` → `ready_to_load_host_cache`), so the stall lands directly in front of the forward launch. Measured below: **2.75 syncs per translation, 54 translations per load, 5.2 ms per load.** ## Modifications - `HostKVCache.dcp_localize_indices(host_indices, device_indices)` translates a transfer's index pair once. - `load_to_device_per_layer()` now *takes* this rank's physical rows — the translation is gone from the MLA implementation. This makes explicit the precondition `_backup_from_device_per_layer` already relies on ("Indices arrive already translated…"). - `HiCacheController.start_loading()` localizes once ahead of its layer loop. - `backup_from_device_all_layer()` keeps translating internally: it owns its own layer loop, so it already paid the cost once per write-back. Pools that are not DCP-sharded return the inputs unchanged, so nothing changes unless `--dcp-size > 1`. ### Deliberately untouched Three other paths reach `load_to_device_per_layer`, and none needs to localize, because none can run under DCP: - **draft KV** — `_resolve_hicache_dcp_compatibility` rejects `speculative_algorithm` with `--dcp-size > 1`, and the draft host pool is built without `dcp_size`. The draft KV is replicated, so it wants logical slots anyway. - **HiSparse** — the same guard rejects `--enable-hisparse` with `--dcp-size > 1`, citing that the HiSparse host pool is constructed without DCP translation. - **`HostPoolGroup`** (hybrid) — forwards to per-entry pools, every one of which is `dcp_size == 1`. All three are correct with un-localized indices, since the translation is the identity at `dcp_size == 1`. ## Benchmarking and Profiling **Setup.** 8×B300, DeepSeek-V2-Lite-Chat (MLA, 27 layers), `--tp-size 8 --dcp-size 8 --page-size 64 --enable-hierarchical-cache --hicache-ratio 4 --hicache-io-backend kernel`, `--max-total-tokens 16384` per rank (→ 131072 logical radix slots under DCP). Workload `generated-shared-prefix`: 96 groups × 8 prompts, 4096-token system prompt, 768 requests, concurrency 16 — ~393k tokens of unique shared prefix, ≈3× logical device capacity, so prefixes evict to L2 and are pulled back constantly. Both arms moved an identical **14,352,384 tokens** through the load path. Fresh server per arm, no profiler attached, 2 reps each. ### `sglang:load_back_duration_seconds` — the load loop itself | arm | loads | sum (s) | **per load** | |---|---|---|---| | base rep1 | 1232 | 6.384 | 5.18 ms | | base rep2 | 1224 | 6.300 | 5.15 ms | | patched rep1 | 1216 | 2.120 | **1.74 ms** | | patched rep2 | 1240 | 2.116 | **1.71 ms** | **5.16 ms → 1.73 ms per load, a 2.99× reduction.** Spread within each arm is ≤1%, so the effect is ~100× the run-to-run noise. ### End-to-end (mean of 2 reps) | metric | base | patched | | |---|---|---|---| | Request throughput | 23.64 req/s | 24.78 req/s | **+4.8%** | | Total token throughput | 104,326 tok/s | 109,372 tok/s | **+4.8%** | | Mean TTFT | 470.99 ms | 445.79 ms | **−5.4%** | | Median TTFT | 455.22 ms | 431.24 ms | −5.3% | | P95 TTFT | 533.73 ms | 494.62 ms | −7.3% | | Mean E2E latency | 673.92 ms | 642.68 ms | −4.6% | ### Torch profiler, TP-0, ~6 s window, 12 load loops in each arm `transfer_hicache` 324 (base) vs 326 (patched) confirms both windows did the same transfer work. | op | base | patched | Δ | |---|---|---|---| | `aten::nonzero` | 661 / 51.4 ms | 40 / 3.7 ms | −621 calls, **−93% time** | | `aten::index` | 1387 / 86.1 ms | 772 / 26.8 ms | −615 calls, **−69% time** | | `aten::floor_divide` | 1374 | 718 | −656 | | `aten::eq` | 799 | 179 | −620 | | `cudaStreamSynchronize` | 14825 | 13108 | **−1717** | | `Memcpy DtoH` | 14975 | 13260 | **−1715** | 12 loops × 52 eliminated translations = 624, which matches every op-count delta. The sync hypothesis holds: removing 624 translations removed ~1717 stream syncs and ~1715 device→host copies — **~2.75 syncs per translation**, exactly the `nonzero` readback. Caveat: V2-Lite is a small model, so the *relative* e2e gain is favourable to the change; on a larger MLA model the forward dominates more, though the absolute per-load saving grows with layer count (Kimi-K2's 61 layers ⇒ 122 translations vs 54 here). ## Accuracy Tests No numerical change: the indices handed to the transfer kernels are identical, only computed once per transfer instead of once per layer. Unit tests in `test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_hicache_dcp_host_pool.py`: - `test_load_forwards_localized_rows_unchanged` — the per-layer path passes localized rows to the kernel untouched. This guards a *silent* failure: re-translating at `dcp_size=8` turns 64 rows into 8 **and passes** the `numel` assert inside `dcp_kernel_indices`, so a reintroduced translation would quietly read the wrong slots rather than crash. - `test_localization_is_hoisted_out_of_the_layer_loop` — drives `start_loading` with a 24-layer fake pool and asserts `dcp_localize_indices` is called exactly once and that every layer receives those exact tensors. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Code Formatting with Pre-Commit](https://docs.sglang.ai/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-formatting-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests. - [x] Provide accuracy results. - [ ] Update documentation / docstrings / example tutorials if this PR changes the behavior of the code. - [ ] For reviewers: If you haven't made any contributions to this PR and are only assisting with merging the main branch, please remove yourself as a co-author when merging the PR. - [x] Please feel free to join our Slack channel at https://slack.sglang.ai to discuss your PR. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

signal.title: [AMD] Fix weight checking for AITER-shuffled block FP8 weights
signal.text: ## Motivation This ports #34016 from `sglang-miles` to `main` following maintainer feedback. AITER pre-shuffles block-FP8 weights on ROCm for optimized inference kernels. The weight checker was treating the shuffled physical layout as the original logical layout during dequantization, causing false weight-update mismatches even though inference was correct. AITER rotary `cos_cache` and `sin_cache` buffers were also missing from the checker's existing derived-buffer skip patterns. ## Modifications - Mark dense and MoE block-FP8 parameters after AITER layout shuffling. - Propagate the layout metadata into the weight checker. - Restore the logical FP8 layout before checker dequantization, checksum, and ULP comparison. - Skip AITER rotary `cos_cache` and `sin_cache` buffers during weight checking. - Add unit tests for layout restoration, metadata propagation, and rotary-cache handling. - Register the weight-checker unit tests for AMD CI. The layout conversion is only applied to weights explicitly marked as AITER-shuffled. NVIDIA and other unshuffled paths retain the existing behavior. ## Accuracy Tests Validated on AMD MI355 with the Miles [DeepSeek V4 four-layer E2E test](https://github.com/radixark/miles/blob/main/tests/e2e/megatron/model_scripts/test_deepseek_v4_flash_4layer_ci.py). Both rollout runs passed, and all checked FP8 weights reported `num_exceed=0`. Weight-checker unit tests: - New focused tests: 6 passed - Full unit suite: 64 passed, 1 skipped because NVIDIA DeepGEMM is unavailable on ROCm This PR does not modify model forward computation or inference kernels. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Not applicable. The only inference-path change is setting metadata during weight loading. Layout restoration runs exclusively when the weight checker is enabled and does not affect normal inference performance. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #31815213513](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31815213513)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #31815213147](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31815213147)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [AMD] Broadcast the EAGLE greedy verify decision across TP ranks on ROCm
signal.text: Co-author-with: @XinyuJiangCMU <!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. --> ## Motivation <!-- Describe the purpose and goals of this pull request. --> On ROCm with TP > 1, EAGLE speculative decoding can intermittently deadlock. Observed on 4x MI355X (gfx950), GLM-4.7-Flash, TP4, with **2 deadlocks in 5 runs**. Before the watchdog fires, TP ranks disagree on the running batch: ```text TP0: batch_size()=24, first_req=86e5957d… TP1: batch_size()=24, first_req=86e5957d… TP2: batch_size()=25, first_req=f224663e… TP3: batch_size()=25, first_req=f224663e… ``` On ROCm, _is_hip makes `eagle_sample()` always use the greedy verify path. This path can receive different draft candidates across ranks, while the sampling path already broadcasts its result from rank 0. With different draft candidates, TP ranks can therefore accept different numbers of drafts, and eventually diverge in `seq_lens` / batch composition and deadlock. ## Modifications <!-- Detail the changes made in this pull request. --> On ROCm, broadcast `predict`, `accept_index`, and `num_correct_drafts` from TP rank 0 after the verify decision is finalized. A normal process-group broadcast is sufficient because `eagle_sample()` runs after the target forward CUDA graph replay. ## Accuracy Tests <!-- If this pull request affects model outputs (e.g., changes to the kernel or model forward code), provide accuracy test results. --> End-to-end on 4x MI355X, GLM-4.7-Flash, EAGLE + MTP. Deadlock rate: | | runs | deadlocks | |---|---:|---:| | before | 5 | **2** | | after | 6 | **0** | All six post-fix runs completed without watchdog, memory access fault, or scheduler divergence. ## Speed Tests and Profiling <!-- If this pull request impacts inference speed, provide benchmarking and profiling results. --> ## Checklist - [ ] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [ ] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. signal.title: [Bug] [Diffusion] Attention backend fallback change introduced errors on most models
signal.text: ### Checklist - [x] I searched related issues but found no solution. - [x] The bug persists in the latest version. - [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback. - [x] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed. - [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed. ### Describe the bug Hi! Previously, if the desired attention backend was not part of any of the supported attention backends for the component, it defaulted to SDPA. PR #33707 changed the behavior so that it raises an error instead. Most text encoders (and some other components) have attention in them, but it's only supported via FAv3 or SDPA due to the input tensor dimensions. On ROCm, the default requested attention backend is AITER, so this now raises an error for pretty much all models. Most models don't outright crash entirely, they just revert to the diffusers version of the component instead of using the optimized sgl-d version, though MiniMax-H3 crashes fully (diffusers versions are not allowed). This is not limited to ROCm only - any desired backend that is not FA or SDPA will run into this issue (SageAttention, NPU etc). While it is possible to overcome this by adding `--component-attention-backends.text_encoder torch_sdpa`, this is not signaled to the user nor is it really that nice UX. I made this into a ticket instead of PR, as I'm not sure what's the best fix instead of just reverting it. It seems there's currently some attention backend related refactoring going on, maybe this is included in it. signal.title: Support prefill-side pipeline parallelism with EAGLE under PD disaggregation
signal.text: # Support prefill-side pipeline parallelism with EAGLE under PD disaggregation Lets a PD prefill engine run `--pp-size > 1` together with EAGLE speculative decoding. The two were mutually exclusive; the assert is narrowed to allow the combination on a PD prefill engine only (decode stays pure TP). Validated on Qwen3.5-397B-A17B across two 8-GPU nodes, gsm8k 1319 questions at concurrency 128: | prefill | KV transfer path | accuracy | throughput | |---|---|---|---| | `pp=1 × tp=8` + EAGLE | `send_kvcache` | 0.961 | 4127 tok/s | | `pp=2 × tp=4` + EAGLE | `send_kvcache_slice` | 0.961 | 3501 tok/s | | `pp=8 × tp=1` + EAGLE | `send_kvcache_slice` | 0.961 | 3127 tok/s | | `pp=2 × tp=4`, no spec | `send_kvcache_slice` | 0.960 | 2503 tok/s | --- ## The draft lives on the last stage only The EAGLE draft needs the target's last-layer hidden states and the sampled token, which exist only on the last pipeline stage: ```python self._hosts_draft = get_pp_group().is_last_rank self._draft_worker = EagleDraftWorker(...) if self._hosts_draft else None ``` The split is at `EagleDraftWorker`, not at `EAGLEWorkerV2`: every rank keeps an `EAGLEWorkerV2`, so the scheduler's dispatch and `run_batch` stay rank-uniform. A rank without a draft runs the target, returns its proxy tensors, and stops. ### Memory impact The last stage carries the draft's weights *and* a full-size draft KV pool. Qwen3.5-397B at `pp=8 × tp=1` (60 layers, `full_attention_interval=4` ⇒ 15 full-attention layers, default split `7,7,7,7,8,8,8,8`): | stage | full-attn layers | weights | KV pool | GPU used | |---|---|---|---|---| | PP0 | 1 | 88.6 GB | 36.7 GB | 58.6% | | PP1–3 | 2 | 86.6 GB | 73.5 GB | 68.0% | | PP4–6 | 2 | 98.9 GB | 73.5 GB | 74.5% | | **PP7** | 2 **+ draft 1** | 100.8 + **16.1** GB | **110.2 GB** | **92.6%** | Three factors stack on the last rank: the split is by *total* layers while KV cost tracks *full-attention* layers, the total layer count is itself uneven, and the draft sits on top. Spread is **1.58×**; since `max_total_num_tokens` is MIN-synced across stages, the tightest rank caps everyone and **27.7% of cluster memory is idle**. ### Mitigation: manual repartition Effective full-attention layers are `15 + 1 (draft) = 16` over 8 stages, so each stage should hold 2 and the last stage 1 target layer plus the draft. Full-attention layers occur every 4 layers, so the smallest contiguous range holding two is 8, fixing the partition uniquely: ``` SGLANG_PP_LAYER_PARTITION=8,8,8,8,8,8,8,4 ``` | | default | repartitioned | |---|---|---| | KV pool per stage | 36.7 / 73.5 / **110.2** GB | **40.2 GB on all eight** | | GPU spread | 1.58× | 1.29× | | tightest rank | 92.6% | 62.6% | | `max_total_num_tokens` | 16,949,376 | **21,099,648 (+24.5%)** | PP0 now binds and is already at the structural minimum, so this is optimal under the contiguous-range constraint. The residual 0.85% is the embedding (measured 1.83 GB gap vs 1.90 GB embedding), which cannot move off stage 0. --- ## Changes to EAGLE So a rank can hold an `EAGLEWorkerV2` with no draft inside it and still behave like a plain target worker. - **Proxy tensors** — `EAGLEWorkerV2.forward_batch_generation` takes `pp_proxy_tensors` and passes it to the target worker. The speculative branch in `run_batch` previously dropped it. - **Guards for a missing draft** — `get_draft_kv_pool` dereferenced the inner `EagleDraftWorker` unconditionally and crashed on every non-last stage; it now returns `None`, which is also what the transfer path wants. The adaptive controller is built only where the draft is. - **Half-shared embed/head** — the target's embedding is on the first stage and its lm_head on the last, so a draft on the last stage receives only one of them. `set_embed_and_head` replaced both unconditionally and crashed in `vocab_parallel_embedding` on `None`; it now keeps what the draft loaded for the missing half. - **Result-shape guards** — `copy_to_cpu` is gated on the existing `has_sampled_token_ids`, as the non-speculative branch already was. `FutureMap`'s lazy init keyed `need_topk` on the algorithm alone while `need_hidden_states` also checked the payload; both now check it. - **Shared hidden-state spec** — the PD wire schema needs the draft's hidden width and dtype on ranks with no draft runner, so the helper is split into a config-only core with the runner entry point delegating to it. ## Changes to PP mechanics - **Draft parallel state** — the draft is one layer and never spans stages, but the model reads `get_pp_group()` in `__init__`, so a draft on a non-first stage turns its embedding into `PPMissingLayer`. Added `_SELF_PP`, a single-member pipeline group per rank, and `patch_pipeline_parallel_group` mirroring the existing `patch_tensor_parallel_group`. `new_group` is collective, so all `world_size` groups are created by every rank. `ps` also needs `pp_size=1`, not just `pp_rank=0`, or `model_runner`'s `support_pp` assert fires first; the same omission is fixed in five sibling spec workers. - **No collectives on last-stage-only paths** — two WORLD collectives would have hung with the draft on a subset of ranks: the pre-model-load memory probe in `bootstrap.py` (the draft reuses the target's `memory_pool_config`, so its own value feeds nothing) and the random seed broadcast (the target's seed is now injected). - **Output ring carries the draft proposal** — every rank consumes the result rebuilt from the output ring, including the last stage, which receives its own output after a full loop. The rebuilt result had no `next_draft_input`, so `topk_p` / `topk_index` / `hidden_states` are relayed and the proposal is rebuilt and rebound to `batch.spec_info`. Cost is `bs × hidden × 2B` per hop per micro-batch. - **Device tensors on the ring** — the speculative branch D2H-copied `next_token_ids` before the ring send, so the relayed tensor reached `FutureMap.stash` on the host while the buffers stayed on device. Under PP that copy is wasted and destructive, so it is gated on `pp_size == 1`. - **Partition env vs. the draft** — `SGLANG_PP_LAYER_PARTITION` is process-global, so the `pp_size=1` draft read the target's list and rejected it for the wrong length. `get_pp_indices` now ignores the list when `pp_size == 1`. Prerequisite for any custom partition under PP + spec. - **Linear-state budget was charged model-wide** — `mamba_cache_per_req` counts every linear layer while the pools are built from the stage-local slice, a 7.5× over-charge at `pp_size=8` on a 45-linear-layer model. `pp=8` with `--max-running-requests 512` failed to start before this. Independent of speculative decoding. ## Changes to PD disaggregation - **Hybrid-linear KV transfer under PP** (also in #33457, independent of EAGLE) — a hybrid-linear pool stores KV only for its full-attention layers, but `prefill_start_layer` came from `pool.start_layer`, a global index that also counts linear layers, while the decode peer's pointer list is dense over full-attention layers. Translated to a full-attention-relative offset, and layer-id pairing is now preferred whenever both peers publish ids. - **Draft KV buffers get their own layer ids** — `kv_layer_ids` must cover every entry in `kv_data_ptrs`, but the draft buffers appended after the target's had none, so both peers suppressed the list and fell back to positional slicing, which slices the wrong layers under `pp_size > 1`. The draft pool's ids are remapped into a reserved band above the target's layer range; both peers derive it from the same draft config. `send_kvcache_slice` also learns to pair by layer id, since the flat pointer list is no longer `[K block, V block]` once draft entries are appended. --- ## Not covered - No automatic layer partitioner; `SGLANG_PP_LAYER_PARTITION` must be set by hand for balanced memory. - Failure containment on the last stage: an exception in draft extend still escapes `run_batch`. - `send_kvcache_slice` has no unit test — it needs a real transfer engine, unlike `_send_kvcache_generic`. - Only the mooncake slice path was changed; nixl's equivalent is unverified. - Head-sliced transfer now rejects non-uniform KV item lengths instead of mis-computing addresses, tightening a pre-existing assumption. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #31858436958](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31858436958)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #31858436794](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31858436794)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [Tokenizer] Keep dispatched request state so the delayed abort can fire
signal.text: ## Motivation When a streaming client disconnects, SGLang may leave the request running on the scheduler. `create_abort_task` waits 2 seconds before sending the abort. On the failing path, `generate_request` handles cancellation first and `_discard_pending_req_states(obj)` removes the request from `rid_to_state`. In single-tokenizer mode, `abort_request` then treats the missing state as already finished and returns without dispatching an `AbortReq`. The cleanup was intended for failures before scheduler IPC enqueue, such as input-length validation. Removing the state after dispatch instead strands a request that the scheduler is still running. The same guard can also make `/abort_request` return 200 without dispatching an abort. This was observed on one TP4 replica in a four-replica deployment, with each replica using the default `--tokenizer-worker-num 1`. A client disconnected after 3 seconds, but the request continued for another 71.4 seconds and generated 1,803 tokens before finishing normally. During a 1,800-second observation window on that replica, 16 abandoned requests averaged 477 seconds of observed post-disconnect decoding; one remained active for the full window. This corresponds to approximately 4.24 continuously occupied slots, or ~13% of the configured `--max-running-requests=32`. At one sampled instant, abandoned requests occupied 5 of the 32 slots. ## Modifications 1. Add `ReqState.dispatched`, set after successful scheduler IPC enqueue. 2. Make `_discard_pending_req_states` remove only requests that were never dispatched. Dispatched states remain until `_handle_batch_output` or `_handle_abort_req` removes them. 3. Add `expect_obj` to `abort_request` so delayed aborts target the request instance that created them. 4. Pass the originating object from `create_abort_task`, including the cached `obj[i]` objects for batched requests. The identity check prevents a delayed abort from killing a newer request that reused the same rid. It applies in both single- and multi-tokenizer modes. Explicit `/abort_request` calls do not pass `expect_obj`. In multi-tokenizer mode they still dispatch when the rid is absent locally, since the request may belong to another tokenizer worker. ## Accuracy Tests Not applicable. No kernel or model-forward code is changed, and tokens delivered before a disconnect are unaffected. ## Speed Tests and Profiling No throughput impact is expected. The change recovers scheduler capacity occupied by abandoned requests. A 12-hour A/B run on the same machine produced: | | Patched | Unpatched | |---|---:|---:| | Decode batches | 26,119 | 25,258 | | Disconnected rids | 142 | 333 | | Post-disconnect decode lines per rid | 17 | 6,262 | Post-disconnect decoding per rid fell by 99.7%. This run used a simplified version that removed the guard outright, rather than the exact implementation in this PR. It demonstrates the capacity benefit of delivering aborts to the scheduler; request-identity safety is covered by unit tests. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Tests Added 13 test cases to `test/registered/unit/managers/test_tokenizer_manager_rid_cleanup.py`: ```console $ python3 -m pytest test/registered/unit/managers/test_tokenizer_manager_rid_cleanup.py -q 31 passed, 2 warnings in 25.78s ``` Coverage includes: - cleanup of dispatched, undispatched, and partially dispatched batches - delayed abort delivery after client disconnect - protection against rid reuse in single- and multi-tokenizer modes - explicit `/abort_request` behavior across tokenizer workers - request identity for single and batched background aborts Eight of the new cases are regression tests that fail when their corresponding change is reverted. The other five preserve existing compatibility and implementation invariants. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #31857985953](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31857985953)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #31857985880](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31857985880)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [AMD][DCP] Skip unused QuickAllReduce allocation for DCP groups
signal.text: ## Motivation On ROCm, `GroupCoordinator` currently initializes QuickAllReduce whenever custom all-reduce is enabled. That is useful for TP, but current DCP communication paths do not dispatch to QuickAllReduce: - `ag_rs`: all-gather plus reduce-scatter for MLA, or an FP32 all-reduce for MHA. - `a2a` / `fi_a2a`: all-to-all. In a Kimi-K3 TP8/DCP8 profile on MI350X, constructing the DCP QuickAllReduce communicator reserved 4.002 GiB per GPU. Across 1,152 recorded rank-0 DCP collective dispatches, QuickAllReduce was selected zero times. TP QuickAllReduce remains useful and must stay enabled. Related to #29736. ## Modifications - Add an optional `use_quick_allreduce` control to `GroupCoordinator` and `init_model_parallel_group`. - Preserve the existing behavior by default: the new option inherits `use_custom_allreduce` when unspecified. - Disable QuickAllReduce only for the DCP group. - Keep the AITER custom-all-reduce and PyNccl setup unchanged. - Add a unit test that verifies DCP opts out while TP retains the default behavior. ## Accuracy Tests This does not change model math or the collective selected by current DCP paths. The targeted construction test passes: ``` 1 passed, 5 deselected ``` ## Speed Tests and Profiling This PR targets static memory rather than latency. Measured DCP communicator initialization on MI350X: | Component | Reserved per GPU | | --- | ---: | | PyNccl | 1.883 GiB | | AITER custom all-reduce | 3.002 GiB | | QuickAllReduce | 4.002 GiB | QuickAllReduce had zero selections in the recorded DCP dispatches, so this change reclaims the 4.002 GiB DCP allocation without removing TP QuickAllReduce. ## Checklist - [x] Ran pre-commit on the changed files. - [x] Added a focused unit test. - [x] No documentation change is required; the default API behavior is preserved. - [x] No model kernel or output math is changed. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #31354533291](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31354533291)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #31354533157](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31354533157)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: feat(kernels): generalize persistent CuTe JIT cache
signal.text: ## Motivation SGLang already has a persistent CuTe JIT cache for FlashAttention, but it lives under the FlashAttention package and only supports TVM-FFI exports. Kimi-K3 KDA also uses explicit `cute.compile` calls, but its cache is process-local. ## Modifications - Move the existing cache to `sglang.kernels.jit.cute_aot_cache`. - Generalize it over consumer source roots and CuTe ABI while keeping per-key file locking. - Include the explicit `CUTE_DSL_ARCH` target, or the detected local CUDA architecture, in the source fingerprint. GPU probing remains lazy when persistence is disabled. - Publish compiled objects through a temporary path and `os.replace`, so readers never observe a partially written final object and failed exports leave no temporary artifact. - If an object fails to load, discard it while the per-key shared lock still excludes writers, then fall back to compilation. - Keep routine cache activity at debug level so enabling persistence does not add normal INFO-level server noise. - Keep FlashAttention as the TVM-FFI consumer. A small cache adapter preserves `FLASH_ATTENTION_CUTE_DSL_CACHE_*` behavior and gives `SGLANG_CUTE_AOT_CACHE_DIR` precedence when both configurations are present. - Add `SGLANG_CUTE_AOT_CACHE_DIR` as the shared opt-in cache root and document that it must be trusted. - Make Kimi-K3 KDA MTP the second consumer using the native CuTe ABI. - Normalize CUDA device ordinals only for disk keys so same-architecture ranks can share objects; KDA includes compute capability and indexing width in its compile key. The default remains process-local. This does not introduce rank authority, compiler monkeypatching, or kernel math changes. ## Reviewability Git detects the existing cache module as a 51%-similarity rename. The aggregate patch is 394 additions and 86 deletions across six files; 184 added lines are focused tests. The large add/delete presentation from the previous revision was caused by rename detection falling below GitHub's threshold and has been removed. ## Accuracy tests ### Focused unit and static validation - Eleven focused cache cases cover new/legacy FlashAttention environment precedence, quiet routine logging, disabled behavior, lazy architecture detection, factory/source/architecture namespacing, CUDA device ordinal normalization, both native and TVM-FFI export/load paths, atomic publication, failed-export cleanup, and invalid-object eviction. - SGLang's registered-test collector resolves the pytest file to `base-a-test-cpu`. - Black, Ruff, isort (for applicable paths), codespell, Python syntax compilation, `scripts/lint/check_registered_tests.py`, and `git diff --check` pass. ### Real GPU cache validation Validated commit `e48384b39c` on one NVIDIA B300 SXM6 AC (SM103) with Python 3.12.3, PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130, NVIDIA CUTLASS DSL 4.6.2, and TVM-FFI 0.1.11. This was cache/kernel validation only; no model was loaded. - **KDA native ABI:** `TestKimiK3ComputeKernels.test_mtp_replayssm_ring` cold-compiled and exported two objects. A fresh process with `cute.compile` replaced by an exception loaded both objects, passed the same output and recurrent-state checks, and left object hashes unchanged. - **FlashAttention TVM-FFI ABI:** a BF16 `[1, 64, 4, 64]` causal forward cold-compiled and exported one object. A fresh process with `cute.compile` replaced by an exception loaded it and produced the identical output SHA-256 (`780881b74eb262e7831f1f2a710c53a5ec209f52f371ec4fe51c6b43b2ff9678`). Against an FP32 reference, relative L2 was `0.001861` and max absolute error was `0.007716`. - **Corruption recovery:** the FlashAttention object was replaced with invalid bytes. The next process detected and removed it, recompiled with the same output SHA-256, and published a repaired object. A final fresh process with `cute.compile` blocked loaded the repaired object successfully. [Validation run](https://modal.com/apps/modal-flash/main/ap-3PyR14z34YcGgsm8zGdHgO) - No object hashes changed and no `.tmp.o` artifacts remained after validation. ### Recommended targeted CI ```text /rerun-test test/registered/unit/kernels/test_cute_aot_cache.py test/registered/kernels/ops/kimi_k3/test_compute.py test/registered/kernels/ops/attention/test_flash_attention_4.py ``` These tests cover the shared cache, its two consumers, both ABIs, and the relevant B200/large-GPU registrations. Targeted reruns are sufficient in addition to the repository's normal required CI; a manual all-CI rerun is not necessary for this scoped change. ## Speed tests and profiling No end-to-end speed benchmark is included. A warm process can load an existing FlashAttention or KDA object instead of compiling it again. ## Checklist - [x] Format code according to the project configuration. - [x] Add focused unit tests. - [x] Document the new environment variable and trust boundary. - [x] Validate native and TVM-FFI cold-to-warm round trips on a real GPU. - [x] Validate invalid-object eviction, recompilation, and repaired warm loading. - [x] Keep the cache move visible as a rename for review. - [x] Follow the SGLang code style guidance. - [ ] Provide an end-to-end speed benchmark (out of scope for cache validation). <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #31857404368](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31857404368)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #31857404089](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31857404089)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [WIP][DCP] Support PD disaggregation with DCP + DSPARK
signal.text: ## Motivation Reimplementation of #33043 on `main`, as that PR instructed. It targeted the `kimi-k3` branch and was closed with: > **This PR needs to be reimplemented on main after Kimi K3 is merged into main.** … the disaggregation transfer paths it touches differ between the two branches. Original author: @yhyang201. The design below is theirs; this PR ports it to `main`. PD disaggregation hangs when the decode side runs DCP and both sides run DSPARK. Each of the three works on its own; only the combination fails. **Root cause.** DSPARK appends the draft KV buffers to `kv_args.kv_item_lens`, so the draft shares `kv_indices` with the target. Under DCP the target indices are virtualized and `send_kvcache_dcp` relayouts them per token owner (`pos % dcp_size`, compacted to `pos // dcp_size`), but the draft pool is replicated and consumes those locs untranslated. `prepare_dcp_token_item_lens` then fails its per-entry geometry check: ``` RuntimeError: PD DCP source/destination KV geometry differs: src=[1152 x24, 256, 256, ...] ``` That raise happens inside `bootstrap_thread`, which had no exception handling, so the thread died and every later bootstrap/room/abort message went unprocessed. Requests hung silently until the client timed out. ## Modifications Move the draft KV to its own `StateType.DSPARK_DRAFT_KV` state component, following the existing DSV4 NextN precedent. The state channel copies rows verbatim with per-token item lengths, so prefill (physical locs) and decode (virtual locs) stay aligned by position with no relayout, and the target KV channel goes back to being homogeneous. - `kv_layer_ids` is restored for the speculative path. The draft entries used to force it empty, which silently disabled the PP x DCP layer-id pairing. - Draft pools that are not `MHATokenToKVPool` (the DSV4 self-draft path, whose buffers and loc space differ) now fail at startup instead of transferring garbage. Two robustness fixes, because the combination is undiagnosable without them: - `bootstrap_thread` no longer dies on a message-handling error; the mooncake session is marked failed so pending rooms abort through the existing path instead of hanging. - The transfer worker skips rooms whose session never registered, instead of raising `KeyError` and killing the worker thread. Prefill-side guards for `--enable-hierarchical-cache` (load-back restores target KV only, leaving draft rows uninitialized) and `--enable-prefill-context-parallel` (each CP rank only writes its own token shard). ### Deltas from #33043 - **nixl now fails at startup instead of at transfer time.** #33043 listed this as uncovered. nixl's `maybe_send_extra` has no `DSPARK_DRAFT_KV` branch, so it falls through to its unknown-state-type `raise`. That raise is caught by `transfer_worker`'s catch-all and propagated via `failure_exception()`, so the behaviour today is a loud per-request transfer failure, not silent corruption — but it happens only after the model is loaded and traffic is flowing. This rejects the combination during arg handling instead. Purely a pre-flight improvement; remove the guard if a nixl branch is added. - Moved `_dspark_draft_kv_payload` above the `MINIMAX_INDEX_K` comment in both `prefill.py` and `decode.py`; as applied it separated that comment from the `payloads` dict it describes. - Added four unit tests to the existing `_handle_pd_disaggregation` guard suite. ## Accuracy Tests TODO ## Speed Tests and Profiling TODO ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). Tests added to `test/registered/unit/server_args/test_server_args.py` (CPU-only, registered): the two prefill DSPARK guards, the nixl rejection across both PD modes, and a negative asserting mooncake is still accepted. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #31852477680](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31852477680)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #31852477477](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31852477477)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [Diffusion] Add MiniMax H3 cube sparse attention
signal.text: ## Summary - add a FlexAttention-based cube sparse attention backend for MiniMax H3's 3D visual streams - wire H3 packed-sequence metadata and denoise-step sparsity schedules into the native pipeline - keep text, audio, standalone reference images, and the text-only token refiner on dense attention - document the component-scoped command and add numerical, CUDA, admission, and parallelism coverage ## Behavior Select the backend only for the H3 transformer: ```bash --component-attention-backends transformer=cube_sparse_attn \ --attention-backend-config '{"local_cube_size":[4,4,4],"topk_ratio_list":[1.0,1.0,0.8,0.7,0.6,0.5,0.5]}' ``` A ratio of `1.0` uses H3's native FlashAttention path. Ratios below `1.0` use approximate cube sparsity. Ring parallelism is rejected because its attention exchange does not compose with this backend; Ulysses remains supported. ## Performance On 2×H100 with the 1344×768, 4-second, 8-step TP2 workload: - dense FlashAttention denoise: 16.51s - aggressive all-`0.05` sparse schedule: 13.32s (19.3% faster) - mixed `[1.0, 1.0, 0.8, 0.7, 0.6, 0.5, 0.5]` schedule: 19.67s The mixed schedule is slower on this short sequence because FlexAttention routing overhead outweighs the sparse-kernel savings, so the feature remains opt-in and the cookbook calls out the tradeoff. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #31856755676](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31856755676)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #31856755577](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31856755577)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: Fix inconsistent input_ids and seq_lens
signal.text: In `prepare_attn_tp_scatter_input`, `input_ids` needs to be padded to a multiple of `attention_tp_size`, but `seq_lens` is not modified accordingly. For example, for a single sequence of length 21, len(input_ids) = 21 and seq_lens = [21]. After padding, len(input_ids) = 24 while seq_lens remains [21]. ```python import torch from flashinfer.prefill import BatchPrefillWithRaggedKVCacheWrapper ws = torch.empty(128 * 1024**2, dtype=torch.uint8, device="cuda") wrapper_raged = BatchPrefillWithRaggedKVCacheWrapper(ws, "NHD", backend="fa3") seq_len = 21 seq_len_with_pad = 24 q = torch.randn(seq_len_with_pad, 16, 128, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16) k = torch.randn(seq_len_with_pad, 1, 128, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16) v = torch.randn(seq_len_with_pad, 1, 128, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16) q[seq_len:] = torch.nan k[seq_len:] = torch.nan v[seq_len:] = torch.nan wrapper_raged.plan( qo_indptr=torch.tensor([0, seq_len], dtype=torch.int64, device="cuda"), kv_indptr=torch.tensor([0, seq_len], dtype=torch.int64, device="cuda"), num_qo_heads=16, num_kv_heads=1, head_dim_qk=128, q_data_type=torch.bfloat16, ) o = wrapper_raged.run(q, k, v) print(o.view(o.shape[0], -1).sum(dim=-1)) ``` NaNs in the regions outside indptr will cause a large number of NaNs in the output: ``` tensor([nan, nan, nan, nan, nan, nan, nan, nan, nan, nan, nan, nan, nan, nan, nan, nan, nan, nan, nan, nan, nan, 0., 0., 0.], device='cuda:0', dtype=torch.bfloat16) ``` So how are the NaNs in the padded part introduced? Because the padded part is outside `indptr`, the values in the padded region of flashinfer’s output are undefined. We found that for some inputs, `BatchPrefillWithPagedKVCacheWrapper.run` may return NaNs in the padded region. In this patch, we modify `seq_lens` to make it consistent with `len(input_ids)`, ensuring that the lengths of `qo_indptr` and `q` match, thereby avoiding NaNs during the attention computation. @ch-wan ## Motivation <!-- Describe the purpose and goals of this pull request. --> ## Modifications <!-- Detail the changes made in this pull request. --> ## Accuracy Tests <!-- If this pull request affects model outputs (e.g., changes to the kernel or model forward code), provide accuracy test results. --> ## Benchmarking and Profiling <!-- If this pull request impacts inference speed, provide benchmarking and profiling results. --> ## Checklist - [ ] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [ ] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). - [ ] Work with maintainers to merge your PR. signal.title: [fix] fix incorrect output in pp mode when server_args.pp_async_batch_depth > 1
signal.text: Addresses #15527 Summary: To prevent premature freeing of PP proxy tensors, this change records them on the forward stream right after they're received; this keeps CUDA allocations alive while kernels are in flight when ```pp_async_batch_depth``` > 1. The main change is that I moved ```_pp_commit_send_output_work_and_preprocess_output_tensors``` to after ```_pp_launch_batch``` in all PP event loops and call it unconditionally, so we keep a single ordering for all depths. ## Checklist - [ ] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [ ] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). - [ ] Work with maintainers to merge your PR. signal.title: Make torchvision an optional dependency
signal.text: ## Motivation torchvision is a heavy dependency that can cause compatibility issues on some platforms (e.g., aarch64) and isn't needed by users who only use text-based LLMs. Making it optional reduces install friction and avoids version conflicts for the majority of sglang users. Related discussion: Previously discussed with maintainers who indicated this change would be reasonable. ## Modifications - Removed `torchvision` from main `dependencies` in `pyproject.toml` - Added `vl = ["torchvision"]` as an optional dependency for vision-language model users Users who need VL models (InternVL, Qwen-VL video, DeepSeek-VL2) can install with: pip install sglang[vl] ## Accuracy Tests N/A - No changes to model outputs.
